events.working_title: Kalayavana Is Burned by Muchukunda's Glance
events.one_line_summary: Krishna lures Kalayavana into Muchukunda's cave; the Yavana kicks the sleeping king and is reduced to ashes.

sources.source_excerpt: Pursued by the Yavana, Krishna entered the mountain cave; the fool kicked the sleeping man thinking him Krishna, and Muchukunda, opening his eyes, burned Kalayavana to ashes with the fire of his glance. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-11)

when pursued by his Mlechcha enemy he humbly entered into Muchukunda's cave. ... With the touch of the foot the royal saint Muchukunda awoke ... he looked at the Yavana king with angry eyes. As soon as he was eyed, the king of Yavanas was all ablaze.

The rash Yavana entering the cave, and beholding a man lying asleep there, concluded it must be Krishńa, and kicked him; at which Muchukunda awoke, and casting on him an angry glance, the Yavana was instantly consumed, and reduced to ashes.

events.notes: Same event in HV 1.114 and BP 10.51: Krishna lures Kalayavana into the cave; the sleeping Muchukunda burns him with his gaze.

events.working_title: Sesha Departs from Balarama
events.one_line_summary: As Krishna watches, the great serpent Sesha issues from Balarama's mouth and enters the ocean, hymned by saints and serpents, and Ocean comes forth to receive him.

sources.source_excerpt: Going towards Ráma, who was sitting at the root of a tree, they beheld a large serpent coming out of his mouth. Having issued from his mouth, the mighty snake proceeded towards the ocean... and entered into the waters of the deep.

Proceeding then to the forest, Keshava beheld Rama sitting in a solitary spot thereof. He also saw that Rama had set himself to Yoga and that from out his mouth was issuing a mighty snake. The colour of that snake was white... that high-souled naga of a 1,000 heads... proceeded along that way which led to the ocean.

events.notes: Same departure scene (VP 5.37, MB 16.4): the serpent Sesha issues from Balarama and enters the ocean.

events.working_title: Balarama Drags the Yamuna
events.one_line_summary: Intoxicated by Varuni, Balarama summons the Yamuna to sport; when she refuses, he drags her with his plough until she begs forgiveness.

sources.source_excerpt: Drinking the Varuni that flowed from a tree, Balarama, intoxicated, summoned the Yamuna to sport with him; when she did not come, he dragged her with the tip of his plough, and the frightened river, bowing, begged his pardon, after which he released her and bathed. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 18-33)

Thereupon Rāma said to Yamunā:—'O great river, going to the ocean, I wish to marry you by bathing in your water; come to me therefore in your bodily form.' ... Dragged with force by Rāma the powerful river Yamunā ... began to follow the way pointed out by the plough-share.

Ráma in a rage took up his ploughshare, which he plunged into her bank, and dragged her to him, calling out, "Will you not come, you jade? will you not come?"... he compelled the dark river to quit its ordinary course.

events.notes: Same feat (HV 1.102, BP 10.65): inebriated Balarama drags the Yamuna with his plough until the river begs pardon. | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: Balarama Revisits Vraja
events.one_line_summary: Balarama returns to Nanda's Gokula, consoles the pining gopis with Krishna's message, and stays two months in their company.

sources.source_excerpt: Balarama went to Nanda's Gokula, was embraced by the gopas and gopis, and consoled the gopis, who asked after Krishna, with Krishna's heart-felt messages; he stayed two months, sporting with them in the Yamuna groves. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-17)

After some days had thus elapsed, Rāma, recollecting his friendship with Gopas, alone went to Vraja with Krishna's consent. ... 'We had been reared by you and spent our boyhood in sporting here. We took our meals in your houses and tended the kine.'

Baladeva... being desirous of seeing his kinsmen, went to Nanda's cow-pens, and there again conversed with the herdsmen and their females... Ráma consoled them by communicating to them agreeable, modest, affectionate, and gentle messages from Krishńa.

events.notes: Same visit (HV 1.102, BP 10.65): Balarama returns to Nanda's village and the gopis. | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: Krishna Sends Uddhava to Badarikashrama
events.one_line_summary: Krishna commands Uddhava to leave for his hermitage at Badarikashrama and abide in the teaching he has received; the grief-stricken Uddhava circumambulates him, places his feet upon his own head, and departs bearing Krishna's sandals.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna said: 'Go, Uddhava, as I have commanded, to my hermitage called Badari; there, dwelling on what I have taught, you will come to me beyond the three paths.' Uddhava, unable to leave him, walked around him again and again, placed Krishna's feet on his head, and, bearing his sandals, at last went forth. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 40-45)

Uddhava said: 'So, having worshipped his feet and received the path of self-knowledge, I bowed to the Lord and came away, heart-torn with separation; I will go to the hermitage of Badari, where Narayana and Nara performed their long austerities.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 19-21)
Do you go by a celestial route... to the holy place Badarikáśrama... and on that spot, sanctified by them, thou, by meditating on me, shalt obtain perfection through my favour.

Hearing that they had taken up their abode on the sea-coast, Uddhava, the wisest of men, who was, besides, well-versed in Yoga, proceeded there and took his leave (for departing). Krishna, with joined hands, saluted Uddhava, and seeing him bent on departing (from the world) and knowing that the destructions of the Vrishnis was at hand, did not feel any disposition to prevent him.

events.working_title: The Yadava Fratricide at Prabhasa
events.one_line_summary: Drunk on maireya wine at Prabhasa, the Yadavas, deluded by Krishna's maya and the brahmins' curse, fall upon one another, and when their weapons fail they seize the eraka reeds — which have become iron clubs — and annihilate one another; Balarama then yields up his body in yoga.

sources.source_excerpt: Drinking the maireya wine, their minds overthrown, the proud heroes fell upon one another — Pradyumna against Samba, Akrura against Bhoja, Aniruddha against Satyaki; fathers against sons, kinsmen against kinsmen. When their arrows were spent, they seized the eraka reeds, which had become like iron clubs, and with them slew one another. Then Balarama, entering yoga at the ocean's shore, gave up his mortal frame. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-20, 25)
Uddhava said: 'Their minds deranged by the fault of the maireya wine, at sunset there was among them a crushing of one another, like reeds.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1)

As they drank, the destructive flame of dissension was kindled amongst them... The rushes in their hands became like thunderbolts, and they struck one another with them fatal blows... In a short time there was not a single Yádava left alive, except the mighty Krishńa and Dáruka.

Then Yuyudhana, inebriated with wine, derisively laughing at and insulting Kritavarma in the midst of that assembly, said, 'What Kshatriya is there who... will slay men locked in the embraces of sleep and, therefore, already dead?' ... Having said these words, Satyaki rushed at Kritavarma and severed his head with a sword in the very sight of Keshava.

The delighter of the Yadus, beholding his own son, and the son of Sini too, slain, took up, in wrath, a handful of the Eraka grass that grew there. That handful of grass became a terrible bolt of iron endued with the energy of the thunderbolt. With it Krishna slew all those that came before him... Son killed sire, and sire killed son, O Bharata.

events.notes: Same catastrophe (VP 5.37, BP 11.30, MB 16.3): the kinsmen destroy one another with reed-weapons.

events.working_title: The Sages Curse Samba and the Yadavas
events.one_line_summary: Yadu boys dress Samba as a pregnant woman and ask the visiting sages what 'she' will bear; the angered sages curse that he will bring forth an iron mace to destroy the clan, and the mace appears, is ground and cast into the sea, and its remaining iron, swallowed by a fish, later becomes the hunter's arrow.

sources.source_excerpt: Disguising Samba as a woman, the boys asked the sages: 'This dark-eyed one is pregnant; what will she give birth to?' The angry sages answered: 'She will bear an iron mace, the destroyer of your clan.' Samba brought forth the mace; the Yadava king had it ground and cast into the sea, and a fish swallowed the last bit of iron, which in the hunter's hands became the arrow. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 13-15, 20-22)
Uddhava said: 'Once, in the city, the sages, angered by the Yadu and Bhoja boys at their play, pronounced a curse — knowing the mind of the Lord.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 23)
they dressed and adorned Sumba, the son of Jámbavatí, as a damsel... The sages... said, "She will bring forth a club, that shall crush the whole of the Yádava race."

'This heir of Vasudeva, by name Samva, will bring forth a fierce iron bolt for the destruction of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas... The blessed hero armed with the plough will enter the ocean, casting off his body, while a hunter of the name of Jara will pierce the high-souled Krishna while lying on the ground.' ... The slayer of Madhu, informed of what had taken place, summoned all the Vrishnis and told them of it... he simply said that that which was destined would surely happen.

events.notes: Same curse episode (BP 11.1, MB 16.1): youths disguise Samba as a pregnant woman; the sages curse him to bear the iron bolt.

events.working_title: Shishupala's Outburst Against Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Enraged at Krishna's honor, Shishupala rises and heaps insults on Krishna, calling him a cowherd unworthy of worship; the assembly rebukes him and some draw weapons.

sources.source_excerpt: Shishupala, son of Damaghosha, rises from his seat in fury and abuses Krishna, saying a cowherd who abandoned his caste cannot be honored while the great sages are present. The assembled sages stop their ears and curse him, and the enraged Pandavas and their allies rise with weapons to slay him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 29-41)

This wretch born in the race of the Vrishnis unrighteously slew of old the illustrious king Jarasandha. ... Having spoken these words, Sisupala rose from his excellent seat, and accompanied by the kings, went out of that assembly.

If Krishna in his infancy slew a vulture, what is there remarkable in that ... O Bhishma, what is there remarkable in this one's having supported for a week the Govardhan mount which is like an anthill? ... Bhimasena endued with energy became angry. ... the mighty-armed Bhishma caught him like Mahadeva seizing Mahasena.

events.notes: Same assembly scene (BP 10.74, MB 2.41): Shishupala derides Krishna's deeds and honour.

events.working_title: Krishna Slays Shishupala
events.one_line_summary: Krishna, restraining his own men, cuts off Shishupala's head with the sharp-edged discus, and Shishupala's effulgence merges into Krishna.

sources.source_excerpt: Restraining his followers, Krishna rises and with his razor-edged discus severs the head of the rushing Shishupala. A great uproar follows, and before the eyes of all beings a brilliant light issuing from Shishupala's body enters Krishna, as he who had meditated on Krishna in enmity through three births attained oneness with him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 42-45)

the queen with great pleasure herself placed the child on the lap of Damodara. As soon as the child was placed on his lap, those superfluous arms of his fell down and the eye on his forehead also disappeared.

events.notes: Same slaying (BP 10.74, MB 2.42): the discus ends Shishupala after the hundredth offence.

events.working_title: Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna Approach Jarasandha in Disguise
events.one_line_summary: Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna travel to Girivraja disguised as brahmanas and ask Jarasandha for alms, testing his charity.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna, wearing the marks of brahmanas, go to Girivraja where Jarasandha dwells. They arrive at the hour of hospitality and ask the generous king, famed for giving even his own head to suppliants, to grant them what they desire. Jarasandha, recognizing them by their voices and marks, resolves to give whatever they ask. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 14-26)

the trio Krishna, Arjuna and Bhima, all possessed of great energy, set out for Magadha attired in the garb of Snataka Brahmanas of resplendent bodies, and blessed by the agreeable speeches of friends and relatives.

events.notes: Same journey (MB 2.20-21, BP 10.72): the three come to Girivraja as brahmanas asking alms.

events.working_title: Krishna Reveals Their Identities and Challenges Jarasandha
events.one_line_summary: Krishna reveals their true identities and asks for single combat; Jarasandha laughs, taunts Krishna as a coward who fled Mathura, and chooses Bhima as his opponent.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna tells Jarasandha they have come seeking battle, and reveals that the man is Bhima, the other Arjuna, and himself Krishna, his enemy. Jarasandha laughs aloud and taunts that he will not fight Krishna, a coward who abandoned Mathura and fled to the sea, but that Bhima is his match in strength. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 27-32)

Desirous of liberating the captive monarchs from thee, know that we are certainly not Brahmanas. I am Hrishesha otherwise called Sauri, and these two heroes among men are the sons of Pandu. O king of Magadha, we challenge thee. Fight standing before us. Either set free all the monarchs, or go thou to the abode of Yama.

events.notes: Same confrontation (MB 2.22, BP 10.72): Krishna casts off the disguise; Jarasandha taunts; single combat is set.

events.working_title: Krishna Sports with His Sixteen Thousand Wives
events.one_line_summary: Krishna sports in the lakes with his sixteen thousand wives, splashing and being splashed, while the women's songs of longing express their single-hearted devotion.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, delighting in Dwaraka, sports with his sixteen thousand wives, bathing and playing in the lakes, splashing them as they splash him, like the lord of the yakshas among his yakshinis. The queens, wholly devoted to Krishna, pour out songs of longing to the birds, the moon, the wind and the clouds, and by such constant love attain the supreme state. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-24)
amongst the women of Keshava every one thought:—"I am the most favourite of Keshava: he is sporting only with me"... at the command of Vāsudeva the water of the ocean was freed from salt

events.notes: Same scene (HV 1.235, BP 10.90): Krishna's water-sports; each queen believes she alone is favoured.

events.working_title: Krishna Names the Pandavas to Balarama
events.one_line_summary: At Draupadi's svayamvara, Krishna, seated among the Yadava chiefs, recognizes the five Pandavas disguised as Brahmins and tells Balarama who each of them is.

sources.source_excerpt: And Halayudha (Valadeva) and Janardana (Krishna) and the chief of the Vrishni, Andhaka, and Yadava tribes who obeyed the leadership of Krishna were also there, viewing the scene. And beholding those elephants in rut--the five (Pandavas)--attracted towards Draupadi like mighty elephants towards a lake overgrown with lotuses, or like fire covered with ashes, Krishna the foremost of Yadu heroes began to reflect. And he said unto Rama (Valadeva), 'That is Yudhishthira; that is Bhima with Jishnu (Arjuna); and those are the twin heroes.'

And beholding those feats of both Jishnu and his brother, Damodara (Krishna) of superhuman intelligence and inconceivable feats, addressing his brother, Halayudha (Valadeva) of fierce energy, said, 'That hero there, of tread like that of a mighty lion, who draweth the large bow in his hand four full cubits in length, is Arjuna! ... And that other hero who having speedily torn up the tree hath suddenly become ready to drive off the monarchs is Vrikodara! ... I heard that the sons of Pandu along with their mother Pritha had all escaped from the conflagration of the house of lac.' Then Halayudha ... said with great satisfaction, 'O, I am happy to hear ... that our father's sister Pritha with the foremost of the Kaurava princes have all escaped (from death)!'

events.notes: Same identification scene (MB 1.189, 1.191): at the svayamvara Krishna tells Balarama who each disguised brother is.

events.working_title: The Yadavas Resolve to Abandon Mathura for Dwaraka
events.one_line_summary: Fearing Kalayavana's assault, the Vrishnis and Andhakas make Krishna their president and resolve to leave Mathura for Kushasthali (Dwarka).

sources.source_excerpt: Thereupon starting for Mathura with one Akshouhini of soldiers Kalayavana sent his messenger to the house of Vrishnis and Andhakas... being united the Vrishnis and Andhakas, making the highly intelligent Krishna their president, held a conference in fear of Kalayavana... resolved upon flying away from the charming city of Mathura and thought of settling down in Kushasthali Dwarka.

the lotus-eyed Krishna addressed the following reasonable words to the Yadus in their assembly:—'This Mathurā city is the abode of the Yadus ... the city of Mathurā is very limited and the enemies can easily enter it. ... it is better that we should live elsewhere.'

events.notes: Same decision (HV ~1.113; one member carries a mis-cited locator "1.35" — content is the Kalayavana-era flight; confidence lowered for that locator). | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: Viswakarma Builds Dwaraka for Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Facing Kalayavana and Jarasandha together, Krishna builds the fortress-city of Dvaraka in the sea and relocates the Yadavas.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna built a fortress twelve yojanas wide within the sea, wondrous in every way, and by his mystic power conveyed all the people there; Indra sent the Sudharma hall and the Parijata tree, Varuna swift white horses. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 42-56)

Krishna ... thought of Viswakarmā, in his mind, so that he might come there. ... 'O ocean, if you have any respect for me, then withdraw thy form in the water extending over twelve yojanas.' ... by Viswakarma's mental effort that beautiful Vaishnava city, by name Dwarkāvati, was built.
Krishńa solicited a space of twelve furlongs from the ocean, and there he built the city of Dwáraka, defended by high ramparts... Thither Janárddana conducted the inhabitants of Mathurá.

events.notes: Same founding (BP 10.50, HV 1.115): Krishna selects the sea-site; the divine architect raises the city.

events.working_title: Krishna, Balarama and Pradyumna Fly to Sonitpura on Garuda
events.one_line_summary: To rescue Aniruddha from Bana, Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna fly out on Garuda, Krishna assuming eight arms and innumerable heads with his weapons.

sources.source_excerpt: Desirous of killing Vāna the lotus-eyed Keshava assumed a form having eight arms... Janārddana... assumed innumerable heads. In his four right hands he had sword, discus, club and arrows
Govinda thought of Garuda in his mind: and he too, with folded hands, arrived before Krishna... Krishna... sat on his back. Thereupon... Halāyudha and Pradyumna... sat behind him

events.notes: Round-2 audit merge: HV 1.264 (eight-armed divine form) and 1.268 (Garuda flight after Narada's report) are the same departure beat for the Bana-war rescue of Aniruddha. | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: The Doom Prophecy Warns Kamsa of Devaki's Eighth Child
events.one_line_summary: At Vasudeva's wedding procession, Kamsa drives the chariot and hears a bodiless voice declare that Devaki's eighth child will slay him.

sources.source_excerpt: As Kamsa drives the chariot bearing the newly-wed Vasudeva and Devaki, a bodiless voice warns him: the eighth child of the woman he escorts will be his death. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 28-33)
The child, of the eighth conception of your youngest sister Devaki who lives in Mathura, will be your death.

As they were going along, a voice in the sky, sounding aloud and deep as thunder, addressed Kansa, and said, "Fool that you are, the eighth child of the damsel whom you are driving in the car shall take away your life!" On hearing this, Kansa drew his sword, and was about to put Devakí to death; but Vasudeva interposed.

events.variant_notes: BP/VP: a bodiless heavenly voice warns at the wedding; HV: Narada delivers the warning. VP 5.1 also folds in the pacification beat.

events.working_title: Vasudeva Pacifies Kamsa and Promises to Surrender His Sons
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa seizes Devaki to kill her, but Vasudeva placates him with reasoning and vows to surrender every newborn son to him.

sources.source_excerpt: Kamsa draws his sword on his own sister, but Vasudeva soothes him with words on death and destiny, promising to hand over each son born to Devaki; at this Kamsa relents. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 34-54)

events.variant_notes: See also 'prophecy' (VP 5.1 combines warning + pacification).

events.working_title: Kamsa Imprisons Devaki and Destroys Her Children
events.one_line_summary: After Narada reveals that the gods are incarnating among the Yadavas, Kamsa imprisons Devaki and Vasudeva and kills each child as it is born.

sources.source_excerpt: Told by Narada that the gods have taken birth among the Yadavas, Kamsa has Devaki and Vasudeva chained in prison and kills every son she bears, one by one. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 55-68)
'Do ye always be on your guard for destroying the (eight born) children of Devaki... destroy all the embryos of Devaki.'

The Muni Nárada informed Kansa that the supporter of the earth, Vishńu, would be the eighth child of Devakí; and his wrath being excited by this report, he placed both Vasudeva and Devakí in confinement.

events.working_title: Vishnu Resolves to Incarnate to Relieve the Earth
events.one_line_summary: Narada tells Vishnu that the gods' incarnations alone cannot destroy the demons reborn as kings, and urges him to descend himself.

sources.source_excerpt: 'O Narayana, useless have been the incarnations of the gods for the destruction of the kings... Methinks their work cannot be accomplished without Narayana's Yoga.'
Going to the region of men and assuming a human form I shall bring about the destruction of all those mighty demons headed by Kansa... Being born as a milkman with them he will live there happily.

the supreme lord plucked off two hairs, one white and one black, and said to the gods, "These my hairs shall descend upon earth, and shall relieve her of the burden of her distress... This my (black) hair shall be impersonated in the eighth conception of the wife of Vasudeva, Devakí... and shall slay Kansa, who is the demon Kálanemi."

events.variant_notes: VP: Earth petitions at Meru and Vishnu plucks black/white hairs; HV: Narada urges Vishnu, Brahma foretells the birth.

events.working_title: Vishnu Commands Yogamaya to Transfer Balarama and Arrange the Exchange
events.one_line_summary: Vishnu directs Yogamaya to draw the unborn Balarama from Devaki's womb into Rohini's, and to be born herself as Nanda's daughter.

sources.source_excerpt: Vishnu instructs Yogamaya to transfer the unborn Balarama from Devaki's womb into that of Rohini in Gokula, and to take birth herself as the daughter of Nanda and Yasoda. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 4-15)

'take that eldest brother of mine in the seventh month and place him within Rohini's womb... I will be taken to Yashoda and you will be taken to Devaki. By this our interchange Kansa will be stupified.'

To her Vishńu said, "Go, Nidrá, to the nether regions, and by my command conduct successively six of their princes to be conceived of Devakí... I will myself become incarnate in the eighth conception of Devakí; and you shall immediately take a similar character as the embryo offspring of Yaśodá."

events.working_title: The Conception of Devaki and the Six Demon Embryos
events.one_line_summary: Vishnu enters Vasudeva's mind; Devaki conceives the Lord and glows with brilliance, and Kamsa, though uneasy, refrains from harming her.

sources.source_excerpt: The Lord enters Vasudeva's heart; Devaki, bearing the whole world's support in her womb, shines so brightly that Kamsa sees in her the presence of his own destroyer, yet he stays his hand. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 15-23)
'O ye great Asuras Saragarbhas, you all six will be born in order from Devaki and Kansa will kill you.'

conveyed the six several embryos into the womb of Devakí, and transferred the seventh after a season to that of Rohińí; after which, Hari, for the benefit of the three regions, became incarnate as the conception of the former princess, and Yoganidrá as that of Yaśodá.

events.variant_notes: HV gives the backstory (six Saragarbha demons cursed by Hiranyakashipu); BP omits the six-embryo detail.

events.working_title: Devaki's Seventh Embryo Is Transferred to Rohini (Balarama Born)
events.one_line_summary: The seventh embryo is transferred from Devaki to Rohini by the goddess of sleep, and the child is born as Sankarshana (Balarama).

sources.source_excerpt: 'O fair one, I have extracted the embryo out of Devaki's womb and placed it in yours. Therefore this your son will be celebrated by the name of Sangkarshana.'

events.variant_notes: Execution of the command in 'command_yogamaya'; see also 'conception' (VP 5.2 covers this transfer).

events.working_title: The Gods Praise the Unborn Lord in Devaki's Womb
events.one_line_summary: Brahma, Shiva and the host of gods descend to praise the unborn Lord in Devaki's womb and then depart.

sources.source_excerpt: Brahma and Shiva, with sages and gods, come to Devaki's prison and praise the unborn Lord who will lift the earth's burden; having sung his glories they return to heaven. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 24-42)

events.working_title: Krishna Is Born at Midnight in the Prison
events.one_line_summary: At a supremely auspicious hour, with nature rejoicing, Krishna is born of Devaki in the prison at midnight.

sources.source_excerpt: At midnight, as the directions turn calm and all beings rejoice, the Lord appears from Devaki as the full moon rises in the east. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-7)

In the auspicious midnight and in Abhijit Muhurtta, Devaki gave birth to Vishnu and Yashoda to that daughter... the oceans were agitated, the pillars of the earth were shaken... Indra too, along with the gods, eulogised the glories of Madhusudhana.

As soon as Ánakadundubhi beheld the child, of the complexion of the lotus leaves, having four arms, and the mystic mark Śrívatsa on his breast, he addressed him in terms of love and reverence, and represented the fears he entertained of Kansa.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.3 also includes the four-armed form and withholding of it (see 'reveal_form').

events.working_title: Krishna Reveals His Divine Form and Recalls Past Births
events.one_line_summary: The infant reveals a four-armed form bearing conch and discus; Vasudeva and Devaki praise him, and he recalls his earlier births to them before resuming an ordinary infant form.

sources.source_excerpt: The newborn shows himself four-armed, holding conch, discus, mace and lotus, adored by his parents; he reminds them of their past births and their long austerities, then becomes an ordinary infant again. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 8-45)

events.variant_notes: See also 'birth' (VP 5.3 folds this in).

events.working_title: Vasudeva Carries Krishna Out of Prison Across the Yamuna
events.one_line_summary: Prompted by the Lord, Vasudeva carries the baby out; the prison doors open by themselves, Shesha shelters them from rain, and the Yamuna parts to give passage.

sources.source_excerpt: The guards are struck with sleep and the prison doors open by themselves; as Vasudeva bears the child through the night, the serpent Shesha spreads his hoods against the rain and the Yamuna parts its waters to let them cross. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 46-49)

To protect the infant from the heavy rain that fell from the clouds of night, Śesha, the many-headed serpent, followed Vasudeva, and spread his hoods above their heads; and when the prince... crossed the Yamuná river... the waters were stilled, and rose not above his knee.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.3 also includes the exchange at Gokula (see 'exchange').

events.working_title: Vasudeva Exchanges Krishna for Yashoda's Daughter
events.one_line_summary: Vasudeva places Krishna in Yasoda's bed in Nanda's Gokula and carries Yasoda's newborn daughter back to Mathura.

sources.source_excerpt: Vasudeva sets his son in Yasoda's bed in Gokula, takes up the girl-child born there, and returns to the prison, where he lays her beside Devaki and resumes his chains. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 50-52)

Taking that boy, Vasudeva too, fond of his sons, speedily repaired to the house of Yashoda. Placing his son in her house against her knowledge he brought her daughter and placed her on Devaki's bedstead.

events.working_title: Kamsa Comes to Slay the Newborn Girl
events.one_line_summary: Awakened by the guards, Kamsa rushes to the prison and snatches the newborn girl from Devaki, who pleads for her life.

sources.source_excerpt: Hearing of the birth, Kamsa hastens to the lying-in room; the grieving Devaki begs him to spare the infant girl, but he tears the child from her hands. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-6)

events.variant_notes: See also 'yogamaya_warn' (the dashing that follows).

events.working_title: Kamsa Dashes the Infant and Yogamaya Warns Him
events.one_line_summary: When Kamsa dashes the girl against a stone she rises as the eight-armed goddess Yogamaya, warns him that his slayer is already born, and Kamsa, shaken, repents and frees Devaki and Vasudeva.

sources.source_excerpt: The flung infant springs into the sky as the eight-armed goddess Yogamaya and declares, 'Your slayer is already born elsewhere'; humbled, Kamsa releases Devaki and Vasudeva and begs their forgiveness. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 7-27)

Taking her with contempt by the legs and whirling her Kansa dashed her against a stone... 'O Kansa, for thy own destruction thou hast whirled and dashed me against a rock... I will tear off thy body with my hands and drink thy hot blood.'

he threw it ruthlessly against a stone; but it rose into the sky, and expanded into a gigantic figure, having eight arms, each wielding some formidable weapon... "he is born who shall kill thee, the mighty one amongst the gods, who was formerly thy destroyer."

events.working_title: Kamsa Repents and Devaki Forgives Him
events.one_line_summary: Kansa, ashamed, confesses to Devaki and throws himself at her feet; Devaki forgives him, saying Time alone is the instrument.

sources.source_excerpt: 'I throw myself at your feet like a son. Be not offended with me.'... Devaki said:—'I forgive you for the sin that you have committed by destroying my children.'

events.variant_notes: HV-specific; BP 10.4.2 folds repentance into the Yogamaya episode.

events.working_title: Kamsa's Ministers Counsel Slaughtering the Righteous
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa's demon ministers urge him to kill all newborn children and to destroy the brahmanas, cows and all in whom Vishnu dwells.

sources.source_excerpt: The demon ministers persuade Kamsa to slay every infant in city and village, and to root out the brahmanas, cows and austerity in which, they say, the gods have their life. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 28-41)

events.working_title: Kamsa Orders the Slaughter of Children and the Pious
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa dispatches shape-shifting demons across the land to massacre the sages' and infants' protectors, and returns to his palace.

sources.source_excerpt: Kamsa sends forth demons who can assume any form, bidding them slaughter the holy everywhere, and himself withdraws into his palace. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 42-46)
Let therefore active search be made for whatever young children there may be upon earth, and let every boy in whom there are signs of unusual vigour be slain without remorse.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.4 also includes the release of Vasudeva and Devaki.

events.working_title: Nanda Celebrates the Birth of His Son
events.one_line_summary: Nanda performs the birth rites with lavish gifts of cows and gold, and the whole of Gokula rejoices over the newborn child.

sources.source_excerpt: Nanda performs the birth ceremonies with thousands of adorned cows and heaps of gifts; the cowherd men and women, scented and adorned, pour into his home to bless the child. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-17)

events.working_title: Nanda Visits Mathura and Meets Vasudeva
events.one_line_summary: Nanda goes to Mathura to pay his annual tribute, and Vasudeva joyfully embraces him as a brother.

sources.source_excerpt: Nanda travels to Mathura to pay the yearly tax; Vasudeva, learning of his arrival, rises and embraces him as if life had returned to his body. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 18-20)

events.working_title: Vasudeva Warns Nanda of Danger in Gokula
events.one_line_summary: Vasudeva affectionately inquires after his sons and urges Nanda to return quickly to Gokula, for evil omens are gathering there.

sources.source_excerpt: Vasudeva, anxious for the two boys hidden in Nanda's care, tells him not to linger, for great disturbances are rising in Gokula; Nanda and his men hasten back with their carts. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 21-32)

events.working_title: Putana Enters Gokula Disguised as a Woman
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa's agent Putana, a demoness who kills infants, disguises herself as a beautiful woman and enters Nanda's village.

sources.source_excerpt: Putana, sent by Kamsa and wandering among villages killing infants, flies into Gokula and by her magic takes the form of a lovely woman. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-5)

events.variant_notes: See also 'putana_kill'.

events.working_title: Krishna Drains the Demoness Putana's Life
events.one_line_summary: Putana offers the baby her poisoned breast, but Krishna sucks out her very life-breath, and she falls dead, revealing her true demon form.

sources.source_excerpt: Taking the baby to her breast, the demoness is seized in her vital parts; Krishna drinks out her life along with her milk, and with a terrible cry she dies and crashes down in her monstrous true form. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 6-12)

Uddhava said: 'Alas! The wicked Putana, who with murderous intent gave him her breast of deadly poison, attained the goal of a nurse. To what other compassionate one could we turn for refuge?' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 22)
Thereupon drinking up all her vital breaths together with her milk Krishna set up a terrible sound. She too, having her breast sundered, fell down earth.

the female fiend Pútaná, the child-killer, came thither by night, and finding the little Krishńa asleep, took him up, and gave him her breast to suck... but Krishńa... sucked it with such violence, that he drained it of the life.

events.variant_notes: bpc1_032 is Uddhava's recollection of the same episode.

events.working_title: The Villagers Burn Putana's Body
events.one_line_summary: The gopis perform protective rites over the child, and the cowherds cut up and burn Putana's vast corpse, from which rises a fragrant smoke, for she attained a mother's reward.

sources.source_excerpt: The cowherd women bathe the child and chant protective hymns over him; the men hew Putana's enormous body to pieces and burn it, and a fragrance like aloe rises from the fire, for she was granted the goal of a mother. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 13-33)

events.working_title: The Infant Krishna Overturns the Cart with His Foot
events.one_line_summary: During the birth ceremonies, the unattended infant kicks the great cart, shattering it and scattering its vessels, to the astonishment of all.

sources.source_excerpt: Left beneath a cart while Yasoda attends the rites, the crying infant kicks it with his tender foot; the cart overturns, its wheels and axle broken and its vessels scattered, leaving everyone amazed. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 3-16)
Then raising up his legs he overturned the carriage with one of them. And then crawling on his legs he began to cry for milk.
whilst Madhusúdana was asleep underneath the waggon, he cried for the breast, and kicking up his feet he overturned the vehicle, and all the pots and pans were upset and broken.

events.working_title: Trinavarta the Whirlwind Carries Off the Baby
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa's servant Trinavarta, in the form of a whirlwind, snatches the child away, blinding Gokula with dust as Yasoda searches in vain.

sources.source_excerpt: The demon Trinavarta, as a whirlwind of dust and grit, sweeps up the child so that Yasoda cannot find him, and the whole village is plunged into darkness and confusion. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 17-24)

events.working_title: Trinavarta Is Crushed by the Child's Weight
events.one_line_summary: Unable to carry the ever-heavier baby through the sky, Trinavarta falls onto a rock and is crushed, while the child is found safe on his chest.

sources.source_excerpt: The demon, finding the child heavier than a mountain, cannot fly on; seized by the throat, he crashes down upon a rock and is shattered, and the cowherds find Krishna lying safe upon his breast. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 25-32)

events.working_title: Yasoda Sees the Universe in the Nursing Child's Mouth
events.one_line_summary: As Yasoda nurses the yawning child, she glimpses the whole cosmos within his open mouth and trembles in wonder.

sources.source_excerpt: While Yasoda fondly looks at her child, he yawns and she beholds within his mouth the sky, the earth, the oceans, the sun and moon, and all beings, and she is struck with awe. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 33-37)

events.working_title: Garga Secretly Names Rama and Krishna
events.one_line_summary: The family priest Garga, sent by Vasudeva, secretly performs the naming ceremony, calling the boys Rama and Krishna, and foretells their glories.

sources.source_excerpt: Garga, coming quietly at Vasudeva's bidding, performs the naming rites in secret: the son of Rohini he names Rama and Balabhadra, and Nanda's son he names Krishna, and he declares that they will dispel all evil. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-19)
The initiatory rites requisite for the two boys were performed by Garga, who was sent to Gokula by Vasudeva for that purpose... and named the elder of them Ráma, and the other Krishńa.

events.working_title: Krishna and Rama's Childhood Pranks and Butter-Stealing
events.one_line_summary: The two boys crawl and toddle about Gokula, and Krishna steals butter and curds from the gopis' homes with playful tricks.

sources.source_excerpt: The boys crawl through the mud of Gokula to the delight of all; Krishna, the gopis complain, lets loose the calves, steals curd and butter, and smashes pots when he cannot reach them. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-30)

events.working_title: Krishna Eats Mud and Shows the Cosmos in His Mouth
events.one_line_summary: Accused of eating dirt, Krishna opens his mouth before Yasoda, who sees the entire universe within it and is overwhelmed.

sources.source_excerpt: When his playmates accuse him of eating mud, Krishna tells his mother to look in his mouth, and there she beholds the whole world with its mountains, oceans and stars; the Lord then veils her mind again in motherly love. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 31-45)

events.working_title: Krishna Breaks the Butter Pot
events.one_line_summary: While Yasoda churns, the hungry child climbs onto her lap; when she leaves, he breaks the churn-pot, steals the butter and feeds it to the monkeys, then flees as she chases him.

sources.source_excerpt: Interrupted in her churning to nurse the child, Yasoda returns to find the pot shattered and Krishna, with the stolen butter, feeding it to a monkey; he darts away and she pursues him with a stick. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-10)

events.working_title: Yasoda Binds Krishna to the Mortar
events.one_line_summary: Yasoda tries to tie the mischievous Krishna with a rope, but every rope falls short by two fingers, until, moved by her effort, he lets himself be bound.

sources.source_excerpt: However much rope Yasoda joins, it is always two fingers too short to bind him; seeing her toil and sweat, Krishna of his own grace submits and is bound to the mortar. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 11-20)

events.variant_notes: HV 1.62 and VP 5.6 fold this binding into the uprooting episode (see 'uproot_trees').

events.working_title: Krishna Notices the Twin Arjuna Trees
events.one_line_summary: While his mother is busy, Krishna sees the two arjuna trees that were once the guhyaka sons of Kubera, Nalakuvara and Manigriva.

sources.source_excerpt: Left to himself, Krishna catches sight of the twin arjuna trees, who in a former life had been Nalakuvara and Manigriva, the sons of Kubera. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 21-22)

events.working_title: Krishna Uproots the Twin Arjuna Trees (Named Damodara)
events.one_line_summary: Dragging the mortar to which he is tied, the crawling Krishna passes between the two trees and uproots them.

sources.source_excerpt: Pulling the mortar after him, Krishna passes between the two arjuna trees and, with a single tug, brings them crashing down. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 23-26)

Placing that mortar between the two trees he began to drag it... those two Arjuna trees were uprooted with their roots and branches... From that day in which he was bound with the rope Krishna was called Damodara.

Fastening a cord round his waist, she tied him to the wooden mortar... the lotus-eyed Krishńa... pulled the mortar after him to the space between two Arjuna trees... and as Krishńa pulled it through, it pulled down the trunks of the trees... It is hence that Krishńa is called Dámodara.

events.variant_notes: HV/VP fold in the mortar-binding beat.

events.working_title: The Two Devotees Are Liberated from the Trees
events.one_line_summary: From the fallen trees emerge two radiant beings who bow to Krishna, praise him, and, released from their curse, depart to the north.

sources.source_excerpt: From the fallen trees rise two brilliant figures who bow to Krishna, extol him as the ancient Lord, and, at his word, depart; the cowherds hear the crash and marvel. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 27-43)

events.working_title: The Fruit-Seller Receives a Gift of Jewels
events.one_line_summary: Krishna takes grain to barter for fruit, but the fruit-seller's basket fills with gems as her fruit spills into his hands.

sources.source_excerpt: Going out to buy fruit with a fistful of grain, Krishna lets it spill, and the fruit-seller finds her basket filled with jewels where her fruit had been. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 6-10)

events.working_title: The Cowherds Decide to Migrate to Vrindavan
events.one_line_summary: Citing the many evil omens that have befallen Gokula, the elder Upananda persuades the cowherds to migrate with their herds.

sources.source_excerpt: The elder Upananda declares that omens threaten the children, and that the whole colony, with its cattle and carts, should depart at once for a safer pasture. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-30)
The elders of the cowherds, with Nanda at their head... said they... 'We cannot remain in this place... let us go to Vrindávana, where terrestrial prodigies may no more disturb us.'

events.variant_notes: BP: prompted by Upananda citing omens; VP: alarmed by Putana's death, the waggon and the trees.

events.working_title: The Cowherds Settle in Vrindavan
events.one_line_summary: The cowherd community journeys with their herds and carts and settles in Vrindavan, forming their camp in a crescent of wagons.

sources.source_excerpt: With cattle before them and horns sounding, the cowherds travel to Vrindavan and pitch their camp there, delighted with the forest, the Govardhana hill and the banks of the Yamuna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 31-35)

events.working_title: Krishna Conjures Wolves to Move the Milkmen to Vrindavan
events.one_line_summary: Desiring a new forest, Krishna produces hundreds of wolves from his body to terrify the milkmen so they will abandon Vraja for Vrindavan.

sources.source_excerpt: From the hairs of his body there arose hundreds of wolves living on fat, blood and flesh... striking terror to the entire land of milkmen.

events.variant_notes: HV's version of the migration; BP/VP attribute the move to omens/portents instead (see 'migrate_decision').

events.working_title: Krishna Slays the Calf-Demon Vatsasura
events.one_line_summary: The boys take up calf-herding, and Krishna seizes the demon Vatsasura, who has taken the form of a calf, and hurls him dead into a kapittha tree.

sources.source_excerpt: As Krishna and Balarama tend the calves, the demon Vatsasura mingles with the herd in the form of a calf; Krishna whirls him by his hind legs and dashes him lifeless against a tree. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 36-44)

events.working_title: Krishna Slays the Crane-Demon Bakasura
events.one_line_summary: The crane-demon Bakasura, Kamsa's ally, swallows Krishna, but Krishna burns and tears him apart and frees himself.

sources.source_excerpt: The great crane-demon Bakasura gulps down Krishna, but the child sears his palate and then tears the demon apart, to the wonder of the cowherd boys. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 46-52)

events.working_title: Aghasura Becomes a Giant Python
events.one_line_summary: Aghasura, brother of Putana and Bakasura, takes the form of a vast python and lies with open mouth across the path of the boys.

sources.source_excerpt: The demon Aghasura, eager to avenge his kin, stretches his body into a gigantic python and lies across the path with gaping jaws, which the boys mistake for a mountain cave. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 12-24)

events.working_title: Krishna Kills Aghasura and Revives His Friends
events.one_line_summary: Entering the demon's throat with his friends, Krishna expands and chokes Aghasura to death, then revives the swallowed boys and calves; the demon's soul merges into Krishna as a great light.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna enters the demon's mouth and grows until he blocks its throat; as the demon's life departs, Krishna raises up his companions and calves and walks out, while a great radiance from the demon's body enters Krishna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 25-35)

events.working_title: Brahma Steals the Calves and Boys
events.one_line_summary: While Krishna searches for the strayed calves, Brahma, wanting to test the Lord, carries off all the calves and cowherd boys and hides them.

sources.source_excerpt: While the boys are at play, the calves wander off, and as Krishna goes to find them, Brahma secretly carries away both calves and boys, hiding them by his power. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 11-16)

events.working_title: Krishna Expands Into All the Calves and Boys
events.one_line_summary: To console their mothers, Krishna himself becomes every missing calf and boy, and for a year plays their roles in the cowherd homes.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna expands himself into every vanished calf and boy, and for a full year each mother unknowingly nurses and loves the Lord himself as her own child, with a love deeper than before. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 17-26)

events.working_title: Brahma Is Bewildered and Worships Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Returning after a moment of his time, Brahma finds everything as before and, seeing all the boys as four-armed forms of Vishnu, falls at Krishna's feet in humility.

sources.source_excerpt: Bewildered by what he sees, Brahma beholds all the cowherd boys and calves as countless Vishnu-forms and, understanding the Lord's majesty, bows and praises Krishna, who then restores his friends. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 27-63)

events.working_title: Brahma Praises Krishna and Departs
events.one_line_summary: Brahma hymns Krishna's boundless glories, confesses his own arrogance, and returns to his abode after circumambulating the Lord.

sources.source_excerpt: Brahma pours out a long hymn before Krishna, confessing that even he cannot fathom the Lord's power, and, walking three times around him and bowing, departs for his own realm. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-41)

events.working_title: The Boys Resume Their Meal Unaware of the Lost Year
events.one_line_summary: Krishna returns the boys and calves as before, and, though a year had passed, to them it seemed but a moment, and they finish their picnic and go home.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna brings the boys and calves back to the sandbank as though nothing had happened; to them the whole year seemed no more than half a moment, and they return, carrying the python's dried skin as a trophy. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 41-47)

events.working_title: The Boys Long for the Palm Grove's Fruit
events.one_line_summary: The cowherd boys ask Krishna and Balarama to take them to the talavana, whose sweet fruit is guarded by the donkey-demon Dhenuka.

sources.source_excerpt: The boys tell Krishna and Balarama of the palm grove whose fragrant fruit lies uneaten because the fierce donkey-demon Dhenuka and his kin guard it. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-26)

events.working_title: Balarama Slays the Ass-Demon Dhenuka
events.one_line_summary: Balarama shakes the palm trees to bring down the fruit, and when Dhenuka charges, he seizes the donkey and dashes it lifeless against a palm.

sources.source_excerpt: Balarama shakes the palms till the fruit falls; the enraged Dhenuka rushes in, and Balarama, catching him by the hind legs, whirls him and hurls him dead against a great palm. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 27-34)

Ráma, however, seized him by both hind legs, and whirling him round until he expired, tossed his carcass to the top of a palm tree... The animals that were of kin to Dhenuka came running to his aid; but Krishńa and Ráma treated them in the same manner.

events.variant_notes: BP attributes the deed jointly to Balarama; VP to Rama alone.

events.working_title: Krishna and Balarama Clear the Grove of Dhenuka's Kin
events.one_line_summary: As Dhenuka's kin charge to avenge him, Krishna and Balarama slay them all, and men and beasts freely enjoy the grove.

sources.source_excerpt: Dhenuka's kindred rush upon the brothers and are flung lifeless among the palms, until the grove lies strewn with their bodies and the people and cattle freely enjoy its fruit and grass. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 35-40)

events.working_title: Krishna Revives the Cowherds from Poisoned Water
events.one_line_summary: Thirsty cowherds and cattle drink the poisoned waters of the Yamuna and die; Krishna revives them all with a glance of nectar.

sources.source_excerpt: The cowherds and cattle, overcome by the poisoned water of the Yamuna, fall lifeless, but Krishna, the master of all yoga, restores them with a single nectar-showering glance. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 46-51)

events.working_title: Krishna Leaps into Kaliya's Poisoned Pool
events.one_line_summary: Seeing the Yamuna polluted by the serpent Kaliya's venom, Krishna climbs a kadamba tree and plunges into the deep poisoned pool to subdue him.

sources.source_excerpt: Determined to cleanse the Yamuna of Kaliya's poison, Krishna climbs a tall kadamba tree, slaps his arms, and dives into the serpent's deep and venomous pool. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 3-5)
Climbing up to the top of the tree and emitting a leonine roar the cloud-hued and lotus-eyed Krishna jumped headlong down into the lake.
he bound his clothes tightly about him, and jumped boldly into the lake of the serpent-king... Coiling themselves around Krishńa, they all bit him with teeth from which fiery poison was emitted.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.7 also includes the biting and the despair of the watchers.

events.working_title: Kaliya Coils Around Krishna and Vraja Despairs
events.one_line_summary: Kaliya coils around Krishna and holds him motionless in the depths, while the cowherds, cows and all of Gokula rush to the bank in grief.

sources.source_excerpt: The serpent Kaliya winds his coils about Krishna and holds him in the water; seeing their beloved gripped by the snake, the whole of Vraja, with Nanda and the gopis, comes wailing to the bank. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 8-20)

events.working_title: Krishna Dances on Kaliya's Heads
events.one_line_summary: Breaking free of the serpent's coils, Krishna leaps up and dances upon Kaliya's raised heads, trampling each hood that will not bow.

sources.source_excerpt: Slipping from the coils, Krishna springs onto the serpent's hoods and dances there, crushing each head that refuses to bow, while the celestial beings shower flowers and music upon him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 22-30)

events.variant_notes: HV/VP fold this dance into the banishment episode (see 'kaliya_banish').

events.working_title: Kaliya's Wives Plead for His Life
events.one_line_summary: The serpent's wives, with disheveled hair and folded hands, praise Krishna and beg him to spare their husband's life.

sources.source_excerpt: As Kaliya lies broken, his wives come before Krishna with folded hands and, praising him, plead that the chastisement itself is grace and that their husband's life be spared. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 30-52)

events.working_title: Krishna Spares and Banishes Kaliya
events.one_line_summary: Krishna spares Kaliya, orders him to leave the Yamuna for the ocean, and Kaliya departs with his family, leaving the river's waters sweet again.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna bids Kaliya depart with his kin to the ocean, declaring that the mark of Krishna's feet will protect him from Garuda; Kaliya worships him and leaves, and the Yamuna becomes pure and sweet once more. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 53-67)

Uddhava said: 'The cows, perishing from drinking the poisoned water, he restored; subduing the king of serpents, he raised them up and made that water again fit to drink.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 30)

placing his feet on the hoods of the serpent-king that were above the water... he began to dance there... 'O serpent, I do not wish to allow you to live in this water of Yamuna. Therefore repair to the ocean with your wife and kinsmen.'

Laying hold of the middle hood of their chief with both his hands, he bent it down, and set his foot upon the hitherto unbended head, and danced upon it in triumph... So saying, Hari set the snake-king at liberty, who... departed to the ocean.

events.variant_notes: HV/VP fold in the dance on the hoods; bpc1_035 is Uddhava's recollection.

events.working_title: Why Kaliya Took Refuge in the Yamuna
events.one_line_summary: The sage recounts how Kaliya, having withheld Garuda's tribute and been beaten by him, fled to the Yamuna pool, where a curse forbade Garuda to enter.

sources.source_excerpt: It is told how Kaliya, who had scorned the tribute owed to Garuda, was struck by his wing and fled into the Yamuna; there the sage Saubhari's curse kept Garuda from entering. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-11)

events.working_title: Krishna Emerges and the Villagers Rejoice
events.one_line_summary: Krishna comes out of the pool adorned with gems; the cowherds embrace him, and Nanda gives cattle and gold to the brahmanas for his deliverance.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna emerges from the pool, and the cowherds, as though their breath had returned, embrace him; Nanda bestows cows and gold upon the brahmanas in thanksgiving for his son's escape. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 12-18)

events.working_title: Krishna Resolves to Subdue the Serpent Kaliya
events.one_line_summary: Finding the Yamuna's lake poisoned by the serpent-king Kaliya, Krishna resolves to leap in and vanquish him.

sources.source_excerpt: 'I should, however, vanquish this king of serpents... I shall climb this Kadamba tree, jump into the lake and vanquish Kalya.'

events.variant_notes: HV-specific precursor; see 'kaliya_leap'.

events.working_title: Krishna Swallows the Forest Fire at Night
events.one_line_summary: As a forest fire surrounds the sleeping settlement at night, the villagers call on Krishna, who drinks up the fierce flames.

sources.source_excerpt: When a blazing forest fire closes in on the sleeping Vraja, the terrified people cry out to Krishna, and the Lord, of boundless power, drinks the whole fire into himself. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-24)

events.working_title: Pralamba Joins the Games in Disguise
events.one_line_summary: The demon Pralamba, intent on seizing the boys, joins their play disguised as a cowherd, and Krishna, knowing him, allows it, planning his death.

sources.source_excerpt: Pralamba, a demon in cowherd's form, enters the boys' games; Krishna, who knows all, welcomes his friendship while resolving his destruction. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 16-18)

events.working_title: Balarama Slays the Demon Pralamba
events.one_line_summary: In the riding game, Pralamba carries Balarama far off and reveals his terrible form, but Balarama strikes his head with a mighty fist and fells him dead.

sources.source_excerpt: When the demon Pralamba, carrying Balarama in the game, flees skyward and shows his giant form, Balarama strikes him once on the head with his fist, and the demon falls dead like a mountain. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 19-29)
with his well-formed fist resembling a thunder-bolt struck the wicked Pralamva on the head... on that Daitya... being slain, the celestials... gave him the name Baladeva after his action.

the powerful Baladeva laughed, and squeezed Pralamba with his knees, striking him at the same time on the head and face with his fists, so as to beat out both his eyes... fell upon the ground, and expired.

events.working_title: The Cattle Stray Into the Munja Forest and a Wildfire Breaks Out
events.one_line_summary: While the boys play, the cattle wander into a dense grove of munja grass, and a fierce wildfire springs up around them.

sources.source_excerpt: The cattle, roaming at will, stray into the munja thicket and are lost, and as the boys search, a great wildfire, driven by the wind, surrounds them and the herds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-8)

events.working_title: Krishna Swallows the Wildfire and Saves the Herd
events.one_line_summary: Krishna bids the terrified cowherds close their eyes, drinks up the flames, and, when they open them, they stand safe at Bhandira.

sources.source_excerpt: Telling them not to fear and to shut their eyes, Krishna drinks the raging fire into his mouth, and the cowherds, opening their eyes, find themselves and their herds delivered at Bhandira. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 9-13)

events.working_title: Krishna Enjoys the Monsoon Pastures
events.one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama enter the rain-washed forest with the herd, and the boys share a simple meal of curd-rice with him on a rock.

sources.source_excerpt: In the rains, Krishna and Balarama lead the cattle into the lush forest, where they picnic on curd and rice set out on a stone and rest among the contented cows. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 24-30)

events.working_title: The Gopis Praise Krishna's Flute
events.one_line_summary: Krishna plays his flute in the forest, and the gopis, describing its sweetness to one another, are carried away into his pastimes.

sources.source_excerpt: As Krishna's flute-song sounds through the forest, the gopis tell one another how even the deer, the rivers and the gods are enchanted by it, and they are lost in remembrance of him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-19)

events.working_title: The Gopis Perform the Katyayani Vow
events.one_line_summary: Through the first month of winter, the young gopis bathe in the Yamuna and worship the goddess Katyayani, praying that Krishna become their husband.

sources.source_excerpt: Through the first month of winter the gopis keep their vow, bathing before dawn in the Yamuna and worshipping an image of the goddess, with the single prayer that Nanda's son become their husband. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-5)

events.working_title: Krishna Steals the Gopis' Clothes
events.one_line_summary: Krishna carries off the gopis' garments as they bathe, climbs a kadamba tree, and teasingly bids them come and take them back.

sources.source_excerpt: While the gopis bathe, Krishna gathers up their clothes, climbs a kadamba tree, and, laughing, tells them to come and receive their garments one by one. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 6-11)

events.working_title: Krishna Returns the Clothes and Blesses the Gopis
events.one_line_summary: The shivering gopis come from the water, and Krishna, pleased with their sincerity, returns their clothes and promises their wish will be fulfilled.

sources.source_excerpt: Coming from the water with hands pressed together, the gopis receive back their garments, and Krishna tells them he has understood their vow, and that their longing for him shall bear its fruit in the coming nights. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 12-27)

events.working_title: The Brahmanas Refuse Krishna's Request for Food
events.one_line_summary: Hungry, Krishna sends the cowherd boys to ask food of brahmanas performing a sacrifice, but they turn the request away, mistaking Krishna for a mere man.

sources.source_excerpt: Sent by Krishna to beg food from the brahmanas performing the Angirasa sacrifice, the boys are refused, for the ritualists, proud of their learning, do not recognize the Lord. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-11)

events.working_title: The Brahmanas' Wives Bring Food to Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Krishna then sends the boys to the brahmanas' wives, who, longing for his sight, hasten to him with every kind of food, disregarding their families.

sources.source_excerpt: The wives of the brahmanas, hearing that Krishna has come, take dishes of fine food and hurry to him like rivers to the sea, heedless of husbands and kinsmen who would stop them. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 12-19)

events.working_title: The Wives Refuse to Return and Krishna Welcomes Them
events.one_line_summary: The brahmana wives, granted Krishna's sight, refuse to return to their homes, and Krishna, pleased with their devotion, assures them of his grace and sends them back with their minds fixed on him.

sources.source_excerpt: Falling at Krishna's feet, the wives declare they have no refuge but him and will not return; Krishna welcomes them and, teaching that he is won by remembrance rather than by nearness, sends them home with hearts fixed on him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-31)

events.working_title: The Brahmanas Repent and Praise Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Reflecting that their wives' devotion surpassed their own empty rituals, the brahmanas lament their blindness and sing Krishna's praise, longing to see him.

sources.source_excerpt: Realizing that the Lord they had spurned was Vishnu himself, the brahmanas reproach their own pride and empty rites, and, praising Krishna, yearn for his sight yet do not dare approach, fearing Kamsa. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 32-51)

events.working_title: Krishna Questions the Indra Sacrifice
events.one_line_summary: Krishna, bowing humbly, asks Nanda and the elders what ceremony they have begun, its fruit, for whom, and by what means it is accomplished.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, bowing humbly, asked the elders led by Nanda: 'Tell me, father, what is this ceremony you have undertaken? What is its fruit, for whom, and by what means is the sacrifice accomplished?' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 2)

events.working_title: Nanda Explains the Indra Worship
events.one_line_summary: Nanda explains that Indra, lord of rain, is worshipped with offerings produced by his own showers.

sources.source_excerpt: Nanda replied: 'Indra is the lord of the clouds, and by his showers all beings are nourished; we and other men worship him with offerings made of the things his rain produces.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 7-8)

events.working_title: Krishna Argues for Worshipping Govardhana Hill
events.one_line_summary: Krishna tells Nanda the cowherds should worship Govardhana hill, the cows and the brahmins rather than Indra.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, to break Indra's pride, argued that beings are born and perish by their own karma, that the cowherds' living is cattle and forest, and so the sacrifice should be offered to Govardhana hill, the cows and the brahmins, not to Indra. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 12-24)
'We are all milk-men who range in the forest. The precious kine constitute our subsistence. We should therefore worship the kine, the mountains and the forests.'

We, father, are neither cultivators of the soil, nor dealers in merchandise; we are sojourners in forests, and cows are our divinities... Let prayer and offerings then be addressed to the mountain Govarddhana.

events.working_title: The Cowherds Worship Govardhana and Krishna Receives Offerings as the Hill
events.one_line_summary: Nanda and the cowherds accept Krishna's words and perform the sacrifice to Govardhana hill.

sources.source_excerpt: Nanda and the cowherds accepted Krishna's words and performed everything as he had said: they gave offerings to the hill, the cows and the brahmins, and with their cattle made circumambulation of Govardhana. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 30-32)

Krishna, taking another form and declaring 'I am the hill,' ate the abundant offerings, and the people of Vraja, seeing the embodied hill, bowed to it, saying 'Behold, the hill has favored us.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 34-36)
Upon the summit of Govarddhana, Krishńa presented himself, saying, "I am the mountain," and partook of much food presented by the Gopas.

events.variant_notes: BP splits the worship (10.24) and Krishna's manifestation (10.24) into two beats; VP 5.10 combines them.

events.working_title: Indra Becomes Furious
events.one_line_summary: Indra learns his worship has been stopped and grows angry with the cowherds whose lord is Krishna.

sources.source_excerpt: When Indra learned that his own worship had been obstructed, he grew angry with the cowherds, Nanda and the rest, whose lord was Krishna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 38)

events.working_title: Indra Unleashes the Storm on Vrindavan
events.one_line_summary: Furious Indra sends the Samvartaka storm-clouds to destroy Nanda's gokula with torrent, hail and wind.

sources.source_excerpt: Furious Indra set in motion the Samvartaka clouds of destruction, saying 'Scatter the pride of these cowherds, drive their cattle to destruction'; and the clouds, freed of restraint, tormented Nanda's gokula with torrents, lightning, thunder and hail. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)
'Therefore within seven nights, distress, with rain and winds, the precious kine which constitute their life-long subsistence.'

Now, therefore, afflict the cattle, that are their sustenance, and whence their occupation is derived, with rain and wind... In an instant the earth, the points of the horizon, and the sky, were all blended into one by the heavy and incessant shower.

events.working_title: Krishna Lifts Govardhana Hill
events.one_line_summary: Krishna lifts Govardhana hill with one hand and holds it aloft like an umbrella to shelter the cowherds.

sources.source_excerpt: Seeing the cowherds stricken by hail and wind, Krishna reasoned that Indra in anger was sending this out-of-season storm, and to destroy the pride of those who fancy themselves lords, he lifted Govardhana hill with one hand and held it up like an umbrella. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 13-18)

Uddhava said: 'He had the cowherd king perform the go-savana sacrifice; and when Indra, his pride broken, rained down in fury, the terrified Vraja was sheltered by the umbrella of the hill, the Lord favouring his devotees.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 31-32)
For protecting the Gopas like unto Brahma the Lord Krishna raised up that mountain and kept it on the tip of his finger.

Krishńa immediately plucked up the mountain Govarddhana, and held it aloft with one hand in sport... For seven days and nights did the vast clouds sent by Indra rain upon the Gokula of Nanda... but they were protected by the elevation of the mountain.

events.variant_notes: HV/VP specify seven nights/days; bpc1_036 is Uddhava's recollection.

events.working_title: Seven Days Beneath Govardhana
events.one_line_summary: The cowherds shelter beneath the hill for seven days while Krishna holds it, until Indra relents.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna told the cowherds to enter the hollow beneath the hill with their cattle without fear, and he held the mountain for seven days without moving from his place; Indra, astonished, checked his clouds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 19-23)

events.variant_notes: Folded into 'govardhana_lift' in HV/VP.

events.working_title: Krishna Restores the Hill and the Cowherds Rejoice
events.one_line_summary: Krishna sets the hill back in place; Nanda, Yashoda and Balarama embrace him and the gods rain flowers.

sources.source_excerpt: When the storm ceased the cowherds came out with their goods, and Krishna set the hill back in its place as before; Nanda, Yashoda, Rohini and Balarama embraced him, the gods rained flowers, and the gopis sang of his deeds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-32)

events.working_title: The Cowherds Wonder at Krishna's Deeds
events.one_line_summary: Astonished at Krishna's deeds, the cowherds wonder how a boy could do such things, and Nanda reassures them with Garga's words.

sources.source_excerpt: The cowherds, astonished at Krishna's superhuman deeds, wondered how a seven-year-old boy could hold up a great mountain, and Nanda recounted to them the words of Garga, who had foretold that this child was Vasudeva, equal to Narayana, who would protect them from all dangers. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-16)

Assuredly we repose at the feet of Hari... for, having witnessed thy power, we cannot believe thee to be a man... Krishna replied, '...be satisfied to know that I am your kinsman. I am neither god, nor Yaksha, nor Gandharba, nor Dánava.'

events.variant_notes: BP adds Nanda recounting Garga's prophecy.

events.working_title: Indra Surrenders and Begs Forgiveness
events.one_line_summary: Ashamed Indra approaches Krishna, touches his feet, and asks forgiveness for his pride.

sources.source_excerpt: Indra, ashamed, approached Krishna in seclusion, touched his feet with his crown, and said: 'I, intoxicated by my sovereignty, have offended you, not knowing your power; forgive me, Lord, and may such evil intention never arise in me again.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-15)

events.working_title: Indra Installs Krishna as Govinda
events.one_line_summary: Surabhi the divine cow praises Krishna, and Indra bathes and names him Govinda.

sources.source_excerpt: Surabhi, the divine cow, praised Krishna, saying the gods, urged by Brahma, would consecrate him; then Indra, with the waters of the celestial Ganga, bathed Krishna and named him Govinda, and the gods, Gandharvas and Siddhas celebrated. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 20-22)
Thereupon taking those jars full of heavenly water the king of gods... sprinkled Govinda... 'the people of this world will hymn thee as Govinda.'
I have now come by desire of the cattle, grateful for their preservation, in order to install you as Upendra; and, as the Indra of the cows, thou shalt be called Govinda.

events.working_title: Indra Asks Krishna to Befriend Arjuna
events.one_line_summary: Indra asks Krishna to protect his son Arjuna, Krishna's cousin, in the coming war of the Bharatas.

sources.source_excerpt: 'O Govinda, he will be thy friend and help in battle... do thou instruct him in spiritual knowledge... always regard and take care of him as thou dost me.'
A portion of me has been born as Arjuna, the son of Pritha: let him ever be defended by thee... To this Krishńa replied, "I know thy son... and I will befriend him as long as I continue upon earth."

events.working_title: Nanda Is Seized by Varuna and Rescued
events.one_line_summary: A servant of Varuna seizes Nanda as he bathes at night; Krishna goes to Varuna's abode and frees him.

sources.source_excerpt: While Nanda bathed in the Yamuna at night, a servant of Varuna seized him and carried him to Varuna's abode; Krishna, hearing the cowherds' cries, went there, and Varuna, honoring him, returned Nanda with apologies. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

events.working_title: Krishna Reveals His Supreme Abode
events.one_line_summary: Krishna shows the cowherds his own abode beyond darkness, the eternal Brahman-light.

sources.source_excerpt: Nanda told his kinsmen of the wondrous honor shown by the lord of the waters; and Krishna, wishing to grant his people's desire, revealed to the cowherds his own abode beyond darkness, the eternal light of Brahman. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-15)

events.working_title: Nanda Is Swallowed by a Serpent and Freed
events.one_line_summary: A great serpent swallows Nanda as he sleeps; Krishna's touch frees the cursed Vidyadhara Sudarshana.

sources.source_excerpt: As the cowherds slept in Ambika's forest, a great hungry serpent swallowed Nanda; the cowherds struck it with firebrands in vain, but when Krishna touched it with his foot it became Sudarshana the Vidyadhara, freed from a sage's curse, and Nanda was released. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 4-17)

events.working_title: Shankhachuda Abducts the Gopis
events.one_line_summary: As Krishna and Balarama sing in the forest, the demon Shankhachuda carries off the gopis.

sources.source_excerpt: As Krishna and Balarama sang in the forest at night among the gopis, the demon Shankhachuda, servant of Kubera, carried off the women, who cried 'Krishna! Rama!'; and the two brothers pursued him like two lions. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-27)

events.working_title: Krishna Slays Shankhachuda and Takes the Jewel
events.one_line_summary: Krishna overtakes the demon, strikes him dead and gives the crest-jewel to Balarama.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna overtook the fleeing demon, struck his head with his fist and took the bright jewel from his crest, and gave it to his elder brother Balarama while the women looked on. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 29-31)

events.working_title: The Gopis Abandon Their Homes
events.one_line_summary: Krishna plays his flute on an autumn night and the gopis leave homes, husbands and duties to rush to him.

sources.source_excerpt: Seeing the autumn nights, Krishna resolved to enjoy himself; he played his flute, and the gopis, their minds captured, left their homes, husbands, children and duties and hurried to him, heedless of all restraint. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-7)

events.working_title: Krishna Tests the Gopis
events.one_line_summary: Krishna tells the gopis to return to their husbands, and they plead that he is their very soul.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna first told the gopis to return to their husbands and children, speaking of the duty of women; but the gopis answered with tears that he was their very soul, and that having abandoned everything for his feet, they could not return. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 17-41)

events.working_title: Krishna Relents and Sports with the Gopis
events.one_line_summary: Krishna smiles, shows the gopis favor, and enjoys himself with them on the Yamuna's bank.

sources.source_excerpt: Hearing their lament, Krishna, though self-satisfied, smilingly showed them favor and enjoyed himself with them on the sandy bank of the Yamuna, and the gopis thought themselves the most blessed of women. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 42-46)

events.working_title: Krishna Vanishes
events.one_line_summary: To quell the pride rising in the gopis, Krishna suddenly disappears.

sources.source_excerpt: Seeing the pride that had arisen in the gopis from their good fortune, Krishna vanished then and there, to humble them and favor them. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 47)

events.working_title: The Gopis Search the Forest
events.one_line_summary: The gopis wander the forest questioning the trees and plants about the vanished Krishna.

sources.source_excerpt: When Krishna disappeared, the gopis searched for him like madwomen from wood to wood, questioning the trees and plants, 'Have you seen Nanda's son, who stole our hearts with his smiles?' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 3-4)

events.working_title: The Gopis Enact Krishna's Lilas
events.one_line_summary: In their frenzy the gopis imitate Krishna's childhood deeds, each playing a part.

sources.source_excerpt: In their frenzy the gopis imitated Krishna's deeds: one played Putana and another the cart; one lifted her arm like Govardhana, and another declared 'I am Krishna, see my graceful gait.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-19)

events.working_title: The Favored Gopi's Pride and Krishna's Second Vanishing
events.one_line_summary: Finding footprints of Krishna and his chosen gopi, the gopis marvel; she grows proud, and Krishna vanishes again.

sources.source_excerpt: Finding Krishna's footprints and those of the gopi he had taken aside, the gopis marveled at her fortune; that favored gopi, grown proud, asked Krishna to carry her, and when he took her on his shoulder he vanished again, and she repented. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-38)

events.working_title: Krishna Reappears Among the Gopis
events.one_line_summary: Krishna reappears smiling and the gopis rise as if their life had returned; their grief ends.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna then appeared among the gopis, smiling, and they all rose at once as if their very life had returned; each embraced him in her own way, and their grief of separation was dispelled. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-9)

events.working_title: Krishna Teaches About Love
events.one_line_summary: Krishna answers the gopis' question about why he loves those who love him, explaining the ways of love.

sources.source_excerpt: When the gopis asked why he loves those who love him, Krishna explained the ways of love, and told them their love for him, which had severed the bonds of home, could never be repaid, but that it returned to them of itself. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 15-21)

events.working_title: The Great Rasa Dance
events.one_line_summary: Krishna multiplies himself to dance between every gopi in the moonlit rasa; the gods watch and rain flowers.

sources.source_excerpt: There Govinda began the rasa dance with the gopis, multiplying himself to stand between every pair; the gods rained flowers, the celestial women watching were bewildered, and Krishna sported with them through the moonlit autumn nights. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-24)
Uddhava said: 'Honouring the face of night washed by the rays of the autumn moon, he sang sweet songs and sported as the ornament of the circle of the women.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 33)
Thus encircled by the milk-women Krishna used to sport, of his own accord, in the autumnal night adorned by the moon.

Krishńa thought the lovely moonlight night of autumn propitious to the Rasa dance... Then proceeded the dance to the music of their clashing bracelets, and songs that celebrated in suitable strain the charms of the autumnal season.

events.variant_notes: bpc1_037 is Uddhava's recollection.

events.working_title: Krishna Slays the Bull-Demon Arishta
