events.one_line_summary: The bull-demon Arishta terrorizes Vrindavan until Krishna seizes and slays him.

sources.source_excerpt: The bull-demon Arishta, terrifying the cowherds and cattle, charged at Krishna, who seized him by the horns, flung him aside, threw him down and slew him; and the gods praised Krishna with showers of flowers. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-14)

he seized him as an alligator would have done, and held him firmly by the horns, whilst he pressed his sides with his knees... and then tearing off one of the horns, he beat the fierce demon with it until he died.

events.working_title: Krishna Slays the Horse-Demon Keshi
events.one_line_summary: The horse-demon Keshi attacks, and Krishna thrusts his arm into its mouth until it chokes and dies.

sources.source_excerpt: The horse-demon Keshi, sent by Kamsa, terrified the cowherds, but Krishna thrust his arm into the demon's open mouth and expanded it until Keshi, choked, fell dead, and the gods showered flowers on Krishna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-7)
Krishna, stretching his hands a good deal, sundered him in twain... 'Since thou hast slain Keshi, thou shalt pass by the name of Keshava in the world.'

Krishńa enlarging the bulk of his arm, thrust it into his mouth, and wrenched out the teeth... The formidable demon, having his mouth rent open by the arm of Krishńa, fell down, torn asunder like a tree struck by lightning... thou shalt be known in the world by the name of Keśava.

events.working_title: Krishna Slays the Demon Vyoma
events.one_line_summary: The demon Vyoma, disguised as a cowherd, carries off boys and seals them in a cave; Krishna slays him and frees them.

sources.source_excerpt: As the cowherd boys played at thieves and keepers, the demon Vyoma, son of Maya, carried off many of them in a cowherd's disguise and sealed them in a mountain cave; Krishna seized and slew him and freed the boys. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 25-32)

events.working_title: Akrura Journeys to Vrindavan
events.one_line_summary: On the road Akrura, filled with devotion, ponders what merit has earned him the sight of Krishna.

sources.source_excerpt: On the road Akrura, filled with devotion, pondered what merit had earned him the sight of Krishna, and he arrived at Gokula at sunset, gazing at the footprints of the Lord marked with the lotus and other signs. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-23)

events.working_title: Akrura Arrives in Vrindavan and Beholds Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Akrura sees Krishna and Balarama, prostrates, and is honored by Nanda with food and questions.

sources.source_excerpt: Akrura saw Krishna and Balarama among the milking cows, fell at their feet, and was embraced; Nanda received him with food and honor, and asked how the Yadavas fared under the cruel Kamsa. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 33-42)
As soon as he entered the gate... he saw Krishna stationed at the milking-place in the midst of calves like a bull... he praised him again and again.

he saw Krishńa amongst the cattle, dark as the leaf of the full blown lotus... Akrúra also beheld there Balabhadra, white as a jasmine, a swan, or the moon... When Akrúra saw these two youths, his countenance expanded with delight.

events.working_title: Akrura Reveals Kamsa's Plan and Krishna Agrees to Go
events.one_line_summary: Krishna questions Akrura, who tells him of Kamsa's enmity and the purpose of his mission.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna asked Akrura the news, and Akrura told him everything: Kamsa's enmity toward the Yadavas, his resolve to kill Vasudeva, and the reason he himself had been sent as messenger. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 3-8)
'O Krishna, that ascetic lady is being exhausted with your sorrow... do thou now make such an exertion... for saving thy aged parents overwhelmed with grief.'... Krishna... said 'So be it.'
Akúra told them how their father Ánakadundubhi... had been insulted by the iniquitous demon Kansa... The destroyer of Keśin said to him, '...Within three nights I will slay Kansa and his adherents.'

events.variant_notes: VP 5.18 has Krishna vow to slay Kansa within three nights.

events.working_title: The Gopis Grieve at Krishna's Departure
events.one_line_summary: When Nanda proclaims the journey to Mathura, the gopis lament that Akrura is taking Krishna away.

sources.source_excerpt: When Nanda proclaimed that they would go to Mathura, the gopis were stricken with grief, and they lamented, saying that Akrura, whose name means 'not cruel,' was cruel indeed to take Krishna away. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 12-30)

The Gopís, seeing them about to set forth, were much afflicted; they wept bitterly... 'Alas! alas! we see now only the dust of his chariot wheels! and now he is far away, for even that dust is no longer to be seen!'

events.working_title: Krishna Consoles the Gopis
events.one_line_summary: As the chariot leaves, Krishna promises the weeping gopis that he will return.

sources.source_excerpt: The gopis wept and followed the departing chariot, and Krishna consoled them with messages, saying 'I will come back'; and they returned, singing of his deeds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 31-36)

events.working_title: Akrura Beholds the Divine Vision in the Yamuna
events.one_line_summary: Diving in the Yamuna, Akrura sees Krishna and Balarama as the Lord resting on Shesha surrounded by gods.

sources.source_excerpt: At the Yamuna, Akrura bathed and, diving, beheld Krishna and Balarama there as the Lord resting on Shesha, surrounded by the hosts of gods; and he rose and praised him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 37-56)
sinking into the lake of Yamuna... he saw there the thousand-headed Deity Ananta... and the dark blue hued Vishnu... seated at ease on the lap of that king of serpents.

he beheld mentally Balabhadra, having a thousand hooded beads... On his lap he also beheld... Krishńa, of the complexion of a cloud... armed with the discus and other weapons... Apprehending, therefore, their real character, he thus eulogized the eternal deity.

events.working_title: Akrura Reports to Kamsa
events.one_line_summary: Krishna withdraws the divine vision; Akrura drives on and reports to Kamsa before going home.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna withdrew the vision as an actor withdraws a play; Akrura, wondering, drove on, and after Krishna bade him go ahead, he entered Mathura, reported to Kamsa, and went to his own house. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-18)

events.working_title: Narada Reveals the Truth to Kamsa
events.one_line_summary: Narada tells Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama are the sons of Devaki and Rohini; Kamsa binds Vasudeva and Devaki.

sources.source_excerpt: Narada came and told Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama were the sons of Devaki and Rohini, whom the frightened Vasudeva had entrusted to Nanda; hearing this, Kamsa seized his sword and bound Vasudeva and Devaki in iron fetters. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 15-18)

Nárada went to Kansa, and related to him the whole, beginning with the transference of the child from Devakí to Yaśodá... Kansa was highly incensed with Vasudeva, and bitterly reproached him, and all the Yádavas.

events.working_title: Kamsa Orders the Wrestlers and Elephant to Kill Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa summons Chanura and Mushtika and orders Krishna and Balarama killed by wrestling and by the elephant Kuvalayapida.

sources.source_excerpt: Kamsa summoned Chanura, Mushtika and his other wrestlers and ministers, and ordered that Krishna and Balarama be brought to Mathura to be killed in a wrestling match, with the elephant Kuvalayapida set at the arena gate to slay them. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 19-25)

'Forsooth, fighting in the arena with those two forest-ranging cow-herd boys Krishna and Sangkarshana... you will be able to throw them on earth and kill them.'... 'Keep at the gate of the arena the... elephant Kuvalayapida.'

events.working_title: Kamsa Sends Akrura to Fetch Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa, taking Akrura by the hand, sends him with sweet words to bring Krishna and Balarama to Mathura.

sources.source_excerpt: Kamsa, taking Akrura by the hand, sent him with sweet words to bring Krishna and Balarama from Vraja, saying the bow sacrifice was to be seen; and Akrura, though he knew Kamsa's intent, agreed to carry out the command. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-39)
'Whatever it may be, O giver of gifts, go to Vraja, at my command and bring these two boys, Nanda and other Gopas who pay tributes to me.'

I will send the noble Yadu, Akrúra the son of Swaphalka, to Gokula, to bring them hither: I will order the fierce Keśin... to attack them... my elephant Kuvalayápíd́a shall trample to death these two cow-boy sons of Vasudeva.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.15 also folds in the sending of Kesin.

events.working_title: Krishna and Balarama Enter Mathura
events.one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama enter Mathura with the cowherds, and the city's women throng to see them.

sources.source_excerpt: In the afternoon Krishna and Balarama entered Mathura with the cowherds, and the women of the city thronged to see them, forgetting their dress and work, and the brahmins honored them with curd, rice and garlands. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 18-30)

events.working_title: Krishna Slays the Insolent Washerman
events.one_line_summary: The king's washerman refuses Krishna clothes and abuses him; Krishna strikes off his head and takes the garments.

sources.source_excerpt: When Krishna asked the king's washerman for fine clothes, the washerman abused him, saying these belonged to the king; and Krishna, angered, struck off his head with his hand, took the garments and distributed them to the cowherds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 31-38)
Krishna grew offended with him and struck him on the head with his fist strong as the thunder-bolt. With his head sundered he fell down lifeless on earth.

The washerman was the servant of Kansa, made insolent by his master's favour; and he provoked the two lads with loud and scurrilous abuse, until Krishńa struck him down, with his head to the ground, and killed him.

events.working_title: The Weaver and Sudama (Flower-Seller) Honor Krishna
events.one_line_summary: A weaver dresses Krishna and Balarama, and the garland-maker Sudama honors them and receives a boon.

sources.source_excerpt: A weaver gladly dressed Krishna and Balarama in fine clothes, and Sudama the garland-maker, honoring them with garlands and sandal paste, received from Krishna the boon of unshakable devotion. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 39-51)

Krishńa then, being much pleased with him, gave him this blessing; "Fortune, good friend, who depends upon me, shall never forsake you... you shall finally obtain... a heavenly region, the consequence of my favour."

events.variant_notes: BP adds the weaver; VP has only the flower-seller.

events.working_title: Krishna Straightens the Hunchback Kubja
events.one_line_summary: Kubja gives Krishna sandal paste, and he straightens her crooked body into a beautiful woman.

sources.source_excerpt: The hunchback woman Kubja gave Krishna her sandal paste; pleased, Krishna pressed her cheeks and straightened her crooked body into a beautiful woman, and she begged him to come to her house, and he promised. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-12)

Krishna, conversant with the art of arranging for sports, softly touched the haunch of Kuvja with his fingers... Knowing her haunch (thus) broken, the beautiful and sweet smiling Kuvja... said with love to Krishna.

Then Krishńa, skilled in the curative art, took hold of her, under the chin, with the thumb and two fingers, and lifted up her head, whilst with his feet he pressed down her feet; and in this way he made her straight.

events.working_title: Krishna Breaks Kamsa's Great Bow
events.one_line_summary: Krishna seizes Kamsa's great bow and breaks it, then strikes down the attacking guards.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna entered the hall of the great bow, seized it though the guards forbade him, and with one hand broke it in the middle like a sugarcane; and with the two pieces he struck down the angry guards Kamsa had sent. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-20)
Bent with force by Krishna that celebrated bow, resembling a serpent, broke in twain.
he took it, and bent it; but drawing it with violence, he snapped it in two, and all Mathurá resounded with the noise which its fracture occasioned.

events.working_title: Kamsa Is Terrified by Evil Omens
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa, hearing of the bow's breaking, spends a sleepless night beset by omens and dreams of death.

sources.source_excerpt: Hearing of the bow's breaking and his guards' death, Kamsa spent a sleepless night terrified by evil omens and dreams — the loss of his own head, visions of corpses, and of himself riding an ass — all foretelling his death. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 25-30)

events.working_title: Kamsa Orders the Wrestling Festival
events.one_line_summary: At dawn Kamsa orders the wrestling festival; the arena is prepared and the cowherds arrive with offerings.

sources.source_excerpt: At dawn Kamsa ordered the wrestling festival, and the arena was prepared with drums and banners; Chanura, Mushtika and the other wrestlers took their places, and Nanda and the cowherds, summoned, arrived with their offerings. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 31-37)

events.working_title: Krishna Slays the Elephant Kuvalayapida
events.one_line_summary: At the arena gate Krishna evades the elephant Kuvalayapida, throws it down, tears out its tusk and slays it.

sources.source_excerpt: At the arena gate stood the elephant Kuvalayapida; when its keeper drove it at Krishna, he dodged beneath it, seized it by the tail and trunk, threw it down, tore out its tusk, and slew the beast and its keepers. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-15)
placing his foot on his lower lip he, with his two hands, uprooted his tusks and struck him therewith... that huge elephant, with his tusks broken, fell down.
Covered with must and blood from the elephant, whom, when goaded upon them by his driver, they had slain, and armed with his tusks, Balabhadra and Janárddana confidently entered the arena.

events.working_title: The Citizens Rejoice in the Arena
events.one_line_summary: Entering with the tusk as weapon, Krishna delights the people, who recount his deeds as Narayana and Rama.

sources.source_excerpt: Entering the arena with the elephant's tusk as his weapon, Krishna delighted the people, who recounted his deeds to one another, saying these two were Narayana and Rama descended in Vasudeva's house. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 16-30)

events.working_title: Chanura Challenges Krishna and Balarama
events.one_line_summary: Chanura invites Krishna and Balarama to wrestle; Krishna answers that they are boys, but Chanura insists.

sources.source_excerpt: Chanura addressed Krishna and Balarama, inviting them to wrestle for the king's pleasure; Krishna replied that they were boys and would play with equals, but Chanura urged, 'Fight me, and let Mushtika fight Balarama.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 30-39)

events.working_title: Krishna and Balarama Slay the Wrestlers
events.one_line_summary: Despite the women's protest, Krishna slays Chanura and Balarama slays Mushtika, Kuta, Shala and Tośala.

sources.source_excerpt: The women protested the unequal match, but Krishna seized Chanura, whirled him and dashed him to the ground, killing him, while Balarama slew Mushtika, and Rama and Krishna slew Kuta, Shala and Tośala. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-27)
Wrestling with Chanura for a long time, Devaki's son... stole away his strength... struck him on the head with his fist... Thus with his eyes drawn out Chanura... lay in the arena.

Having whirled Cháńúra round a hundred times... Krishńa dashed him on the ground with such violence as to smash his body into a hundred fragments... the mighty Baladeva... pummelled him there till he was dead.

events.working_title: Kamsa Orders the Gopas Expelled and Vasudeva Punished
events.one_line_summary: Seeing his wrestlers slain, Kansa orders the cowherds expelled, Nanda bound, and Vasudeva punished; Krishna grows wrathful.

sources.source_excerpt: 'Turn out of the arena these two sinful, grim-visaged and forest-ranging young cow-herds... punish him even today in such a way which persons not, aged, deserve.'

events.variant_notes: HV-specific; the provocation immediately preceding the killing (see 'slay_kamsa').

events.working_title: Krishna Slays Kamsa
events.one_line_summary: As Kamsa orders Nanda bound and Vasudeva killed, Krishna leaps onto the dais, seizes and slays him.

sources.source_excerpt: As Kamsa ordered Nanda bound and Vasudeva killed, Krishna, enraged, leapt onto the high dais, seized Kamsa by the hair, hurled him into the arena and fell upon him, dragging his body about before all the people. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 28-38)

Uddhava said: 'Then, coming to the city of his parents with Balarama to free them, he hurled the leader of the enemy hosts from the high seat and dragged him lifeless upon the earth.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 34)
stretching his own Parigha-like arms Krishna drew Kansa by the hair in the arena... When... Kansa breathed his last Krishna threw away his body.

springing up to the place where he was seated, laid hold of him by the hair of his head, and struck his tiara to the ground: then casting him down upon the earth, Govinda threw himself upon him. Crushed by the weight of the upholder of the universe... Kansa the king, gave up the ghost.

events.variant_notes: bpc1_038 is Uddhava's recollection.

events.working_title: Balarama Slays Kamsa's Brothers
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa's eight brothers rush at Krishna in fury and Balarama slays them all with his club.

sources.source_excerpt: Kamsa's eight brothers, Kanka and Nyagrodha and the rest, rushed at Krishna in fury, and Balarama slew them all with his club, like a lion among cattle. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 39-40)
Holding powerfully by his hands the proud brother of Kansa, by name Urgita, the virtuous-souled Baladeva killed him... Having thus slain Kansa... the lotus-eyed Krishna first touched Vasudeva's feet.

events.variant_notes: HV folds in the greeting of the parents.

events.working_title: Kamsa's Wives Lament and the Funeral Rites Are Performed
events.one_line_summary: The wives of the slain warriors weep, and Krishna comforts them and has the funeral rites performed.

sources.source_excerpt: The wives of the slain warriors wept and lamented their husbands, and Krishna comforted the royal women and had the customary funeral rites performed for the dead. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 41-48)
desirous of performing the obsequial rites of king Kansa according to the ritualastic laws they placed his body in a palanquin and took it to the northern bank of Yamuna... setting fire to the pyre.

events.working_title: Krishna Frees and Bows to Vasudeva and Devaki
events.one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama release their parents from bonds and bow, touching their feet.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna and Balarama released Vasudeva and Devaki from their bonds and bowed, touching their feet; and the parents, knowing their sons to be the lords of the world, embraced them without fear. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 49-50)
Krishńa, accompanied by Balabhadra, embraced the feet of Vasudeva and of Devakí... recalling to recollection what he had said to them at his birth, they bowed to Janárddana.

events.working_title: Krishna Begs His Parents' Forgiveness
events.one_line_summary: Krishna humbly begs Vasudeva and Devaki's forgiveness for having been unable to serve them.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, bowing to his parents, begged their forgiveness that he and Balarama, prevented by Kamsa, had not been able to serve them in their childhood, and could not repay the debt owed to parents. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

events.working_title: Krishna Installs Ugrasena as King
events.one_line_summary: Krishna makes his grandfather Ugrasena king of the Yadavas, honoring Yayati's curse.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna installed his maternal grandfather Ugrasena as king of the Yadavas, declaring that because of Yayati's curse no Yadava should sit on the throne, and that while he served, the gods themselves would pay tribute. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-13)
'I do not care for the kingdom or the royal throne... place yourself on the throne and acquire victory by becoming the king.'... Govinda, well read in laws, installed him on the throne.
The foe of Madhu then liberated Ugrasena from confinement, and placed him on the throne, which the death of his son had left vacant... performed the funeral rites of Kansa.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.21 also folds in the consolation of the widows.

events.working_title: Krishna Restores the Yadava Kinsmen
events.one_line_summary: Krishna brings back and settles all the Yadava kinsmen who had fled in fear of Kamsa.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna brought back all the Yadava, Vrishni, Andhaka and Madhu kinsmen who had fled in fear of Kamsa, settled them in their homes with wealth, and they rejoiced daily at the sight of his face. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-17)

events.working_title: Nanda Departs for Vraja
events.one_line_summary: Krishna embraces Nanda, bids him return to Vraja, and Nanda departs in tears with the cowherds.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna embraced Nanda, told him to return to Vraja, and promised to come and see his kinsfolk; and Nanda, his eyes full of tears, departed with the cowherds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 19-24)

events.working_title: Krishna and Balarama Study Under Sandipani
events.one_line_summary: The two brothers are initiated and go to the teacher Sandipani, mastering all arts in sixty-four days.

sources.source_excerpt: Vasudeva had Krishna and Balarama initiated by the brahmins, and the two, who know all knowledge, went as students to the teacher Sandipani in Avanti, and in sixty-four days mastered all the arts and sciences. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 25-35)

events.variant_notes: See 'sandipani_son' (VP 5.21 combines study + recovery).

events.working_title: Krishna Retrieves Sandipani's Son
events.one_line_summary: As teacher's fee, Krishna slays Panchajana, takes his conch, and brings Sandipani's dead son back from Yama's city.

sources.source_excerpt: As his teacher's fee, Sandipani asked for his son, who had been lost in the ocean at Prabhasa; Krishna slew the demon Panchajana, took his conch-shell body, and going to Yama's city, blew the conch and brought back the boy. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 36-46)

Uddhava said: 'Having studied the whole Veda once through from Sandipani, he granted his guru the boon of his dead son, bringing him back from the belly of Pancajana.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1)

The conch, which Janarddana obtained after slaying Panchajana, is known amongst gods and men as Panchajanya... having vanquished the fearful son of Vivaswan... obtained the child son of his preceptor.
having slain the vile Panchajana, he took the conch shell... The heroes also recovered the boy from the pains of death, and restored him in his former person to his father.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.21 folds in the study; bpc1_039 is Uddhava's recollection.

events.working_title: Krishna Obtains the Celestial Hall Sudharman
events.one_line_summary: Krishna bids Vayu ask Indra to resign the splendid hall Sudharman; Indra yields it, and the Yadava chiefs thenceforth possess the jewel-adorned celestial court.

sources.source_excerpt: Go, Váyu, to Indra, and desire him to lay aside his pomp, and resign to Ugrasena his splendid hall Sudharman... Indra... immediately gave up to him the hall Sudharman.

events.variant_notes: VARIANT of the Sudharman-hall motif: Vishnu Purana 5.21 tells the fetching of the celestial hall for Ugrasena at Mathura; Harivamsha 1.115 folds the same hall into the enrichment of Dwaraka. Different placement — kept separate.

events.working_title: Krishna Sends Uddhava to Vrindavan
events.one_line_summary: Krishna charges Uddhava with a message to console Nanda, Yashoda and the pining gopis.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna sent his beloved devotee Uddhava to Vrindavan with a message to console Nanda, Yashoda and the gopis, who were pining in his absence. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-6)

events.working_title: Uddhava Arrives in Vrindavan and Nanda Longs for Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava reaches Vrindavan at dusk, is honored by Nanda, who asks after Krishna and remembers his deeds.

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava arrived in Vrindavan at dusk, was embraced by Nanda and honored as Vasudeva himself, and Nanda, recounting Krishna's deeds, asked after his son; and Yashoda wept as she listened. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 7-28)

events.working_title: Uddhava Arrives Bearing Krishna's Message
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava arrives in Vrindavan as Krishna's envoy; the gopis, pining for Krishna, surround him and ask why he has come.

sources.source_excerpt: The astonished gopis surrounded him, asking 'Who is this of wondrous beauty, wearing Achyuta's dress and ornaments?' They recognized him as a messenger sent by Krishna for love of his parents. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-9)

events.working_title: The Gopi's Lament to the Bee (Bhramara-gita)
events.one_line_summary: A gopi, seeing a honeybee, addresses it as Krishna's messenger and reproaches Krishna for abandoning the gopis.

sources.source_excerpt: 'O bee, friend of the cheat, do not touch my feet... he who made us drink the nectar of his lips once now abandons us like flowers cast aside.' The gopis sing and weep, remembering Krishna's boyhood and youthful deeds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 10-20)

events.working_title: Uddhava Delivers Krishna's Message and the Gopis Reply
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava conveys Krishna's teaching of unbroken spiritual union; the gopis answer that they cannot forget Krishna.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna's message: 'My separation from you is never complete, as ether, air, fire, water and earth pervade all beings... fix your mind wholly on me and you will soon attain me.' The gopis reply that every river, hill and forest reminds them of Krishna and they cannot forget him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 21-51)

events.working_title: Uddhava Praises the Gopis and Departs
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava extols the gopis' supreme devotion, wishes to be a shrub in Vrindavan, stays some months, then returns to Mathura.

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava declared: 'May I become any shrub, creeper or herb in Vrindavan, blessed by the dust of these gopis' feet.' After consoling Nanda, Yashoda and the gopas, he departed and returned to Mathura. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 52-68)

events.working_title: Krishna Visits Trivakra and Grants Her a Boon
events.one_line_summary: Krishna visits the hunchback woman Trivakra, accepts her hospitality, and grants her a boon, honoring her devotion.

sources.source_excerpt: Knowing the desire of the love-tormented Sairandhri, the Lord went to her house; she arose, adorned herself, and approached him; Krishna granted her the boon she wished and returned to his own abode. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-10)

events.variant_notes: Later visit (10.48); see 'kubja_straighten' for the first meeting.

events.working_title: Krishna Sends Akrura to Hastinapura
events.one_line_summary: Krishna visits Akrura's home and dispatches him to Hastinapura to learn whether the Pandavas are treated justly.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna told Akrura: 'Go to Gajasahvaya (Hastinapura) and learn how the Pandavas, brought there with their mother after their father's death, are faring; the blind king follows his wicked son.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-35)

events.working_title: Kunti Confides Her Sorrow to Akrura
events.one_line_summary: In Hastinapura, Kunti tearfully tells Akrura of the Pandavas' persecution and prays to Krishna for protection.

sources.source_excerpt: Weeping, Kunti said: 'Krishna, Krishna, great yogin, soul of the universe, protect me who am sinking with my children; I see no refuge but your lotus feet.' Akrura and Vidura consoled her. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-14)

events.working_title: Akrura Counsels Dhritarashtra
events.one_line_summary: Akrura advises Dhritarashtra to treat the Pandavas as his own sons, then returns and reports to Krishna and Balarama.

sources.source_excerpt: Akrura told the king: 'Act with fairness toward the Pandavas and your own sons; no one dwells here forever.' Dhritarashtra admitted the truth but confessed his mind was unsteady from love for his sons; Akrura then returned and reported all to Krishna and Rama. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 15-30)

events.working_title: Jarasandha Attacks and Besieges Mathura
events.one_line_summary: Kamsa's widows report to Jarasandha, who vows to destroy the Yadavas and besieges Mathura with twenty-three armies.

sources.source_excerpt: Kamsa's widows Asti and Prapti went to their father Jarasandha and told him of their widowhood; enraged, he resolved to make the earth Yadava-free and besieged Mathura from all sides with twenty-three akshauhinis. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-5)
hearing of Kansa's death from his two daughters... the powerful Jarasandha, in no time, set out with his army... to slay all the Yadus.
'Let the armies of the kings united lay siege on all sides to this city.'
Eighteen times did the haughty prince of Magadhá renew his attack upon the Yádavas, headed by Krishńa; and was as often defeated and put to the rout by them, with very inferior numbers.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.22 folds in the routing of Jarasandha across eighteen attacks; HV splits the march (1.89) and the siege (1.90).

events.working_title: A Divine Chariot and Weapons Descend for Krishna
events.one_line_summary: As Krishna deliberates, a divine chariot and celestial weapons descend from the sky; Krishna and Balarama ride out to battle.

sources.source_excerpt: While Krishna reflected, two chariots with the splendor of the sun descended from the sky with drivers and ancient divine weapons; Krishna blew his conch and terror entered the enemy's hearts. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 6-15)

events.working_title: The Yadavas Rout Jarasandha's Army and Spare Him
events.one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama annihilate Jarasandha's host; Balarama seizes Jarasandha, but Krishna releases him to fight again.

sources.source_excerpt: Balarama seized the chariotless Jarasandha like a lion seizing a lion, but Krishna stayed the binding, saying 'The Magadha is not to be slain; he will gather forces again.' Seventeen times Jarasandha attacked and was routed. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 16-41)
Thus did the great heroes and soldiers, belonging to the army of Vrishnis, fight for twenty-seven days with the highly powerful sovereigns and soldiers of the king of Magadha's party.
'O Rama... this king of Magadha is not to be slain by thee... Jarasandha shall, in no time, meet with his death from the means that I have laid out for his destruction.'

events.variant_notes: HV splits the battle and the divine voice sparing Jarasandha.

events.working_title: The Yadavas Counsel That Mathura Cannot Withstand Siege
events.one_line_summary: The Yadavas tell Krishna that Mathura lacks walls and provisions and cannot withstand Jarasandha's repeated sieges.

sources.source_excerpt: 'This city has a limited supply of food and fuels. It is not protected by a fort... It will not therefore be able to stand attack for even one day.'

events.working_title: Krishna Resolves to Abandon Mathura
events.one_line_summary: Krishna decides to leave Mathura with Balarama and head south, to draw Jarasandha away and protect the city.

sources.source_excerpt: 'Therefore although I am capable, I shall, at this very moment, fly away with the worshipful Baladeva for saving my life like one incapable.'

events.working_title: Krishna Meets Parasurama, Who Counsels Gomanta
events.one_line_summary: On mount Sahya, Krishna meets the sage Parasurama, who counsels him to make his stand against Jarasandha on mount Gomanta.

sources.source_excerpt: 'Getting upon that high summit... if you obstruct Jarasandha by fighting with him in the fort you will be able to conquer him.'

events.working_title: Garuda Restores Vishnu's Stolen Crown to Krishna
events.one_line_summary: Garuda, having recovered Vishnu's crown stolen by Bali's son, places it on Krishna's head on Gomanta.

sources.source_excerpt: that foremost of birds threw from the welkin that crown on Vishnu's head... 'When I fell asleep in the ocean, Virochana's son... stole away my diadem... Garuda has brought this back.'

events.working_title: Krishna Wields the Divine Weapons on Gomanta
events.one_line_summary: On Gomanta, the divine weapons descend to Krishna and Balarama, who rout the kings; Balarama slays king Darada.

sources.source_excerpt: came down for the two Yadavas four powerful Vaishnava weapons namely, the plough-share Samvartaka, the mace Sounanda, the discus Sudarshana, and the club Koumodaki.

events.working_title: The King of Chedi Befriends Krishna and Escorts Him to Karavira
events.one_line_summary: After Jarasandha flees, the king of Chedi, Krishna's kinsman by marriage, befriends him and escorts him to the city of Karavira.

sources.source_excerpt: the highly effulgent king of Chedi, remembering his relationship with the Yadavas, approached Krishna... 'Let us go with our army and followers to the city of Karavira.'

events.working_title: Krishna Slays King Shrigala with the Discus
events.one_line_summary: King Shrigala of Karavira attacks Krishna, who slays him with the Sudarshana discus.

sources.source_excerpt: holding up his discus he hurled it at Shrigala's breast... Shrigala too, having his heart pierced by the discus... fell down, bleeding like a cleft mountain.

events.working_title: Krishna Installs Shakradeva on the Throne of Karavira
events.one_line_summary: At the plea of Shrigala's queen, Krishna installs the slain king's son Shakradeva on the throne of Karavira.

sources.source_excerpt: 'this son of Shrigala is just like mine. I declare safety unto them and gladly annoint him as the king.'... Placing the prince on the throne the powerful Janarddana sprinkled him with celestial water.

events.working_title: Krishna Returns to Mathura
events.one_line_summary: Rama and Krishna, accompanied by Damaghosha, enter Mathura and are received with joy by Ugrasena and the Yadavas before honoring their parents.

sources.source_excerpt: Thereupon seated on a car drawn by beautiful horses Rāma and Keshava entered the city of Mathurā in an auspicious moment. ... they entered into the house of their sire Vasudeva. ... bowing unto the feet of Vasudeva they showed proper honor to king Ugrasena and other leading Yadavas.

events.working_title: News of Rukmini's Swayamvara
events.one_line_summary: Spies inform Krishna that Rukmini, sister of Rukmi, will hold her swayamvara at Kundina; Krishna sets out with the Yadava army, bidding Ugrasena guard Mathura.

sources.source_excerpt: the emissaries announced ... 'Rukshmini, the first sister of Rukshmi, will hold her Swayamvara.' ... Keshava, the foremost of Yadus, set out immediately with his army.

events.working_title: Krishna Summons Garuda at Bhishmaka's House
events.one_line_summary: Arriving at Bhishmaka's house for the swayamvara, Krishna thinks of Garuda to overawe the assembled kings, and the bird-king appears, shaking the earth with his wings.

sources.source_excerpt: in order to terrify the kings and display his own prowess he thought of the highly powerful son of Vinatā ... As soon as he was thought of Vinatā's son, assuming a form that could be seen easily, approached Keshava.

events.working_title: Jarasandha Warns the Assembled Kings
events.one_line_summary: At Bhishmaka's council Jarasandha warns the assembled kings that Krishna is Vishnu himself, whose arrival for the maiden spells calamity; Sunitha concurs.

sources.source_excerpt: This Krishna ... has come here for the maiden and forsooth he will set forth mighty exertions for acquiring her. ... Forsooth I tell you that Vishnu himself has come for this Swayamvara.

events.working_title: The Kings Debate and Bhishmaka Yields
events.one_line_summary: Dantavakra urges peace with Krishna while Salwa scorns fear; Bhishmaka, fearing for his arrogant son Rukmi, resolves to go and propitiate Krishna.

sources.source_excerpt: Dantavakra said: ... 'let us go and offer the high-souled Keshava hospitality ... if we make peace with Keshava we shall be able to live freed from anxiety and fear.' ... Bhismaka felt a desire to go to eternal Krishna for propitiating him.

events.working_title: Kaishika Offers His Kingdom
events.one_line_summary: The Vidarbha kings Kratha and Kaishika offer Krishna their kingdom and arrange his consecration, while a celestial voice announces that Indra has sent a golden seat.

sources.source_excerpt: the two heroic and noble kings of Vidarbha, said: 'Blessed is our birth and fame to-day ... We now install thee in our kingdom.' ... 'For him the king of gods has sent this white seat of gold ... Do thou along with other kings place him on this seat and sprinkle him.'

events.working_title: Krishna's Royal Consecration
events.one_line_summary: Before the assembled kings, celestial jars pour sacred water and Indra himself adorns Krishna, completing the Abhisheka ceremony of his imperial consecration.

sources.source_excerpt: from the sky, celestial jars ... began to pour down, like clouds, water mixed with gold, gems, flowers and scented powders on the occasion of the ceremony of his royal unction. ... Having performed duly according to rites, the Abhisheka ceremony of Janārddana, before the very presence of the kings.

events.working_title: Krishna Reveals Rukmini Is Lakshmi
events.one_line_summary: In dialogue with Bhishmaka, Krishna declares that Rukmini is the goddess Lakshmi born to be his wife and should not be given away in a public swayamvara.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna said: ... 'truly your daughter Rukshmini is not a woman; she is the very goddess Sree. For some object and at the words of Brahmā she is born (as a woman). She should not be given away in a Swayamvara where all the kings will be assembled.'

events.working_title: Bhishmaka Beholds Krishna's Cosmic Form
events.one_line_summary: Krishna takes leave of Bhishmaka, who beholds his universal form of a thousand heads and arms and worships him with a eulogy before the kings follow him out.

sources.source_excerpt: beholding the prime and self-sprung Krishna, having eyes like red lotuses, thousand feet, thousand eyes, thousand arms ... the king Bhishmaka bowed unto him and began to eulogise his glories.

events.working_title: Shalya Proposes Inviting Kalayavana
events.one_line_summary: Shalya tells the kings that Kalayavana, whom no prince of Mathura can slay by Rudra's boon, should be invited against Krishna; Jarasandha dispatches Shalya as envoy.

sources.source_excerpt: Shalya said: ... 'Kālayavana is incapable of being slain by Keshava. ... send an emissary to the capital of the king of Yavanas.' ... 'This effulgent king of Soubha ... let him proceed to the capital of Yavana.'

events.working_title: Rukmini Declares She Weds Only Krishna
events.one_line_summary: After the kings disperse, Rukmini tells her friends that she will accept no husband but the lotus-eyed Krishna.

sources.source_excerpt: the chaste and wise Rukshmini approached her friends and with her face bent down in shame said:—'I tell you truly, I do not wish to be the spouse of any body else save Krishna having lotus eyes.'

events.working_title: Shalya Delivers Jarasandha's Message to Kalayavana
events.one_line_summary: Shalya arrives at Kalayavana's court, recounts the destruction at Gomanta and Jarasandha's plea, and urges Kalayavana to march on Mathura.

sources.source_excerpt: Shalya said:—O king of Yavanas, hear I shall describe at length what the king of Magadha has deputed me to communicate to you. ... 'enter the city of Mathurā with your army establish your glory there.'

events.working_title: Kalayavana Marches on Mathura
events.one_line_summary: Kalayavana, elated by the kings' request, honors Shalya and sets out that very day with his army to vanquish Krishna.

sources.source_excerpt: Kalayavana said: ... 'in this auspicious moment I shall even to-day start for Mathurā for defeating Keshava in the battle-field.' ... he set out with his army for vanquishing Janārddana.

Śyála having called Gárgya the Brahman... impotent, in an assembly of the Yádavas... he engaged in arduous penance to obtain a son, who should be a terror to the tribe of Yadu... Kálayavana assembled many myriads of Mlechchhas... advanced impatiently against Mathurá.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.23 gives Gargya's penance as Kalayavana's origin; HV has Shalya invite him.

events.working_title: Ugrasena Welcomes Krishna Back
events.one_line_summary: Krishna returns to Mathura, where Ugrasena comes out to honor him; Krishna declines the royal arghya and reaffirms Ugrasena as king, then consoles him over Kamsa's death.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna ... said:—'O king of Mathurā, while I have installed you, declaring, Be you the lord of Mathura, it does not behove me to make it otherwise. ... get upon your white car ... govern the city of Mathurā, delightedly with your sons and grand-sons.'

events.working_title: Garuda Reports the Site of Dwaraka
events.one_line_summary: Garuda returns from reconnoitering Kushasthali and praises it as a fitting abode; Krishna, knowing Jarasandha unslayable, resolves to leave Mathura.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna ... said:—'O Vinatā's son, the king Jarāsandha is unslayable by us. ... it never bodes good for us to live in this city of Mathura.' ... Garuda said: ... 'thy city will be celebrated in the three worlds under the name of Dwāravati.'

events.working_title: The Serpent-Jar Stratagem Against Kalayavana
events.one_line_summary: As Kalayavana advances, Krishna sends him a sealed jar holding a black serpent as a warning; Kalayavana answers by filling the jar with ants that devour it.

sources.source_excerpt: Keshava sent an envoy to the king of Yavanas. In order to terrorize him ... put a highly dreadful black serpent ... into a jar and sealed it up. ... understanding that the Yadavas had sent it to terrorize him Kalayavana filled that jar with dreadful ants.

events.working_title: Uddhava Recalls Krishna's Birth and Removal to Vraja
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls that Krishna was born of Vasudeva and Devaki in Bhoja's prison to relieve the earth's burden, and was carried by his father, fearing Kamsa, to Nanda's Vraja, where he lived hidden for eleven years with Balarama.

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava said: 'Born of Vasudeva and Devaki in the prison of the Bhoja king, the Lord, prayed to by the earth, came to relieve her. Then, carried by his father in fear of Kamsa, he dwelt in Nanda's Vraja for eleven years with Balarama, his glory concealed.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-25)

events.variant_notes: Compressed recollection spanning the birth and exchange (see 'birth','exchange').

events.working_title: Uddhava Recalls Krishna's Cowherd Childhood and Kamsa's Demons
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls Krishna's childhood in Vraja — herding calves and cows with the cowherd boys on the Yamuna, playing the flute — and how he playfully defeated the shape-shifting demons Kamsa sent against him.

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava said: 'Surrounded by the calves, he herded them and sported in the Yamuna's groves, showing the cowherds his enchanting childhood play, weeping and laughing with a lion-cub's glance; playing the flute, he delighted the cowherds — and the shape-shifting demons sent by the Bhoja king he dispelled in sport, like toys.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-29)

events.variant_notes: General recollection; see specific demon episodes.

events.working_title: Nanda Brings the Infants Home to Gokula
events.one_line_summary: Set at liberty, Vasudeva bids Nanda take both Krishna and Balarama to Gokula to be reared as his own sons; Nanda and the cowherds return with their waggons.

sources.source_excerpt: let this boy, the son whom Rohińí has borne me, accompany you, and be brought up by you as this your own son. Accordingly Nanda and the other cowherds... returned to their village.

events.working_title: Krishna Carries Off Rukmini
events.one_line_summary: Krishna seizes Rukmini as she leaves the temple, places her on his chariot, and rides off before the assembled kings.

sources.source_excerpt: As Rukmini, having worshipped, came out of the temple and was about to mount her chariot, Krishna seized her and placed her on his own chariot, and went away slowly, breaking through the circle of kings like a lion carrying off his share from the midst of jackals. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 52-56)

Hari contrived, on the eve of the nuptials, to carry off the princess, leaving Ráma and his kinsmen to sustain the weight of his enemies... Pauńd́raka... Śiśupála, Jarásandha... exerted themselves to kill Krishńa, but were repelled by Balaráma.

events.variant_notes: BP 10.53 seizes her at the svayamvara after her temple prayer; VP 5.26 carries her off on the eve of her betrothal to Sisupala.

events.working_title: Krishna Defeats and Spares Rukmi
events.one_line_summary: Krishna's forces rout the pursuing kings; Rukmi chases alone, and Krishna defeats and disfigures him but spares his life at Rukmini's entreaty.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna's host routed the pursuing kings; Rukmi, vowing not to re-enter Kundina without slaying Krishna, overtook him alone; Krishna cut down every weapon Rukmi raised, and as he was about to slay him, Rukmini fell at his feet and begged for her brother's life, so Krishna only shaved and disfigured him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-35)

Hearing that his sister had been carried away by Krishna Rukshmi, filled with anger, promised ... 'I shall not return to the city of Kundina without slaying Krishna and bringing back Rukshmini.' ... Beholding her brother lying down motionless on earth, Rukshmini, for his life, fell at Vishnu's feet.
Krishńa destroyed with his discus... the host of Rukmin... and would have put him to death, but was withheld by the entreaties of Rukminí... 'He is my only brother... give me my brother in charity.'

events.variant_notes: Harivamsha 1.116 has Rukmi vow to slay Krishna then duel near the Narmada; VP/BP have him pursue and be spared at Rukmini's plea.

events.working_title: Krishna Marries Rukmini
events.one_line_summary: Rukmi founds the city of Bhojakata, and Krishna formally weds Rukmini in Dvaraka amid citywide celebration.

sources.source_excerpt: The disgraced Rukmi built the city of Bhojakata, vowing not to return to Kundina; Krishna brought Rukmini to Dvaraka and wed her with full rites, and there was a great festival in every house of the Yadu city. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 35-59)

When Rāma, with the Vrishni army, arrived at Dwārakā the powerful Keshavā duly espoused Rukshmini. ... The powerful Mādhava begat on her ten sons—all mighty car-warriors, namely the highly powerful Pradyumna ...
After the defeat of Rukmin, Krishńa married Rukminí in due form, having first made her his own by the Rákshasa ritual. She bore him the gallant Pradyumna, a portion of the deity of love.

events.variant_notes: VP 5.26 bundles Pradyumna's birth with the marriage; Harivamsha notes Rukmini as first wife and mother of ten sons.

events.working_title: Shambara Steals the Infant Pradyumna
events.one_line_summary: Pradyumna, Kama reborn as Krishna's son, is abducted as a newborn by the asura Shambara and thrown into the sea.

sources.source_excerpt: Pradyumna was born to Rukmini of Krishna's potency; knowing him as his destined enemy, the shape-shifting Shambara stole the newborn and threw him into the ocean. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-2)

On the seventh day at dead of night Kalashamvara stole away that infant son of Krishna from the lying-in room... His beautiful and accomplished wife Māyāvati... gave over that son of Vasudeva to her like his own

When Pradyumna was but six days old, he was stolen from the lying-in chamber by Sambara, terrible as death; for the demon foreknew that Pradyumna, if he lived, would be his destroyer... cast him into the ocean.

events.variant_notes: Age at abduction varies: six days (VP), seventh night (Harivamsha); BP just 'newborn'. All cast him into the sea.

events.working_title: Pradyumna Slays Shambara
events.one_line_summary: Armed with the great science of countering illusion, Pradyumna challenges and beheads the demon Shambara.

sources.source_excerpt: Mayavati gave Pradyumna the Maha-vidya that destroys all illusion; Pradyumna challenged Shambara, countered his hundred forms of maya, and with his sharp sword cut off the demon's head. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 15-23)

Seven times he foiled the delusions of the enchanter, and making himself master of the eighth, turned it against Sambara, and killed him... he proceeded to his father's house, where he alighted, along with Máyávatí, in the inner apartments.

events.variant_notes: BP: 'great science of countering illusion'; VP: slays the enchanter with his own eighth illusion.
events.notes: Harivamsha expands the duel into many beats (hv_b2_043-047). | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: Pradyumna Returns to Dvaraka and Is Recognized
events.one_line_summary: Pradyumna returns to Dvaraka with Mayavati; Rukmini recognizes her long-lost son, and the city rejoices.

sources.source_excerpt: Pradyumna entered the inner apartments with his wife; Rukmini, sensing her lost son, wondered at his resemblance to Krishna, and when Narada told the whole tale, Rukmini, Devaki and Vasudeva embraced the couple in joy, and Dvaraka celebrated him as one returned from the dead. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-39)

Pradyumna... rose up into the welkin and reached the charming city of Dwāravati... Rukshmini... said:—"Blessed is that woman whose son is such a beautiful... boy resembling Kāma"... Krishna... said:—"...here is your son the great bow-man. He has killed Shamvara... Know her as Rati, the beloved consort of Kāma"

events.variant_notes: Harivamsha has Rukmini recognize him by a dream and Vrishni marks; BP has her recognize her long-lost son.

events.working_title: Surya Grants Satrajit the Syamantaka Jewel
events.one_line_summary: Surya gives his devotee Satrajit the Syamantaka jewel, which yields eight loads of gold daily and makes him shine like the sun.

sources.source_excerpt: Pleased with his devotee Satrajit, Surya gave him the Syamantaka jewel; wearing it, Satrajit shone like the sun, so the people of Dvaraka mistook him for the sun-god; the jewel yielded eight loads of gold daily and warded off all calamity. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-10)
Thereupon the lord took out from his neck the peerless jewel Swyamantaka and gave it to him. Thereupon Bhaskara gave him the jewel Swyamantaka.

events.variant_notes: BP: jewel yields eight loads of gold daily; Harivamsha: Satrajit worships the sun on the ocean bank.

events.working_title: Prasena Is Slain by a Lion for the Jewel
events.one_line_summary: Satrajit refuses to hand the jewel to Krishna; his brother Prasena, wearing it on a hunt, is killed by a lion, and rumor blames Krishna.

sources.source_excerpt: Though Krishna asked for the jewel, the covetous Satrajit refused; his brother Prasena, wearing it on a hunt, was slain by a lion, which was in turn slain by Jambavan, and the people whispered that Krishna had killed Prasena for the jewel. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-15)

Once on a time adorned with that jewel Prasena went out a-hunting. He was, for that Swyamantaka, slain by a wild lion. Killing that flying lion a highly powerful bear took that jewel and entered into his den.

events.variant_notes: BP 10.56 bundles Satrajit's refusal and the rumor blaming Krishna into the same beat; Harivamsha adds Jambavan killing the lion and taking the jewel.

events.working_title: Krishna Wrestles Jambavan for the Jewel
events.one_line_summary: To clear his name, Krishna traces Prasena's path, enters Jambavan's cave, and fights the bear-king for twenty-eight days before Jambavan yields the jewel and his daughter.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, tracing Prasena's trail, entered the bear's dark cave and fought Jambavan day and night for twenty-eight days with fists like thunderbolts; Jambavan, exhausted, recognized him as Vishnu, the ancient Lord, and gave him the jewel along with his daughter Jambavati. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 16-31)

Govinda wrestled with Jamvavan in that den for twenty-one days... Having vanquished the highly powerful Jamvavan he married the most beloved daughter of the king of bears by name Jamvavati and took away the jewel for clearing himself.

events.variant_notes: Duration varies: twenty-eight days (BP) vs twenty-one days (Harivamsha).

events.working_title: Krishna Returns the Jewel and Clears His Name
events.one_line_summary: Krishna returns with the jewel and Jambavati, clears his name in open assembly, and returns the Syamantaka to Satrajit, who also offers Satyabhama.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna returned with the jewel and his bride, recounted all in the assembly, and restored the Syamantaka to Satrajit; ashamed, Satrajit gave Krishna his daughter Satyabhama along with the jewel, but Krishna accepted only the bride and returned the jewel to its owner. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 32-44)
Having thus brought the jewel and cleared himself of the charge he handed over Swyamantaka to Satrajit in an assembly of the Satwatas.

events.variant_notes: BP has him clear his name in open assembly and also receive Satyabhama.

events.working_title: Satadhanva Murders Satrajit for the Jewel
events.one_line_summary: Instigated by Akrura and Kritavarma, Satadhanva murders the sleeping Satrajit and steals the Syamantaka jewel.

sources.source_excerpt: While Krishna was away, Akrura and Kritavarma urged Satadhanva to seize the jewel, saying Satrajit had broken his word; the wicked Satadhanva slew the sleeping Satrajit and made off with the Syamantaka. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-5)
Thereupon, having slain Satrajit at the dead of night the highly powerful Shatadhanwa took away the jewel and made a present of it to Akrura.

events.variant_notes: Harivamsha adds that Shatadhanwa secretly gives the jewel to Akrura; BP notes instigation by Akrura and Kritavarma.

events.working_title: Krishna Pursues and Slays Satadhanva
events.one_line_summary: Krishna pursues and beheads Satadhanva near Mithila but finds no jewel; Balarama goes on to visit King Janaka.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna and Rama pursued Satadhanva, who fled a hundred yojanas on horseback; Krishna beheaded him with his discus, but searching him found no jewel; Balarama then went on to Mithila to visit Janaka, where he stayed some months and taught Duryodhana the mace. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-25)
going on foot, Achyuta (Krishna), highly skilled in the use of arms, killed Shatadhanwa on the way to Mithila... he did not see Swyamantaka.

events.variant_notes: Both: killed near Mithila, no jewel found.
events.notes: Balarama's separate departure to Mithila is a distinct beat (hv_a_009).

events.working_title: Krishna Reclaims the Jewel from Akrura
events.one_line_summary: Krishna reveals that Satadhanva had left the jewel with Akrura; Akrura produces it, and Krishna returns it to him after showing it to his kinsmen.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, who knew all, told Akrura the jewel had been entrusted to him; Akrura produced the Syamantaka, and Krishna showed it to his kinsmen to wipe away the stain of suspicion, then returned the jewel to Akrura. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-40)

Thereupon at the words of Krishna the high-minded Akrura, without experiencing the least pain, gave him the jewel in the midst of the assembled Satwatas... Hari, the repressor of enemies, returned it to him with a delighted heart.

events.variant_notes: Both have Krishna discern the jewel is with Akrura and return it to him after showing it in assembly.

events.working_title: Indra Reports Naraka's Tyranny and Asks Krishna's Help
events.one_line_summary: Indra descends to Dwaraka, recounts how the demon Naraka stole Aditi's ear-rings, and asks Krishna to slay him; Krishna departs with Satyabhama on Garuda.

sources.source_excerpt: Indra ... said: 'Elated with the boon conferred on him by Brahmā the great Asura Naraka has foolishly stolen the ear-rings of Aditi. ... Do thou therefore kill that sinful wretch.' ... he, along with Satyabhāmā, sat on Garuda's back and immediately started with Sakra.

The son of the earth, called Naraka, who rules over the city of Prágjyotisha, inflicts a great injury upon all creatures... He has taken away the umbrella of Varuńa... and the celestial nectar-dropping earrings of my mother Adití.

events.variant_notes: VP lists Naraka's thefts (maidens, Varuna's umbrella, Aditi's earrings, demands Indra's elephant); Harivamsha has Indra descend and Krishna depart with Satyabhama on Garuda.

events.working_title: Krishna Slays Narakasura
events.one_line_summary: Krishna beheads the demon king Narakasura (Bhauma) with his discus, freeing the three worlds of his tyranny.

sources.source_excerpt: As Narakasura raised his spear, Krishna cut off his head with the sharp-edged discus, and it fell to earth decked with earrings and crown, while the sages and gods showered flowers in praise. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-22)
Fighting with Naraka for a moment the dreadful Janārddana cut him into two pieces with his effulgent discus. ... Beholding his son slain, Bhumi came with the pair of Kundalas to Govinda.
when Naraka came into the field... the wielder of the discus... cut him in two with his celestial missile... In the apartments of the women he found sixteen thousand and one hundred damsels.

events.variant_notes: Method: discus behead (BP), cut in two with discus (Harivamsha), cut nooses then slay (VP).
events.notes: Harivamsha bundles the slaying of Mura/generals; VP bundles freeing the captive princesses.

events.working_title: Krishna Frees the Sixteen Thousand Captive Maidens
events.one_line_summary: Krishna enters Narakasura's palace and frees the 16,100 captive princesses, who all choose him as their husband.

sources.source_excerpt: In Narakasura's palace Krishna saw the 16,100 royal princesses the demon had seized; seeing him, they all mentally chose him as their husband, and Krishna sent them to Dvaraka with vast treasures and sixty-four white elephants. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 31-36)

Having arrived at the Treasury of Naraka, Janārdana saw there, diamonds, pearls, corals, sapphires, emeralds ... Taking himself the Varuni umbrella capable of showering gold, he rode Garuda ... Having thus welcome[d] those lotus eyed damsels ... took them all to Dwāraka.

events.variant_notes: Both: sixteen thousand maidens choose Krishna as husband.

events.working_title: Krishna Marries the Sixteen Thousand Princesses
events.one_line_summary: Krishna, expanding into as many forms, simultaneously weds the 16,100 princesses, giving each a palace and household.

sources.source_excerpt: In a single moment Krishna, assuming as many forms, wed all the princesses, each in her own palace, living with them as a householder would, though none but the Lord could perform such a feat. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 41-44)

at an auspicious season he espoused all the maidens whom Naraka had carried off... Sixteen thousand and one hundred was the number of the maidens, and into so many different forms did the foe of Madhu multiply himself.

events.variant_notes: Both: Krishna multiplies into 16,100 forms so each wife believes him hers alone.

events.working_title: Krishna Uproots the Parijata Tree from Indra's Heaven
events.one_line_summary: Krishna returns Aditi's earrings to the gods, and at Satyabhama's wish uproots the Parijata tree from Indra's heaven, defeating the gods.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna returned the earrings to Aditi and was worshipped by Indra; urged by Satyabhama, he uprooted the Parijata tree, overcame Indra and the gods, and brought it to Dvaraka, planting it in Satyabhama's garden. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 37-40)

Uddhava said: 'Wishing, like a common man, to please his beloved, the Lord went for the celestial tree; the thunderbolt-wielder, blind with rage, rushed at him with his host, as if he were a plaything of the women.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 4)

Giving to the king of gods the pair of ear-rings belonging to Aditi and saluting him ... Aditi was pleased and took up her two sons on her lap. ... Krishna of unlimited powers, forcibly up-rooted it [the Pārijata] and placed it on Garuda's head.
the illustrious Adhokshaja saw hosts of celestial warriors... That refuge of the pious, the mighty Krishna uprooted the Pārijāta tree and placed it on the back of Garuda even before their eyes
Hari smiled upon her, and taking the Párijáta plant, put it upon Garud́a... 'This Párijáta tree belongs to Śachí... it is not proper, Govinda, for you to remove it.'

events.variant_notes: BP 10.59 and Harivamsha 1.121 bundle the restoration of Aditi's earrings with the uprooting; bpc1_041 is Uddhava's recall.
events.notes: VP splits earrings-restoration (vp5_030_01) from the uprooting (vp5_030_02).

events.working_title: Indra and the Gods Contend with Krishna over the Parijata
events.one_line_summary: The garden-keepers alert Indra, who rides out on Airavata and demands Krishna return the Parijata, challenging him to battle for it.

sources.source_excerpt: Sakra replied saying,—"O lotus-eyed one, thou shouldst not take away this tree, O infallible one, without challenging me to fight"
Indra launched his bolt, but in vain, for Hari caught and arrested it... 'I am not ashamed of being vanquished by him who is the author of the creation, preservation, and destruction of the world.'

events.variant_notes: VP: Krishna disarms all the gods with his discus and spares Indra; Harivamsha: Indra rides Airavata and challenges Krishna to battle.
events.notes: Harivamsha expands the battle (hv_b2_003-008); BP folds 'defeating the gods' into its uprooting beat.

events.working_title: Krishna Brings the Parijata to Satyabhama in Dvaraka
events.one_line_summary: Aditi grants Krishna the Parijata for Satyabhama's rite on condition of its return; Krishna plants it at Raivataka and carries it into Dwarka, where Satyabhama receives it joyfully.

sources.source_excerpt: Aditi... said to Hari:—"O Upendra! take this Pārijāta, go to Dwarkā and perform the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife... you are to bring back this tree"... taking that best of trees Pārijāta he entered into Satyabhāmā's palace

Then alighting from Garud́a, he proceeded with Satyabhámá to her garden, and there planted the great Párijáta tree, the smell of which perfumed the earth for three furlongs, and an approach to which enabled every one to recollect the events of a prior existence.

events.variant_notes: Harivamsha: Aditi grants it on condition of return; VP: planted in Satyabhama's garden.

events.working_title: Balarama Slays the Ape Dvivida
events.one_line_summary: The ape Dvivida insults Balarama and his women; Balarama fells him with his mace, freeing the land of the menace.

sources.source_excerpt: Dvivida, seeing Balarama sporting on Raivataka, mocked him and his women; Balarama, enraged, struck him with his mace, and the ape, after hurling trees and rocks in vain, was felled, vomiting blood, as gods rained flowers. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-27)

the monkey Dwivida came there, and stealing the ploughshare and the club of Baladeva, grinned at and mocked him... Bala replied with a blow of his fist upon the forehead of Dwivida, which felled him, vomiting blood, and lifeless, to the earth.

events.variant_notes: BP: Balarama fells him with his mace; VP: a single blow of the fist.
events.notes: The preceding ravages (bp10c_068) are a distinct beat. | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: Samba Carries Off Duryodhana's Daughter
events.one_line_summary: Samba carries off Lakshmana, Duryodhana's daughter, from her svayamvara; the Kauravas fight him and take him captive.

sources.source_excerpt: Samba, son of Jambavati, carried off Lakshmana, daughter of Duryodhana, from her svayamvara; Karna, Shala, Bhuri and Duryodhana fought him, and though Samba wounded them all, they surrounded and captured him with great effort. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-12)

At the choice of a husband by the daughter of Duryodhana, the princess was carried off by the hero Śámba, the son of Jámbavatí. Being pursued by Duryodhana, Karńa, Bhíshma, Drońa... he was defeated, and taken prisoner.

events.variant_notes: Both: Samba abducts her at the svayamvara and is captured by the Kuru chiefs.

events.working_title: Balarama Drags Hastinapura with His Plough
events.one_line_summary: Enraged, Balarama seizes his plough and drags the city of Hastinapura toward the Ganga; the terrified Kauravas surrender Samba and Lakshmana.

sources.source_excerpt: Balarama, declaring he would make the earth free of Kauravas, dug his plough into Hastinapura and dragged it toward the Ganga; the Kauravas, terrified, surrendered Samba and Lakshmana, and Duryodhana gave rich gifts as the city was released. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 39-53)

Hearing of his confinement the highly powerful Rāma went to that city for releasing him ... taking up his invincible ... weapon, plough-share ... and fixing it on the wall of the city he thought of, throwing that city of the Kauravas into the Ganges. Beholding his city thus whirled the king Duryodhana sent Shamva with his wife to the highly powerful Rāma.

the wielder of the club, Baladeva, his eyes red with rage, plunged the blade of his ploughshare downwards, beneath the ramparts of the city, and drew them towards him... the Kauravas delivered Śámba and his bride to the mighty Balaráma.

events.variant_notes: All: Balarama hooks his plough under the city and threatens to fling it into the Ganga; the Kauravas yield Samba and the bride.

events.working_title: Shalva's Illusion of Vasudeva's Death
events.one_line_summary: Shalva conjures the illusion that his men have captured and beheaded Vasudeva before Krishna's eyes; Krishna, briefly appearing grief-stricken, then sees through the sorcery.

sources.source_excerpt: A man appears weeping and tells Krishna that Shalva has carried off his father Vasudeva like an animal, and Shalva then seems to behead Vasudeva before Krishna, taunting him to save him if he can. Krishna, adopting a human mood, appears bewildered for a moment, then perceives it to be the demon's sorcery wrought by Maya, and seeing neither messenger nor his father's body, prepares to destroy the enemy. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 19-31)

And now I saw, O great monarch, Vasudeva himself falling from the car of precious metals! And, O warrior I swooned away ... Then the bow Sharanga dropped from my hand, and, O son of Kunti I swooned away! ... Then I concluded in my mind that it was certainly illusion.

events.variant_notes: BP: Krishna briefly appears grief-stricken then sees through the sorcery; MB: Krishna swoons and drops the Sharnga bow.

events.working_title: Krishna Destroys the Flying City Saubha and Slays Shalva
events.one_line_summary: Krishna cuts off Shalva's arm, shatters the flying city Saubha with his mace, and beheads Shalva with the discus as he attacks on foot.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna pierces the rushing Shalva with arrows, cuts through his armor, bow and crest-jewel, and crushes the city Saubha to pieces with his mace, so that it falls into the water in a thousand fragments. Then, as Shalva charges on foot with his mace, Krishna severs his arm and, wielding his wondrous discus blazing like the sun at world's end, cuts off his crowned head. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 32-35)

And approaching the town of Saubha whose splendour had disappeared, the discus went right through it, even as a saw divideth a tall tree. And cut in twain by the energy of the Sudarsana it fell like the city of Tripura shaken by the shafts of Maheswara.

And taking it up I once more hurled it with force saying, 'Go thou unto Salwa.' The discus then cleft Salwa in twain who in that fierce conflict was at the point of hurling a heavy mace. And with its energy it set the foe ablaze.

events.variant_notes: MB splits it: discus cuts Saubha in twain (mb_a2_027), then cleaves Salwa (mb_a2_028); BP bundles both (mace shatters Saubha, discus beheads Shalva).

events.working_title: Krishna and Arjuna Journey to Recover the Brahmana's Sons
events.one_line_summary: Krishna, to save the despairing Arjuna, mounts his divine chariot and carries him beyond the darkness to Vaikuntha, where they behold the Supreme Lord upon the serpent Ananta.

sources.source_excerpt: Restraining Arjuna from entering the fire, Krishna mounts his divine chariot and drives westward across the seven continents and seas, beyond the mountain Lokaloka into the great darkness, where he sends his blazing discus to cleave the gloom. Passing through, they behold the Supreme Lord, radiant like a mountain of light, reclining upon the thousand-headed serpent Ananta, and both Krishna and Arjuna bow to him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 41-56)

the ocean again said to Janārddana:—"...I will dry up the path in which your car... will proceed"... we proceeded through that lustrous red water as if we were on land... the mountains... said:—"What are we to do?"... "You are to give me passage"

events.variant_notes: BP: divine chariot beyond the darkness to Vaikuntha; Harivamsha: across the ocean and the seven cosmic mountains.

events.working_title: The Brahmana's Sons Are Restored
events.one_line_summary: The Supreme Lord tells Krishna and Arjuna that he himself had taken the brahmana's sons to bring them together, and returns the children, whom they restore to the brahmana.

sources.source_excerpt: The Supreme Lord tells Krishna and Arjuna that he, wishing to see them, had himself brought the brahmana's sons to his abode, and that having slain the earth's burden they should now return. Taking the children, Krishna and Arjuna return by the way they came and restore the sons to the brahmana, and Arjuna, astounded at the vision of Vishnu's abode, regards all human power as Krishna's grace. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 57-61)

Rishikesha entered into that bundle of effulgence... Within a moment the powerful Krishna returned with the four sons of the Brāhmana and gave those three boys... and the new born baby into the hands of the Brāhmana

events.variant_notes: BP: the Supreme Lord returns the children; Harivamsha: three stolen boys and the new-born infant restored.

events.working_title: Usha Dreams of Aniruddha
events.one_line_summary: Bana's daughter Usha dreams of a beloved youth, and her friend Chitralekha paints the princes to identify him as Aniruddha.

sources.source_excerpt: Usha dreamt of a dark, lotus-eyed youth and woke crying 'where is my beloved?'; her friend Chitralekha, skilled in art, painted the gods and princes, and Usha shyly recognized Aniruddha, Krishna's grandson. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-21)

on that lunar day a youth appeared to Ushá in a dream, of whose person she became enamoured... the moment she beheld the picture of his son, the object of her passion, her eyes wide expanded... 'This is he! this is he!'

events.variant_notes: Both: Usha dreams of the youth and Chitralekha paints the princes until she recognizes Aniruddha.

events.working_title: Aniruddha Is Brought to Usha and They Unite
events.one_line_summary: Chitralekha, by her mystic power, carries the sleeping Aniruddha to Shonitapura, where he lives secretly with Usha.

sources.source_excerpt: Chitralekha flew to Dvaraka and by her yogic power brought the sleeping Aniruddha to Shonitapura; Usha, overjoyed, enjoyed his company in the guarded inner palace, and the days passed unperceived. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 21-25)

Chitralekha... invisibly arrived where Ushā was, and she then brought and showed to Ushā the heroic Aniruddha... united in nuptials according to Gandharva rites they spent the day like a pair of Chakravākas

events.variant_notes: BP: Chitralekha carries the sleeping Aniruddha to Shonitapura; Harivamsha: they are united in secret Gandharva marriage.

events.working_title: Bana Captures and Binds Aniruddha
events.one_line_summary: Bana's guards discover the secret union; Bana finds Aniruddha with Usha and binds him with serpent-nooses.

sources.source_excerpt: The guards reported Usha's defilement; Bana, enraged, rushed to the women's quarters and found Aniruddha playing dice with his daughter, and the furious demon bound him with serpent-nooses, while Usha wept in grief. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-34)

Pradyumna's son was fettered with serpentine shafts. His body was chained with various serpents... Kumbhānda said... "He does not deserve to be slain"... handing over Aniruddha to the guards... Vāna... repaired to his own palace

The guards of the inner apartments discovering him there with Ushá, reported it to the king... Báňa... followed the counsel of his minister, and brought his magical faculties into the conflict, by which he succeeded in capturing the Yadu prince, and binding him in serpent bonds.

events.variant_notes: BP and VP: bound with serpent-nooses; Harivamsha: fettered with serpentine shafts via Tamasika illusion.
events.notes: Aniruddha's rout of Vana's soldiers (hv_b2_057) and Durga's later release (hv_b2_059) are distinct beats. | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: Krishna Stupefies Shiva and Puts Skanda to Flight
events.one_line_summary: Krishna throws the Jrimbhana astra, stupefying Shiva, and Pradyumna routs Skanda, while Bana's mother shields her son.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, stupefying Shiva with the Jrimbhana weapon, slew Bana's army, while Pradyumna's arrows drove the bloodied Skanda from the field; Bana's mother Kotara stood naked before Krishna to save her son's life. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 13-20)

Govinda, with the weapon of yawning, set Śankara a-gape... Hara, overcome with incessant gaping, sat down in his car, and was unable longer to contend with Krishńa... Kártikeya, wounded... took to flight.

events.variant_notes: BP: Jrimbhana astra; VP: weapon of yawning. VP bundles the three-headed Fever's defeat here.
events.notes: The Jvara/Fever episode is expanded in Harivamsha (hv_b2_063-066). | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: Krishna and Shiva Duel with Divine Weapons
events.one_line_summary: The Vrishnis besiege Shonitapura; Shiva and Skanda fight for Bana, and Krishna repels Shiva's celestial weapons.

sources.source_excerpt: Pradyumna, Satyaki, Gada and Samba with twelve armies besieged Shonitapura; Shiva, mounted on Nandi with his hosts, fought for Bana, and Krishna countered Shiva's Brahma, wind, fire and Pashupata weapons with matching astras. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-12)

Vishnu discharged Indra's weapon at Rudra... Hara discharged the highly dreadful fiery weapon... Vāsudeva took up Vāruna weapon... the fire of the fiery weapon was extinguished... Mādhava discharged his Vaishnava weapon... all the Bhutas, Yakshas and Asuras... fled on all sides

events.variant_notes: BP: Krishna repels Shiva's celestial weapons; Harivamsha: exchange of Indra/Shiva/Varuna/Vaishnava weapons.

events.working_title: Krishna Severs Bana's Thousand Arms and Spares Him
events.one_line_summary: Krishna severs Bana's thousand arms with his discus; Shiva intercedes, and Krishna spares Bana with four arms remaining.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna cut off Bana's thousand arms with his discus as if pruning branches; Shiva pleaded for his devotee, and Krishna, honoring the boon given to Prahrada, spared Bana, leaving him four arms and freedom from fear. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 20-48)

taking up that wonderful discus... discharged it and cut off Vāna's arms... Gradually cutting off Vāna's thousand arms and making him the owner of only two the Sudarshana discus returned into Krishna's hands
The discus... lopped off successively the numerous arms of the Asura... 'Since you, Śankara, have given a boon unto Báňa, let him live: from respect to your promises, my discus is arrested.'

events.variant_notes: Arms remaining varies: four (BP) vs two (Harivamsha/VP). Shiva intercedes in all.
events.notes: Bana's subsequent dance and Mahakala boon (hv_b2_074) is a distinct beat. | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: Aniruddha and Usha Are Freed
events.one_line_summary: Bana surrenders, gives Aniruddha and Usha to Krishna, and the Vrishnis return in triumph to Dvaraka.

sources.source_excerpt: Obtaining fearlessness, Bana bowed to Krishna, placed Aniruddha and his bride Usha on a chariot, and sent them with an army; Krishna entered Dvaraka amid conches and drums, greeted by the citizens. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 49-52)

Baladeva, Krishna, Pradyumna, Narada and Suparna entered into the female appartment for releasing Aniruddha. Seeing Garuda, all the huge serpents, which stuck to Aniruddha's person in the shape of arrows, at once left him

events.variant_notes: BP: Bana surrenders and hands them over; Harivamsha: the serpent-bonds fall away at the sight of Garuda.

events.working_title: Balarama Marries Revati
events.one_line_summary: Some days after the founding of Dwaraka, Baladeva weds Revati, the daughter of king Revata, with Rishabha's consent.

sources.source_excerpt: A few days after with Reshava's consent Baladeva acquired the good-natured daughter of Revata, by name Revati.
Thus decorated, Ráma sported two months in Vraja, and then returned to Dwáraká, where the married Revatí, the daughter of king Raivata, by whom he had two sons, Nishat́ha and Ulmuka.

events.variant_notes: Harivamsha: weds Revati, daughter of king Revata; VP: after sporting two months in Vraja, marries Revati daughter of Raivata.

events.working_title: Aniruddha Is Betrothed to Rukmi's Granddaughter
events.one_line_summary: Setting aside his grudge for his sister Rukmini's sake, Rukmi weds his granddaughter Rocana to Aniruddha in Bhojakata.

sources.source_excerpt: Though he still nursed enmity against Krishna, Rukmi, to please his sister Rukmini, gave his granddaughter Rocana in marriage to Aniruddha, and at that wedding Rukmini, Rama, Krishna and the other Yadavas went to Bhojakata. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 19-26)
he had by her the powerful and gallant prince Aniruddha... Upon the occasion of the nuptials Ráma and other Yádavas attended Krishńa to Bhojakat́a, the city of Rukmin.

events.variant_notes: Both: Aniruddha wed to Rukmi's granddaughter, celebrated at Bhojakata.

events.working_title: Balarama Slays Rukmi at the Dice Game
events.one_line_summary: At the wedding, Rukmi cheats Balarama at dice and insults him; enraged, Balarama kills Rukmi with his iron club.

sources.source_excerpt: Urged by the Kalinga king, Rukmi played dice with Balarama; when Rukmi falsely claimed victory, a heavenly voice declared Balarama the winner, but Rukmi jeered that cowherds cannot play dice; enraged, Balarama struck him down with his club, and Krishna said nothing, fearing to wound Rukmini. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-39)
