In that game of dice with Rukshmi, Baladeva betted from ten to a thousand gold coins. ... Enraged at those words, Rāma, the foremost of Yadus, slew with force that harsh-speeched and jealous Rukshmi. ... he struck down the teeth of the Kalinga king.
Balaráma thus excited, his eyes red with rage, started up, and struck Rukmin with the board on which the game was played, and killed him.

events.variant_notes: Weapon varies: iron club (BP), dice-board (Harivamsha). VP adds a heavenly voice confirms the foul play.

events.working_title: Krishna Slays Paundraka and the King of Kashi
events.one_line_summary: Krishna marches to Kashi, beheads the impostor Paundraka with his discus, and casts the head of the Kashi king into his own city.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, seeing Paundraka arrayed in counterfeit divine dress, laughed, then with sharp arrows and his discus cut off Paundraka's head and the Kashi king's head, casting the latter into the city of Kashi. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-24)

he let fly the discus and the mace, by which Pauńd́raka was cut to pieces, and cast on the ground... the valiant king of Káśí... continued the conflict, till Śauri decapitated him with his arrows, shooting his head into the city of Káśí.

events.variant_notes: Both: impostor Paundraka beheaded, Kashi king's head cast/shot into his own city.
events.notes: Paundraka's false claim (bp10c_065) is a distinct beat. | [arc-remap by curator rule]

events.working_title: Sudarshana Consumes the Conjured Fire and Burns Varanasi/Benares
events.one_line_summary: Sudakshina conjures a fiery demon by black magic to kill Krishna; Krishna's Sudarshana discus destroys it and burns Varanasi.

sources.source_excerpt: Sudakshina, son of the Kashi king, worshipped Shiva and by abhichara rites raised a terrible fire-demon; Krishna sent his Sudarshana discus, which destroyed the demon, burned Sudakshina and his priests, and reduced Varanasi to ashes. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 25-42)

Sudarśana, the discus of Vishńu, immediately attacked the fiend... pursued by him with equal velocity, until she reached Varánáśí... Thus was Varánáśí burnt, with all its princes and their followers... The whole of a city, that was inaccessible to the gods, was thus wrapped in flames.

events.variant_notes: BP: Sudakshina conjures the fiery demon; VP: the son of the slain Kashi king conjures the fiend.

events.working_title: Krishna Wins Lakshmana at Her Svayamvara
events.one_line_summary: Krishna weds Bhadra, daughter of his aunt, and carries off Lakshmana of Madra from her svayamvara.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna wed Bhadra, daughter of his aunt Srutakirti, given by her brothers; and he carried off Lakshmana, the fair daughter of the king of Madra, from her svayamvara like Garuda seizing nectar. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 55-57)

Asked by Draupadi how Krishna married them, Lakshmana recounts that her father arranged a svayamvara with a fish target, at which kings from everywhere failed even to string the bow. Krishna took up the bow, strung it effortlessly, and with a single arrow shot the fish, and when the envious kings attacked he cut them down with his arrows and carried Lakshmana to Dwaraka. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 16-38)

events.variant_notes: bp10d_039 gives Lakshmana's own account (strung a bow, shot the fish target); bp10c_040 bundles her abduction with Bhadra's marriage.

events.working_title: Muchukunda's Story || Muchukunda, an Ikshvaku king who once guarded the gods against the asuras, was granted deep sleep as his reward.
events.one_line_summary: Muchukunda, an Ikshvaku king who once guarded the gods against the asuras, was granted deep sleep as his reward.

sources.source_excerpt: Muchukunda, son of Mandhata of the Ikshvaku line, guarded the gods in battle against the asuras; when they released him, he chose sleep as his boon and lay in the cave. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 12-20)

events.variant_notes: BP-only beat; immediately precedes the boon (bp10c_015).

events.working_title: Krishna Grants Muchukunda His Boon || Krishna reveals himself to Muchukunda, who renounces all boons and asks only for devotion; Krishna grants him liberation in a future birth.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna reveals himself to Muchukunda, who renounces all boons and asks only for devotion; Krishna grants him liberation in a future birth.

sources.source_excerpt: Recognizing Narayana, Muchukunda prayed for nothing but Krishna's service, renouncing all heavenly rewards; Krishna granted that in his next birth he would become a brahmana and attain him alone. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 21-62)

events.variant_notes: BP-only beat; follows Muchukunda's story (bp10c_014).

events.working_title: Krishna and Balarama Elude Jarasandha || Krishna and Balarama feign flight from Jarasandha, escape to Dvaraka over the sea, and Jarasandha falsely believes them burned.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama feign flight from Jarasandha, escape to Dvaraka over the sea, and Jarasandha falsely believes them burned.

sources.source_excerpt: Pursued by Jarasandha, Krishna and Rama fled on foot and climbed Mt. Pravarshana; Jarasandha set fire to the hill, but the two leapt down eleven yojanas and returned unseen to their sea-girt city, while Jarasandha wrongly believed them burned. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-13)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Harivamsha resolve to abandon Mathura (hv_a_001) and the founding (bp10c_012/vp5_023_02).

events.working_title: Rukmini Resolves to Marry Krishna and Sends a Brahmana Messenger || Princess Rukmini, hearing of Krishna's virtues, resolves to wed him and sends a brahmana to Dvaraka with her secret message.
events.one_line_summary: Princess Rukmini, hearing of Krishna's virtues, resolves to wed him and sends a brahmana to Dvaraka with her secret message.

sources.source_excerpt: Rukmini, daughter of Bhishmaka of Vidarbha, heard of Krishna's beauty and virtues and resolved he alone was a fitting husband; though her brother Rukmi wished to give her to Shishupala, she sent a trusted brahmana swiftly to Dvaraka. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-27)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster (bp10c_021/vp5_026_01); message is bp10c_018.

events.working_title: Rukmini's Love-Message to Krishna || Rukmini's message begs Krishna to carry her away in the rakshasa manner before Shishupala can claim her.
events.one_line_summary: Rukmini's message begs Krishna to carry her away in the rakshasa manner before Shishupala can claim her.

sources.source_excerpt: Rukmini's message: 'You I have chosen as my husband; come and take my hand before Shishupala, like a jackal, seizes the lion's share. Tomorrow is my marriage; carry me away by the rakshasa rite, defeating the hosts of Shishupala and Jarasandha.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 28-42)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster; resolve is bp10c_017.

events.working_title: Krishna Hastens to Kundina || Krishna receives Rukmini's message and races overnight to Kundina, where rival kings are gathering to enforce Shishupala's claim.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna receives Rukmini's message and races overnight to Kundina, where rival kings are gathering to enforce Shishupala's claim.

sources.source_excerpt: Hearing the message, Krishna said 'I too cannot sleep at night for her'; he set out at once and reached Vidarbha in a single night, while Shishupala, Jarasandha, Shalva and other hostile kings gathered in Kundina resolved to fight if Krishna came. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-20)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster (bp10c_021/vp5_026_01).

events.working_title: Rukmini's Prayer at the Temple of Ambika || Anxious at Krishna's delay, Rukmini visits the temple of goddess Ambika and prays that Krishna alone may be her husband.
events.one_line_summary: Anxious at Krishna's delay, Rukmini visits the temple of goddess Ambika and prays that Krishna alone may be her husband.

sources.source_excerpt: As the wedding hour neared, Rukmini, not seeing Krishna arrive, prayed tearfully; going in procession to the temple of Bhavani, she bowed: 'May Krishna, the Lord, alone become my husband; bless this.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 20-52)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster; distinct prayer beat.

events.working_title: Mayavati (Rati) Rescues and Raises Pradyumna || A fish swallows the infant; a cook finds him, and Mayavati, who is Rati, recognizes Kama reborn and raises him as her own.
events.one_line_summary: A fish swallows the infant; a cook finds him, and Mayavati, who is Rati, recognizes Kama reborn and raises him as her own.

sources.source_excerpt: A great fish swallowed the infant and was caught by fishermen and given to Shambara; the cook found the child in its belly and gave him to Mayavati, who — being Rati, Kama's wife — knew him and raised him, later revealing he was Krishna's son and her own destined husband. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 3-14)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Shambara-stole cluster (bp10c_024); Harivamsha expands (hv_b2_042-047).

events.working_title: Satyabhama Reports Her Father's Murder || Satyabhama finds her father slain, and hastens to Hastinapura to tell Krishna, who laments with Balarama.
events.one_line_summary: Satyabhama finds her father slain, and hastens to Hastinapura to tell Krishna, who laments with Balarama.

sources.source_excerpt: Satyabhama, seeing her father killed, wailed 'father, father, I am slain'; she laid his body in a vat of oil and went to Hastinapura to tell Krishna, who, hearing it, wept with Balarama. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 6-8)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Satadhanva cluster (bp10c_032/hv_a_007).

events.working_title: Krishna Abducts Mitravinda and Wins Satya || Krishna carries off Mitravinda of Avanti from her svayamvara and wins Satya of Kosala by taming seven fierce bulls.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna carries off Mitravinda of Avanti from her svayamvara and wins Satya of Kosala by taming seven fierce bulls.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna forcibly carried off Mitravinda, the princess of Avanti, before the assembled kings; and to win Satya, daughter of Nagnajit of Kosala, he multiplied himself sevenfold and with ease subdued seven untamable bulls, winning the princess. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 29-55)

events.variant_notes: Bundles two moments (Mitravinda + Satya); cross-ref bpc1_040 for the Satya recall.

events.working_title: Krishna Breaches Mura's Fortifications || Indra complains of Narakasura's thefts; Krishna with Satyabhama on Garuda shatters the mountain, weapon, water, fire and Mura-pasha defenses of Pragjyotisha.
events.one_line_summary: Indra complains of Narakasura's thefts; Krishna with Satyabhama on Garuda shatters the mountain, weapon, water, fire and Mura-pasha defenses of Pragjyotisha.

sources.source_excerpt: Indra, robbed of his umbrella, earrings and the Amara hill, complained to Krishna; riding Garuda with Satyabhama, Krishna broke the mountains with his mace, the weapon-forts with arrows, the fire and water with his discus, and Mura's nooses with his sword. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-5)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Naraka cluster; distinct fortification-breach beat (Mura's defenses).

events.working_title: Krishna Slays Mura and His Seven Sons || Krishna beheads the five-headed demon Mura and slays his seven sons who attack in revenge.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna beheads the five-headed demon Mura and slays his seven sons who attack in revenge.

sources.source_excerpt: Mura, roused by Krishna's conch, rose from the waters with five heads and hurled his trident; Krishna shattered it with two arrows and with his discus cut off Mura's heads, then slew Mura's seven sons who attacked to avenge their father. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 5-14)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Naraka cluster (hv_b1_120_02 bundles Mura's slaying).

events.working_title: Bhumi Returns Aditi's Earrings || The earth-goddess Bhumi restores Aditi's earrings and Varuna's umbrella and prays for the protection of Naraka's son Bhagadatta.
events.one_line_summary: The earth-goddess Bhumi restores Aditi's earrings and Varuna's umbrella and prays for the protection of Naraka's son Bhagadatta.

sources.source_excerpt: Bhumi, the earth, came before Krishna and offered the earrings of Aditi, Varuna's umbrella and the great jewel, and praying, begged Krishna to protect her son Bhagadatta; Krishna granted him fearlessness. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 22-31)

events.variant_notes: Distinct: Bhumi (earth-goddess) restores the treasures; cross-ref Krishna's earrings restoration (vp5_030_01).

events.working_title: Krishna Jests with Rukmini || Krishna playfully tells Rukmini she chose a poor, unworthy husband; she faints in grief, thinking he means to abandon her.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna playfully tells Rukmini she chose a poor, unworthy husband; she faints in grief, thinking he means to abandon her.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna jestingly told Rukmini she had foolishly chosen a penniless husband when great kings sought her, and should choose a worthy kshatriya instead; believing him in earnest, Rukmini fainted, her fan falling from her hand. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-27)

events.variant_notes: BP-only; paired with consolation beat (bp10c_049).

events.working_title: Krishna Consoles Rukmini || Krishna lifts Rukmini, reveals his jest, praises her devotion, and the two are reconciled in love.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna lifts Rukmini, reveals his jest, praises her devotion, and the two are reconciled in love.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, seeing her distress, raised her, wiped her tears and said 'I spoke in jest to hear your words'; Rukmini answered with loving devotion, and Krishna praised her faithfulness, and they enjoyed each other's company. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 28-58)

events.variant_notes: BP-only; paired with jest beat (bp10c_048).

events.working_title: Bana's Thousand Arms and Shiva's Boon || The thousand-armed asura Bana, son of Bali and devotee of Shiva, wins the boon of a worthy rival in battle.
events.one_line_summary: The thousand-armed asura Bana, son of Bali and devotee of Shiva, wins the boon of a worthy rival in battle.

sources.source_excerpt: Bana, eldest son of Bali, pleased Shiva with his thousand arms and asked for a rival worthy of him; Shiva declared that when Bana's flag fell, his pride would be humbled in battle with a peer. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-10)

events.variant_notes: BP-only background beat for the Bana episode.

events.working_title: Krishna Liberates King Nriga from a Lizard's Body || The Yadu princes find a giant lizard in a well; Krishna pulls it out with his left hand, and it becomes the radiant King Nriga.
events.one_line_summary: The Yadu princes find a giant lizard in a well; Krishna pulls it out with his left hand, and it becomes the radiant King Nriga.

sources.source_excerpt: The Yadu princes, thirsty, found a mountain-sized lizard in a dry well and could not pull it out with their ropes; Krishna came and with his left hand drew it out, and it became a being of molten-gold splendor. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

events.variant_notes: BP-only; Nriga episode has no cross-source parallel in this chunk.

events.working_title: Nriga's Story of the Disputed Cow || Nriga, an Ikshvaku king famed for charity, tells how he unwittingly gave one brahmana's stray cow to another and was cursed to become a lizard.
events.one_line_summary: Nriga, an Ikshvaku king famed for charity, tells how he unwittingly gave one brahmana's stray cow to another and was cursed to become a lizard.

sources.source_excerpt: Nriga, a great giver of cows, told how a stray cow of one brahmana got mixed into his herd and was given to another; both brahmanas claimed it and refused all compensation, and Yama, giving him the choice, made him first suffer his sin, so he fell as a lizard. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-23)

events.variant_notes: BP-only; follows bp10c_060.

events.working_title: Nriga Ascends and Krishna Warns Against Stealing Brahmanas' Wealth || Touched by Krishna, Nriga ascends to heaven in a celestial car, and Krishna warns the citizens that a brahmana's property is deadly poison.
events.one_line_summary: Touched by Krishna, Nriga ascends to heaven in a celestial car, and Krishna warns the citizens that a brahmana's property is deadly poison.

sources.source_excerpt: Nriga praised Krishna, bowed, and ascended to heaven in a celestial car; Krishna then taught the people that a brahmana's wealth is like poison — it consumes a king and his family for generations. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-43)

events.variant_notes: BP-only; follows bp10c_061.

events.working_title: Paundraka Falsely Claims to Be Vasudeva || Paundraka, king of Karusha, proclaims himself the true Vasudeva and sends a messenger demanding that Krishna surrender his divine insignia.
events.one_line_summary: Paundraka, king of Karusha, proclaims himself the true Vasudeva and sends a messenger demanding that Krishna surrender his divine insignia.

sources.source_excerpt: Paundraka, deluded into believing himself Vasudeva, sent a messenger to Krishna demanding he give up the divine marks he wore; the assembly laughed, and Krishna replied that he would hurl those signs at the fool and slay him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-9)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Paundraka-slaying cluster (bp10c_066/vp5_034_01).

events.working_title: The Gorilla Dvivida Ravages the Land || The gorilla Dvivida, Narakasura's friend, wreaks havoc on the countryside in revenge, burning villages, drowning lands and defiling sages' hermitages.
events.one_line_summary: The gorilla Dvivida, Narakasura's friend, wreaks havoc on the countryside in revenge, burning villages, drowning lands and defiling sages' hermitages.

sources.source_excerpt: Dvivida, the mighty ape and friend of Narakasura, seeking vengeance, set fire to cities and villages, uprooted mountains, drowned the coastal lands, and defiled the sages' hermitages and sacred fires. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Dvivida-slaying cluster (bp10c_069/vp5_036_01).

events.working_title: Balarama Seeks Samba's Release and Is Insulted || Balarama goes to Hastinapura as peacemaker, but the Kauravas, drunk on pride, mock the Yadavas and refuse to release Samba.
events.one_line_summary: Balarama goes to Hastinapura as peacemaker, but the Kauravas, drunk on pride, mock the Yadavas and refuse to release Samba.

sources.source_excerpt: Balarama, restraining the war-eager Vrishnis, went to Hastinapura and asked for Samba's release; the Kauravas mocked the Yadavas as cowherds who had risen above their station, and refused, insulting Balarama. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 13-38)

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Balarama-drags-Hastinapura cluster (bp10c_072).

events.working_title: Narada Sees Krishna in Every Palace of Dvaraka || Narada visits Dvaraka to witness Krishna's household, and sees him simultaneously present in each of the 16,000 palaces performing different duties.
events.one_line_summary: Narada visits Dvaraka to witness Krishna's household, and sees him simultaneously present in each of the 16,000 palaces performing different duties.

sources.source_excerpt: Narada, curious how Krishna wed 16,000 wives with one body, entered palace after palace and saw Krishna everywhere at once — playing dice, raising children, performing sacrifices, worshipping, hunting — in each of the 16,000 mansions. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-38)

events.working_title: Narada Marvels at Krishna's Yoga-Maya and Departs || Narada praises Krishna's unfathomable yoga-maya, and Krishna bids him wander singing his glories throughout the worlds.
events.one_line_summary: Narada praises Krishna's unfathomable yoga-maya, and Krishna bids him wander singing his glories throughout the worlds.

sources.source_excerpt: Narada, amazed, declared 'I understand your yoga-maya, hard to see even for the master of maya, revealed to me by serving your feet'; Krishna bade him roam the worlds singing his purifying pastimes, and Narada departed remembering him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 36-44)

events.working_title: Krishna's Dawn Worship in Dwaraka || Krishna rises in the brahma-muhurta, performs his ablutions, worships the Lord within, gives daily gifts of cows and wealth to brahmanas, and blesses his people.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna rises in the brahma-muhurta, performs his ablutions, worships the Lord within, gives daily gifts of cows and wealth to brahmanas, and blesses his people.

sources.source_excerpt: Waking with Rukmini at his side, Krishna bathes, meditates on the self-effulgent Brahman, performs the sandhya rites, and each day gives herds of milk-giving cows with golden horns to brahmanas. He then adorns himself, mounts his chariot, and enters the Sudharma assembly hall surrounded by the Yadus. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-19)

events.working_title: The Captive Kings Appeal to Krishna || A royal messenger arrives in Krishna's assembly and reports that Jarasandha has imprisoned twenty thousand defeated kings in Girivraja, who beg Krishna for release.
events.one_line_summary: A royal messenger arrives in Krishna's assembly and reports that Jarasandha has imprisoned twenty thousand defeated kings in Girivraja, who beg Krishna for release.

sources.source_excerpt: A man of extraordinary appearance is admitted before Krishna and, with joined palms, tells how Jarasandha has forcibly imprisoned the kings who refused to submit to his conquest, twenty thousand of them in Girivraja. The captive kings declare they have taken refuge in Krishna from the terror of worldly existence. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-30)

events.working_title: Uddhava's Counsel to Slay Jarasandha || Uddhava advises Krishna that the Rajasuya requires conquering the directions, and that Jarasandha — who can only be killed by Bhima in single combat — must first be destroyed.
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava advises Krishna that the Rajasuya requires conquering the directions, and that Jarasandha — who can only be killed by Bhima in single combat — must first be destroyed.

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava counsels that the Rajasuya is to be performed by one who has conquered all directions, so defeating Jarasandha serves both purposes. Since Jarasandha is the equal of Bhima alone and cannot be overthrown with an army, Bhima should go to him disguised as a brahmana, request single combat, and slay him before Krishna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-10)

events.variant_notes: VARIANT of the Rajasuya slaying-plan: Bhagavata Purana attributes the plan to Uddhava's counsel; Mahabharata 2.20 presents Krishna himself proposing it. Attribution difference is material — kept as separate stories.

events.working_title: Krishna's Grand Procession from Dwaraka || Krishna departs Dwaraka for Indraprastha with a vast army, chariots, elephants and his queens, to the sound of drums and conches.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna departs Dwaraka for Indraprastha with a vast army, chariots, elephants and his queens, to the sound of drums and conches.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna orders the departure, entrusts Dwaraka to Balarama, and mounts his Garuda-bannered chariot. Surrounded by an immense army with resounding drums, conches and trumpets, and followed by his queens in their conveyances, he sets out, crossing many lands, rivers and towns on the way to Indraprastha. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 11-21)

events.working_title: The Mace-Duel of Bhima and Jarasandha || Bhima and Jarasandha fight an indecisive mace-duel, exchanging blows that crush their clubs, then striking with iron-hard fists.
events.one_line_summary: Bhima and Jarasandha fight an indecisive mace-duel, exchanging blows that crush their clubs, then striking with iron-hard fists.

sources.source_excerpt: Taking up their great maces, the two heroes clash outside the city, circling in intricate patterns like wrestlers. Their clubs shatter under the force of their blows, and enraged they strike each other with fists hard as iron, the sound like thunder, yet the fight of the equal champions remains indecisive. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 33-38)

events.working_title: Krishna's Signal: Jarasandha Split in Two || Knowing Jarasandha's birth secret, Krishna signals by splitting a twig; Bhima tears Jarasandha in two and kills him.
events.one_line_summary: Knowing Jarasandha's birth secret, Krishna signals by splitting a twig; Bhima tears Jarasandha in two and kills him.

sources.source_excerpt: Knowing his enemy's birth and death, Krishna, wishing to show Bhima the means, splits a twig in two as a sign. Bhima understands, seizes Jarasandha by the feet, throws him down, and tearing him apart kills him, upon which a great cry of lamentation arises. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 39-44)

events.working_title: Sahadeva Crowned and the Kings Freed || Krishna crowns Jarasandha's son Sahadeva king of Magadha and releases all the kings imprisoned by Jarasandha.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna crowns Jarasandha's son Sahadeva king of Magadha and releases all the kings imprisoned by Jarasandha.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna installs Jarasandha's son Sahadeva as lord of the Magadhas, and releases the kings who had been held captive by Jarasandha. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 45)

events.working_title: The Liberated Kings Behold Krishna || Twenty thousand eight hundred freed kings emerge from the mountain prison, behold Krishna's form, praise him, receive his teaching, and are sent home with honor.
events.one_line_summary: Twenty thousand eight hundred freed kings emerge from the mountain prison, behold Krishna's form, praise him, receive his teaching, and are sent home with honor.

sources.source_excerpt: The released kings, emaciated and haggard, gaze upon Krishna's dark four-armed form and bow at his feet in gratitude. Krishna assures them their devotion to him will be firm, bids them rule their realms righteously, has them bathed, feasted and adorned, and sends them home with chariots and kind words. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-29)

events.working_title: Shalva Wins the Flying City Saubha || Shalva, friend of the slain Shishupala, vows to destroy the Yadavas and wins from Shiva through austere penance the flying iron city Saubha, built by Maya.
events.one_line_summary: Shalva, friend of the slain Shishupala, vows to destroy the Yadavas and wins from Shiva through austere penance the flying iron city Saubha, built by Maya.

sources.source_excerpt: Shalva, friend of Shishupala, who had been defeated at Rukmini's wedding, vows before the kings to make the earth devoid of Yadavas. To this end he worships the lord Shiva, eating a handful of dust each day, and after a year Shiva, easily pleased, offers him a boon. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-7)

events.working_title: Shalva Besieges Dwaraka || Shalva arrives at Dwaraka in the indestructible flying city Saubha and rains weapons, rocks and serpents upon the city, terrifying its people.
events.one_line_summary: Shalva arrives at Dwaraka in the indestructible flying city Saubha and rains weapons, rocks and serpents upon the city, terrifying its people.

sources.source_excerpt: Obtaining the self-moving, impenetrable vehicle Saubha, Shalva flies to Dwaraka remembering the enmity of the Vrishnis, and with a vast army shatters its gardens and gates, raining weapons, rocks, trees and serpents upon the city. Pradyumna, seeing his people afflicted, mounts his chariot and cries 'Do not fear,' and the Yadava warriors sally forth. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 7-16)

events.working_title: Pradyumna's Valor and Wounding || Pradyumna destroys Shalva's illusions and slays many foes, but is struck senseless by Dyuman's mace; recovering, he rebukes his charioteer for drawing him from the field.
events.one_line_summary: Pradyumna destroys Shalva's illusions and slays many foes, but is struck senseless by Dyuman's mace; recovering, he rebukes his charioteer for drawing him from the field.

sources.source_excerpt: Pradyumna in a moment dispels the demon's illusions with divine weapons and showers arrows on Shalva's host, winning the admiration of both armies. But Dyuman, Shalva's minister, strikes Pradyumna on the chest with his mace, and the charioteer carries the senseless hero away; regaining consciousness, Pradyumna rebukes him, saying no Yadu may be seen fleeing the field. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 17-32)

events.working_title: Krishna Returns to the Battle || Returning from Indraprastha and seeing evil omens, Krishna hurries to Dwaraka, orders his chariot against Shalva, and joins the fight, shattering Shalva's weapons.
events.one_line_summary: Returning from Indraprastha and seeing evil omens, Krishna hurries to Dwaraka, orders his chariot against Shalva, and joins the fight, shattering Shalva's weapons.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, summoned to Indraprastha for the Rajasuya, returns to Dwaraka perceiving dire omens, and realizing the Chaidya's allies have attacked his city, orders Daruka to drive his chariot against Shalva. Shalva hurls a blazing spear at Krishna's charioteer, which Krishna cuts to a hundred pieces with his arrows, and he pierces Shalva with sixteen shafts. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 5-18)

events.working_title: Krishna Slays Dantavakra and Viduratha || Dantavakra attacks Krishna with a mace to avenge Shishupala and Shalva; Krishna crushes his chest, then beheads his brother Viduratha with the discus.
events.one_line_summary: Dantavakra attacks Krishna with a mace to avenge Shishupala and Shalva; Krishna crushes his chest, then beheads his brother Viduratha with the discus.

sources.source_excerpt: Dantavakra, eager to repay his slain friends, rushes at Krishna on foot, taunting him as the murderer of his kinsmen, and strikes him on the head with his mace. Unshaken, Krishna crushes Dantavakra's chest with his mace Kaumodaki, and when his brother Viduratha comes on to avenge him, Krishna severs his crowned head with the discus. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-11)

events.working_title: Balarama Slays the Suta Romaharshana || At Naimisha, Balarama, seeing the suta Romaharshana seated without rising to honor the sages, kills him with a blade of kusha grass; the sages cry out that he has committed brahma-hatya.
events.one_line_summary: At Naimisha, Balarama, seeing the suta Romaharshana seated without rising to honor the sages, kills him with a blade of kusha grass; the sages cry out that he has committed brahma-hatya.

sources.source_excerpt: Visiting the sages' sacrifice at Naimisha, Balarama sees the suta Romaharshana, a shudra by birth, seated among the brahmanas without rising to honor them. Enraged, Balarama strikes him down with a blade of kusha grass, and the sages cry out that he has committed the sin of slaying a brahmana, saying this was done without knowledge and must be expiated. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 15-31)

events.working_title: The Sages Prescribe Balarama's Penance || The sages instruct Balarama that to expiate the brahmana-slaying he must slay the demon Balvala, who defiles their sacrifice, and then perform a year-long pilgrimage.
events.one_line_summary: The sages instruct Balarama that to expiate the brahmana-slaying he must slay the demon Balvala, who defiles their sacrifice, and then perform a year-long pilgrimage.

sources.source_excerpt: The sages tell Balarama that his atonement is to slay the cruel demon Balvala, son of Ilvala, who rains filth upon their sacrifice at every parvan, and then to wander Bharatavarsha bathing at the sacred fords for twelve months to be purified. Balarama accepts, undertaking the expiation for the world's benefit. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 32-39)

events.working_title: Balarama Slays the Demon Balvala || When Balvala appears at the sacrifice raining impurity, Balarama drags him down with his plough and crushes his head with his mace, and the sages shower Balarama with honors.
events.one_line_summary: When Balvala appears at the sacrifice raining impurity, Balarama drags him down with his plough and crushes his head with his mace, and the sages shower Balarama with honors.

sources.source_excerpt: At the next parvan the terrible demon Balvala appears, raining filth upon the sacrificial hall. Balarama, remembering his plough and mace, drags the sky-roaming Balvala down with the plough's tip and crushes his skull with the mace, and the delighted sages honor Balarama and bestow blessings, a celestial garland and garments upon him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-8)

events.working_title: Sudama's Poverty and Journey || Sudama's wife urges the destitute brahmana to seek his boyhood friend Krishna, and he sets out for Dwaraka with a humble gift of flat rice.
events.one_line_summary: Sudama's wife urges the destitute brahmana to seek his boyhood friend Krishna, and he sets out for Dwaraka with a humble gift of flat rice.

sources.source_excerpt: Sudama, a learned and self-controlled brahmana living in great poverty, is urged by his devoted wife to visit Krishna, his boyhood friend who now dwells in Dwaraka, saying Krishna will give them wealth. She borrows four handfuls of flattened rice and ties them in a rag as a gift, and Sudama sets out for Dwaraka wondering how he may gain sight of Krishna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 5-16)

events.working_title: Krishna Embraces His Old Friend || Krishna rises from his couch, embraces Sudama with tears of joy, washes his feet, and anoints him, while Rukmini fans him, astonishing the palace women.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna rises from his couch, embraces Sudama with tears of joy, washes his feet, and anoints him, while Rukmini fans him, astonishing the palace women.

sources.source_excerpt: Seeing Sudama from afar, Krishna rises from Rukmini's couch, runs to him, and embraces his old friend with tears of joy, then seats him on his own couch, washes his feet and bears the water on his head. The goddess Rukmini herself fans the emaciated brahmana, and the women of the palace marvel at the honor shown to a poor mendicant. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 16-26)

events.working_title: Memories of the Gurukula || Krishna and Sudama recall their student days under Sandipani, when they were sent to fetch firewood and, caught in a fierce storm, wandered lost until the guru found them at dawn.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna and Sudama recall their student days under Sandipani, when they were sent to fetch firewood and, caught in a fierce storm, wandered lost until the guru found them at dawn.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna asks Sudama whether he remembers their days serving the guru, and recounts how, sent by the guru's wife to gather firewood, they entered the forest when a violent wind and rain arose, night fell, and, lost in the darkness and holding hands, they wandered till the guru found them at sunrise and blessed them. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 27-42)

events.working_title: Krishna Eats Sudama's Flat Rice || Krishna asks for the gift and eats Sudama's handful of flat rice with delight, and Sudama, too ashamed to ask for anything, returns home empty-handed.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna asks for the gift and eats Sudama's handful of flat rice with delight, and Sudama, too ashamed to ask for anything, returns home empty-handed.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna asks his friend what gift he has brought, saying even a trifle offered with love pleases him, and taking the flattened rice from Sudama's robe, eats one handful and reaches for a second — but the goddess of fortune, pleased, stays his hand, saying this much suffices to grant all riches. Sudama spends the night, and returns home without asking Krishna for any wealth. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 2-12)

events.working_title: Sudama Finds His Hut a Palace || Returning home, Sudama finds his poor dwelling transformed into a celestial palace and his wife radiant, and he reflects that this is Krishna's unasked grace.
events.one_line_summary: Returning home, Sudama finds his poor dwelling transformed into a celestial palace and his wife radiant, and he reflects that this is Krishna's unasked grace.

sources.source_excerpt: Reaching his home, Sudama finds it surrounded by celestial mansions with gardens and lakes, his wife radiant like the goddess of fortune among her attendants, and his house become a palace with golden couches and jeweled lamps. He reflects that the Lord, knowing wealth would make him forget, gave him prosperity unasked, and that Krishna treasured even his single handful of rice. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 13-37)

events.working_title: The Brahmana's Dying Sons || In Dwaraka, a brahmana's newborn sons die one after another; he lays their bodies at the palace gate and laments the king's failure to protect his subjects.
events.one_line_summary: In Dwaraka, a brahmana's newborn sons die one after another; he lays their bodies at the palace gate and laments the king's failure to protect his subjects.

sources.source_excerpt: A brahmana's infant sons die as soon as they touch the ground, and each time he lays the dead child at the palace gate, lamenting that the king's fault has slain his children. He accuses the unrighteous ruler of failing in his duty, so that his subjects perish in misery. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 20-27)

events.working_title: Arjuna's Failed Vow || Arjuna boasts that he will protect the brahmana's next child, but though he fences the delivery-room with arrows, the newborn vanishes, and the brahmana rebukes him.
events.one_line_summary: Arjuna boasts that he will protect the brahmana's next child, but though he fences the delivery-room with arrows, the newborn vanishes, and the brahmana rebukes him.

sources.source_excerpt: Arjuna, hearing the brahmana's lament, vows that he will protect the next child or enter fire, and when the time comes he rings the delivery-room with a cage of arrows. But the newborn vanishes bodily into the sky, and the brahmana mocks Arjuna, saying that even Balarama, Krishna, Pradyumna and Aniruddha could not save the child, and curses Arjuna's boasting. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 28-40)

events.working_title: Krishna Carries Off Rukmini and Wins Satya || Uddhava recalls how Krishna carried off Rukmini, Bhishmaka's daughter, by the gandharva rite, and how he defeated the proud kings to win Satya (Nagnajiti) at her svayamvara.
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls how Krishna carried off Rukmini, Bhishmaka's daughter, by the gandharva rite, and how he defeated the proud kings to win Satya (Nagnajiti) at her svayamvara.

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava said: 'Summoned by Bhishmaka's daughter, he carried off his own share by the gandharva rite while the suitors looked on; and, humbling the proud kings, he won Nagnajiti at her svayamvara.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 2-3)

events.variant_notes: Recall bundling Rukmini's abduction + Satya's svayamvara; cross-ref both clusters.

events.working_title: Krishna Slays Narakasura and Weds the Sixteen Thousand || Uddhava recalls how Krishna slew the demon Naraka (Bhauma), who had seized the earth's princesses, and how the freed princesses chose Krishna as their husband, who married them all in one moment and begot sons in each.
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls how Krishna slew the demon Naraka (Bhauma), who had seized the earth's princesses, and how the freed princesses chose Krishna as their husband, who married them all in one moment and begot sons in each.

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava said: 'Seeing the son of the earth-goddess who devoured the heavens, he slew him; the princesses seized by Bhauma, seeing Hari the friend of the distressed, rose and chose him, and he took their hands in one moment in their many houses, begetting ten sons in each.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 5-8)

events.variant_notes: Recall bundling Naraka's slaying + the 16,000 marriages; cross-ref both clusters.

events.working_title: Krishna Defeats the Besieging Kings and Demons || Uddhava recalls how Krishna destroyed the hosts of Kala, Magadha (Jarasandha) and Shalva that besieged Dwaraka, and slew Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra and others.
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls how Krishna destroyed the hosts of Kala, Magadha (Jarasandha) and Shalva that besieged Dwaraka, and slew Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra and others.

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava said: 'The hosts of Kala, Magadha and Shalva that besieged the city he slew; Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura and Balvala, and others like Dantavakra, he killed, or had killed.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-10)

events.variant_notes: Recall bundling many battles (Kala, Magadha, Shalva, Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra).

events.working_title: Krishna Foresees the Yadavas' Self-Destruction || Uddhava recalls Krishna's deliberation that the Yadu warriors, themselves the remaining burden of the earth, could be destroyed in no other way than by their own quarrel, and that when he acted, they would destroy themselves.
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls Krishna's deliberation that the Yadu warriors, themselves the remaining burden of the earth, could be destroyed in no other way than by their own quarrel, and that when he acted, they would destroy themselves.

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava said: 'What burden of the earth remained, when Drona, Bhishma, Arjuna and Bhima were gone, but the unbearable host of the Yadavas? When they quarrel among themselves, eyes red with wine, there is no other way to destroy them; when I act, they will vanish of themselves.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 13-14)

events.variant_notes: Recall; cross-ref the Yadavas' self-destruction (vp5_037_03).

events.working_title: The Vrishnis Suspect Krishna of Stealing the Jewel || Hearing of Prasena's death, the Vrishnis and Andhakas suspect Krishna of stealing the Syamantaka; the innocent Krishna resolves to recover it.
events.one_line_summary: Hearing of Prasena's death, the Vrishnis and Andhakas suspect Krishna of stealing the Syamantaka; the innocent Krishna resolves to recover it.

sources.source_excerpt: Hearing of the death of Prasena, all the members of Vrishni and Andhaka families entertained suspicions against Krishna, because they knew that he had a fancy for that jewel.

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Prasena cluster (bp10c_029/hv_a_003); distinct accusation beat.

events.working_title: Balarama Departs to Mithila in Anger || Believing Krishna is withholding the jewel, Balarama angrily leaves for Mithila, where Duryodhana learns the use of clubs from him.
events.one_line_summary: Believing Krishna is withholding the jewel, Balarama angrily leaves for Mithila, where Duryodhana learns the use of clubs from him.

sources.source_excerpt: Repeatedly exclaiming 'Fie on you, Fie on you,' he replied to Janarddana... 'I go away. I have nothing to do with you or other Vrishnis of Dwarka.'

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Satadhanva cluster (bp10c_034/hv_a_008).

events.working_title: Akrura's Exile Brings Drought; His Return Brings Rain || After Akrura leaves Dwarka, Indra withholds rain and drought devastates the land; when he returns, the rains fall again.
events.one_line_summary: After Akrura leaves Dwarka, Indra withholds rain and drought devastates the land; when he returns, the rains fall again.

sources.source_excerpt: After the departure of Akrura Pakashasana did not pour rain... When the liberal Akrura returned to Dwarka the thousand-eyed Indra began to discharge showers on the bank of the ocean.

events.variant_notes: Harivamsha-only; Akrura's exile/drought episode.

events.working_title: Krishna Selects the Site of Dwaraka || The Yadavas reach the ocean shore, and Krishna, seeking a place to build, chooses the coppery tract near Mount Raivata where the Yadavas encamp.
events.one_line_summary: The Yadavas reach the ocean shore, and Krishna, seeking a place to build, chooses the coppery tract near Mount Raivata where the Yadavas encamp.

sources.source_excerpt: Searching for a site where he would lay out a city Krishna ... saw an extensive tract of land situated on the bank of the ocean. ... Keshava selected that site for his city and the Yādavas also wanted to encamp their soldiers there.

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: founding cluster (bp10c_012/vp5_023_02); site-selection beat.

events.working_title: Krishna Enriches Dwaraka || Krishna bids the treasure-guard Sankha shower wealth on every household and sends Vayu to fetch the celestial assembly-hall Sudharma from heaven.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna bids the treasure-guard Sankha shower wealth on every household and sends Vayu to fetch the celestial assembly-hall Sudharma from heaven.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna ... felt a desire of gratifying his own people, who were poor, with profuse riches. ... Sankha ... ordered them to shower heaps of wealth in every house of Dwāravati. ... 'beg of them the assembly Hall Sudharmā and bring it to Dwarkā.'

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: founding cluster; enrichment beat.

events.working_title: Rukmavati's Swayamvara and Marriage || Rukmi's daughter Rukmavati chooses Pradyumna at her swayamvara; later her son Aniruddha is wed to Rukmavati's namesake, the granddaughter of Rukmi.
events.one_line_summary: Rukmi's daughter Rukmavati chooses Pradyumna at her swayamvara; later her son Aniruddha is wed to Rukmavati's namesake, the granddaughter of Rukmi.

sources.source_excerpt: the Bidarbha king's daughter chose Pradyumna the slayer of enemies (for her husband). ... 'I confer Rukshmavati on Aniruddha endued with accomplishments and of a peaceful nature.'

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Aniruddha nuptials (bp10c_050/vp5_028_01) and Pradyumna's marriage to Rukmavati.

events.working_title: Narada Presents the Parijata Flower to Rukmini || Narada gives Krishna a Parijata flower, which Krishna passes to Rukmini; the sage extols Rukmini as the foremost of his wives.
events.one_line_summary: Narada gives Krishna a Parijata flower, which Krishna passes to Rukmini; the sage extols Rukmini as the foremost of his wives.

sources.source_excerpt: Nārada ... gave him a Pārijata flower. ... Bhoja's daughter Rukshmini was by him, so Hari gave her that Parijata flower. ... 'among the sixteen thousand wives of Vāsudeva, I consider thee as the foremost and the most beloved.'

events.working_title: Satyabhama Is Consumed by Jealousy || Satyabhama's maids report Rukmini's good fortune; the proud queen, unable to bear her co-wife's honor, casts off her ornaments and retires to the apartment of anger.
events.one_line_summary: Satyabhama's maids report Rukmini's good fortune; the proud queen, unable to bear her co-wife's honor, casts off her ornaments and retires to the apartment of anger.

sources.source_excerpt: But the highly proud Satyabhāma ... could not bear the accession of such a good fortune unto the other wife of her husband. ... Worked up with anger like the flame of fire ... she entered into the lonely apartment of anger.

events.working_title: Krishna Consoles the Jealous Satyabhama || Krishna steals into Satyabhama's chamber and, fanning her and wiping her tears, protests that his love dwells in her alone.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna steals into Satyabhama's chamber and, fanning her and wiping her tears, protests that his love dwells in her alone.

sources.source_excerpt: he approached Satyabhama with faltering steps. Taking up the fan and standing by her side, he then began to fan slowly ... 'Just as flame is in fire ... so my love resides in thee and thee only.'

events.working_title: Krishna Promises Satyabhama the Parijata Tree || Satyabhama confesses her grief over the Parijata flower given to Rukmini; Krishna vows to fetch the whole Parijata tree from Indra's heaven for her.
events.one_line_summary: Satyabhama confesses her grief over the Parijata flower given to Rukmini; Krishna vows to fetch the whole Parijata tree from Indra's heaven for her.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna ... said: ... 'What to speak of a single flower, I shall fetch that best of all trees namely the Parijata tree itself, from the gardens of paradise, and keep it in thy mansion.' ... 'so be it, then; this shall be my foremost concern.'

events.working_title: Krishna Sends Narada to Ask Indra for the Parijata || Krishna asks Narada to request the Parijata tree from Indra as a brotherly favour, and warns that if refused he will come himself to seize it.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna asks Narada to request the Parijata tree from Indra as a brotherly favour, and warns that if refused he will come himself to seize it.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna ... said: ... 'remind Pakasasana of all our ancient brotherly love ... Ask him therefore to send down to Dwarvati that best of all trees the Pārijāta.' ... 'If that lord of the immortals do not give the Parijata tree at thy request, I shall then hurl my mace at his breast.'

events.working_title: Indra Refuses and Challenges Krishna || Narada relays Krishna's demand; Indra, recounting past grievances, refuses to part with the Parijata tree unless conquered in battle and sends back a challenge.
events.one_line_summary: Narada relays Krishna's demand; Indra, recounting past grievances, refuses to part with the Parijata tree unless conquered in battle and sends back a challenge.

sources.source_excerpt: Indra ... said: ... 'Until I am conquered in a battle by the wielder of the discus Krishna, I will not, O foremost of sages, part with the Pārijata tree.' ... 'tell Achyuta that I am prepared for the quarrel.'

events.working_title: Pradyumna Duels Jayanta in the Sky || Pradyumna, son of Rukmini, battles Indra's son Jayanta; a heavenly weapon burns Pradyumna's chariot to ashes yet cannot harm him, who stands firm in the sky.
events.one_line_summary: Pradyumna, son of Rukmini, battles Indra's son Jayanta; a heavenly weapon burns Pradyumna's chariot to ashes yet cannot harm him, who stands firm in the sky.

sources.source_excerpt: a fierce combat raged between the heroic Jayanta and the son of Rukshmini... The car of the illustrious Pradyumna was burnt down by that weapon but it could not... consume the son of Rukshmini

events.working_title: Satyaki Fights the Brahmana Pravara; Garuda Strikes Him Down || Satyaki duels the twice-born warrior Pravara, who repeatedly disarms him; when Pravara tries to seize the Parijata, Garuda's wing-blow hurls him and his car four miles back.
events.one_line_summary: Satyaki duels the twice-born warrior Pravara, who repeatedly disarms him; when Pravara tries to seize the Parijata, Garuda's wing-blow hurls him and his car four miles back.

sources.source_excerpt: Garuda struck him with his wings so vehemently that he, with his car, fell full four miles back and there fainted away

events.working_title: Garuda Fells Airavata from Heaven || Garuda fights Indra's elephant Airavata, striking it with claws and talons until the wounded elephant falls from the heights of heaven onto the Parijatra mountain.
events.one_line_summary: Garuda fights Indra's elephant Airavata, striking it with claws and talons until the wounded elephant falls from the heights of heaven onto the Parijatra mountain.

sources.source_excerpt: Garuda, of mighty strength, struck Airāvata on the head with his fierce claws furnished with fearful talons. Afflicted sorely with the wound... the elephant fell from the heights of heaven on the top of that best of mountains the Pārijātra

events.working_title: Krishna Worships Shiva and Wins His Boon || Pausing the fight at nightfall, Krishna performs ablutions in the Ganga, eulogizes Shiva with a hymn, and Shiva appears with Uma, granting that he shall carry away the Parijata and remain invincible.
events.one_line_summary: Pausing the fight at nightfall, Krishna performs ablutions in the Ganga, eulogizes Shiva with a hymn, and Shiva appears with Uma, granting that he shall carry away the Parijata and remain invincible.

sources.source_excerpt: Thus eulogised the god Mahādeva... spoke to Nārāyana:—"O best of gods, thou shalt obtain the things desired by thee; thou shalt carry away the Pārijāta tree... thou shalt be invincible"

events.working_title: Shiva Reveals the Danava Stronghold of Satpura || Shiva tells Krishna of the Danavas hidden in the Satpura stronghold beneath the mountain — invincible to the gods by Brahma's boon — and Krishna is enshrined on the Parijatra mountain.
events.one_line_summary: Shiva tells Krishna of the Danavas hidden in the Satpura stronghold beneath the mountain — invincible to the gods by Brahma's boon — and Krishna is enshrined on the Parijatra mountain.

sources.source_excerpt: on the summit of this mountain... there is a stronghold of the Dānavas called Satpura. Hidden inside that fastness live mighty Dānavas of wicked soul... do thou, O Keshava, slay them

events.working_title: Kashyapa and Aditi Reconcile Krishna and Indra || Sent by Brahma, the parents Kashyapa and Aditi halt the battle, and the two 'brothers' lay down their arms, bathe in the Jahnvi, and are reconciled.
events.one_line_summary: Sent by Brahma, the parents Kashyapa and Aditi halt the battle, and the two 'brothers' lay down their arms, bathe in the Jahnvi, and are reconciled.

sources.source_excerpt: holding them both by the hands Aditi said:—"Born of the same parents you are trying to slay each other as if you are not brothers... lay down your arms and hear what I say"

events.working_title: Satyabhama's Punyaka Rite and the Gift to Narada || Satyabhama binds Krishna to the Parijata, dedicates him to the sage Narada, and gifts gold, kine and jewels; Narada releases him for a fee, and Satyabhama distributes celestial garments to the sixteen thousand wives.
events.one_line_summary: Satyabhama binds Krishna to the Parijata, dedicates him to the sage Narada, and gifts gold, kine and jewels; Narada releases him for a fee, and Satyabhama distributes celestial garments to the sixteen thousand wives.

sources.source_excerpt: the lucky damsel, having put a garland of flowers around Krishna's neck, bound him to the Pārijāta tree... she dedicated Keshava unto Nārada... she gave away... mountains of gold and a thousand kine

events.working_title: Krishna Returns the Parijata and Vows to Destroy the Danavas || After a year of festival, Krishna returns the Parijata to heaven, and before Indra vows to slay, within ten days, the Danavas that the gods cannot kill.
events.one_line_summary: After a year of festival, Krishna returns the Parijata to heaven, and before Indra vows to slay, within ten days, the Danavas that the gods cannot kill.

sources.source_excerpt: From to-day within ten days I will kill all those Asuras... Although those Dānavas, proud of the boon conferred on them by Brahmā, are unslayable by the gods, still we will kill them for I am now a man

events.working_title: The Danavas Demand a Share of Brahmadatta's Yajna || At the Brahmana Brahmadatta's year-long sacrifice in Shatpura, the Danava Nikumbha and his kin demand Soma, jewels and the Brahmana's daughters, threatening to disrupt the rite.
events.one_line_summary: At the Brahmana Brahmadatta's year-long sacrifice in Shatpura, the Danava Nikumbha and his kin demand Soma, jewels and the Brahmana's daughters, threatening to disrupt the rite.

sources.source_excerpt: Nikumbha and other Daityas, proud of their boon, assembled there and said:—"Give us our share in the Yajna. We will drink Soma and Brahmadatta must give us his daughters"

events.working_title: Pradyumna Saves the Maidens by Illusion || When the Danavas scatter the sacrifice and carry off Brahmadatta's daughters, Pradyumna, sent by Krishna, rescues the maidens by illusion, leaving only counterfeit figures for the demons.
events.one_line_summary: When the Danavas scatter the sacrifice and carry off Brahmadatta's daughters, Pradyumna, sent by Krishna, rescues the maidens by illusion, leaving only counterfeit figures for the demons.

sources.source_excerpt: Pradyumna... went to Shatpura within a moment and took away the maidens by virtue of his illusive power. Creating their figures by his illusive power... he kept them before the Daityas

events.working_title: Narada Incites the Kings to Aid the Asuras || Narada, foreseeing a clash at the crowded sacrifice, prompts the Asuras to bribe the assembled kings with jewels and maidens so they will fight the Yadavas — while warning the Pandavas to hold back.
events.one_line_summary: Narada, foreseeing a clash at the crowded sacrifice, prompts the Asuras to bribe the assembled kings with jewels and maidens so they will fight the Yadavas — while warning the Pandavas to hold back.

sources.source_excerpt: Nārada... said to Nikumbha:—"...O hero, you invite in proper order the help of other kings..." ...returning... the great Nārada prevented the heroic sons of Pandu

events.working_title: Nikumbha Imprisons the Yadava Heroes by Maya || Using his illusive powers, Nikumbha carries Anadhrishti, Kritavarma, Charudeshna and many other Yadavas one by one into the Shatpura cave and imprisons them, enraging Krishna and Baladeva.
events.one_line_summary: Using his illusive powers, Nikumbha carries Anadhrishti, Kritavarma, Charudeshna and many other Yadavas one by one into the Shatpura cave and imprisons them, enraging Krishna and Baladeva.

sources.source_excerpt: by his illusive powers, took there Kritavarmā, Chārudeshna, Vaitarana... and numerous other Yādavas... he led the Yadavas to the dreadful cave of Shatpura

events.working_title: Krishna Routs the Asuras with the Sarnga Bow || Krishna, with his Sarnga bow, consumes the Danava host like fire on grass, while Jayanta and Pravara slay from the sky every Asura who tries to escape upward.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna, with his Sarnga bow, consumes the Danava host like fire on grass, while Jayanta and Pravara slay from the sky every Asura who tries to escape upward.

sources.source_excerpt: setting string to his Srānga bow... Krishna began to move about amongst the Dānavas as the god of fire ranges on grass... as soon as they rose up into the sky Jayanta and Pravara killed them all with arrows

events.working_title: Pradyumna Binds the Bribed Kings with Shiva's Nooses || Bearing nooses given by Hara and commanded by Nandi, Pradyumna binds Sisupala, Bhagadatta, Rukmi and the other kings who sided with the Asuras, and holds them in the illusory cave.
events.one_line_summary: Bearing nooses given by Hara and commanded by Nandi, Pradyumna binds Sisupala, Bhagadatta, Rukmi and the other kings who sided with the Asuras, and holds them in the illusory cave.

sources.source_excerpt: binding the king Bhagadatta, Shishupāla, Ahvati, Rukshmi and other kings... with the nooses given by Hara Rukshmini's son... took them all to the illusory cave

events.working_title: Krishna Slays Nikumbha with the Sudarshana Discus || As the routed Asuras return to fight, Krishna follows Nikumbha into the Shatpura cave and, commanded by an invisible voice to use his discus, cuts off the demon's head with the Sudarshana.
events.one_line_summary: As the routed Asuras return to fight, Krishna follows Nikumbha into the Shatpura cave and, commanded by an invisible voice to use his discus, cuts off the demon's head with the Sudarshana.

sources.source_excerpt: saluting Mahādeva he discharged his discus Sudarshana... That discus, effulgent like the solar disc... sundered Nikumbha's head adorned with most beautiful ear-rings

events.working_title: Krishna Distributes the Spoils and Grants Shatpura to Brahmadatta || After the victory, Krishna gives the Daitya maidens to the Yadavas, jewels and raiment to the kings, six thousand chariots to the Pandavas, and the city of Shatpura to Brahmadatta.
events.one_line_summary: After the victory, Krishna gives the Daitya maidens to the Yadavas, jewels and raiment to the kings, six thousand chariots to the Pandavas, and the city of Shatpura to Brahmadatta.

sources.source_excerpt: Keshava... conferred upon the Yadavas hundreds of Daitya maidens... he gave the Pāndavas six thousand cars with horses... gave that city of Shatpura to the Brāhmana Brahmadatta

events.working_title: Krishna Brings the Celestial Chhalikya Song to the Yadavas || Krishna stages a music soiree: Narada plays the vina, Krishna dances the Hallishaka with his flute, and the Apsaras Rambha and Urvashi perform, as the celestial Chhalikya song is brought down for mankind.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna stages a music soiree: Narada plays the vina, Krishna dances the Hallishaka with his flute, and the Apsaras Rambha and Urvashi perform, as the celestial Chhalikya song is brought down for mankind.

sources.source_excerpt: Narada began to play on his Vinā... Krishna began to perform Hallishaka accompanied with the music of his flute... the beautiful Rambhā... rose up, played and pleased Rāma and Keshava

events.working_title: Nikumbha Carries Away Bhanumati || While the Yadavas are absorbed in ocean sport, the Danava Nikumbha, avenging Pradyumna's earlier abduction of Prabhavati, steals Bhānu's daughter Bhanumati from her unguarded garden.
events.one_line_summary: While the Yadavas are absorbed in ocean sport, the Danava Nikumbha, avenging Pradyumna's earlier abduction of Prabhavati, steals Bhānu's daughter Bhanumati from her unguarded garden.

sources.source_excerpt: the highly wicked and unapproachable Dānava, Nikumbha... stole away the beautiful daughter of Bhānu by name Bhānumati... Taking advantage of this weak moment the wretched Dānava carried away the maiden

events.working_title: Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna Pursue the Abductor || Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna overtake Nikumbha on Garuda; careful not to wound the maiden, they pierce him with cane-like arrows as he flees across the earth, and Pradyumna recovers Bhanumati.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna overtake Nikumbha on Garuda; careful not to wound the maiden, they pierce him with cane-like arrows as he flees across the earth, and Pradyumna recovers Bhanumati.

sources.source_excerpt: Pārtha, Krishna and Kāma... did not strike the maiden but wounded the Danavas with their cane-like arrows... Pradyumna... got hold of the maiden Bhānumati. And Krishna, and Arjuna began to assail the Asura greatly with arrows

events.working_title: Nikumbha Fells Arjuna and Pradyumna; Krishna Duels Him || Emerging from the Shatpura cave, Nikumbha knocks Arjuna and Pradyumna senseless with his thorned club; enraged, Krishna seizes Kaumodaki and fights him in single combat.
events.one_line_summary: Emerging from the Shatpura cave, Nikumbha knocks Arjuna and Pradyumna senseless with his thorned club; enraged, Krishna seizes Kaumodaki and fights him in single combat.

sources.source_excerpt: Nikumbha... struck Pārtha on his head... Wounded on the head with that unseen stroke of the club the heroic Pradyumna lost his consciousness... Govinda... took up his club Koumodaki and ran towards Nikumbha

events.working_title: Krishna Destroys a Body of Nikumbha with the Discus || As Nikumbha's illusion fills earth and sky with a thousand of his forms, Krishna, perceiving the true form with celestial wisdom, cuts off its head with his discus and frees the abducted Arjuna.
events.one_line_summary: As Nikumbha's illusion fills earth and sky with a thousand of his forms, Krishna, perceiving the true form with celestial wisdom, cuts off its head with his discus and frees the abducted Arjuna.

sources.source_excerpt: they saw all over the earth and welkin thousands of Nikumbha... the Divine Lord Krishna... saw the true form of Nikumbha, the creator of illusions... with his discus, cut off his head

events.working_title: Narada Reveals Bhanumati's Fate; She Weds Sahadeva || Narada explains that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a Durvasa curse softened by the sages; Bhānu then gives her in marriage to Sahadeva.
events.one_line_summary: Narada explains that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a Durvasa curse softened by the sages; Bhānu then gives her in marriage to Sahadeva.

sources.source_excerpt: on one occasion... this your daughter excited the anger of the foremost of Munis Durvāsā who... imprecated a curse on her saying:—'...she must fall into the hands of an enemy'... do you now confer her on Sahadeva

events.working_title: Vajranabha Wins His Boon and Demands the Three Worlds || By austerities on Sumeru, the Asura Vajranabha wins from Brahma the unconquerable city Vajra and immunity from the gods, then challenges Indra for the sovereignty of the three worlds.
events.one_line_summary: By austerities on Sumeru, the Asura Vajranabha wins from Brahma the unconquerable city Vajra and immunity from the gods, then challenges Indra for the sovereignty of the three worlds.

sources.source_excerpt: Vajranābha... prayed for two boons that even the gods might not kill him, and that he might get the city Vajra... he said "O slayer of Pāka, all the three worlds are the common properties... I therefore wish to govern the three worlds... give me battle"

events.working_title: Krishna's Stratagem: the Actor Bhadra and the Swan Emissaries || Indra consults Krishna, who promises to slay Vajranabha after Vasudeva's horse-sacrifice; an actor named Bhadra wins a boon of entering the impenetrable city, and Indra sends swans to win Prabhavati for Pradyumna.
events.one_line_summary: Indra consults Krishna, who promises to slay Vajranabha after Vasudeva's horse-sacrifice; an actor named Bhadra wins a boon of entering the impenetrable city, and Indra sends swans to win Prabhavati for Pradyumna.

sources.source_excerpt: Indra... said to Dhārtarāshtra swans:—"...Do you describe to her the various accomplishments... of the high-souled Pradyumna... An actor, Bhadra by name, has of late obtained the boon (of entering into his city)"

events.working_title: The Yadavas Enter Vajra Disguised as Actors || Disguised as actors, the Yadavas enter Vajranabha's impenetrable city and perform the Ramayana and Rambhabhisara so skilfully that the Danavas shower them with jewels until their own wealth is drained.
events.one_line_summary: Disguised as actors, the Yadavas enter Vajranabha's impenetrable city and perform the Ramayana and Rambhabhisara so skilfully that the Danavas shower them with jewels until their own wealth is drained.

sources.source_excerpt: the Daityas, living in branch cities, took the Yadavas, disguised as actors, to the charming city of Vajra... Giving away presents in this way at every scene those Dānavas were deprived of their riches and jewels

events.working_title: Pradyumna in Bee Form Meets Prabhavati || Pradyumna, aided by Prabhavati's goose friend Suchimukhi, assumes the form of a bee hidden in a flower-garland, alights on Prabhavati's ear, and the long-pining lovers meet by night.
events.one_line_summary: Pradyumna, aided by Prabhavati's goose friend Suchimukhi, assumes the form of a bee hidden in a flower-garland, alights on Prabhavati's ear, and the long-pining lovers meet by night.

sources.source_excerpt: seeing a fragrant garland filled with bees carried for Prabhāvati, the highly powerful... Pradyumna... sat there on assuming the form of a bee... the heroic Bhaima chief slowly sat on Prabhāvati's ear

events.working_title: Kashyapa Warns Vajranabha, Who Marches on Heaven || After Kashyapa's sacrifice, Vajranabha rejects his father's warning that he cannot vanquish Indra and sets out with his kinsmen to conquer the celestial region.
events.one_line_summary: After Kashyapa's sacrifice, Vajranabha rejects his father's warning that he cannot vanquish Indra and sets out with his kinsmen to conquer the celestial region.

sources.source_excerpt: you will not be able to vanquish him but yourself will be killed... Vajrānābha did not approve of the words of Kashyapa... He first set out for conquering the region of the celestials

events.working_title: The Danava Princesses Arm Their Yadava Husbands || When Vajranabha orders the arrest of the young Yadava sons, Prabhavati hands Pradyumna a sword and blesses him with victory, while Chandravati and Gunavati arm Gada and Shamba.
events.one_line_summary: When Vajranabha orders the arrest of the young Yadava sons, Prabhavati hands Pradyumna a sword and blesses him with victory, while Chandravati and Gunavati arm Gada and Shamba.

sources.source_excerpt: Prabhāvati... handed over a sword to Rukshmini's son... saying, "Acquire victory"... Chandravati delightfully gave to Gada one Nishtringsha and Gunavati gave another such weapon to the highly powerful Shāmva

events.working_title: Pradyumna Fights with Ananta as Charioteer || Pradyumna creates a celestial car with the thousand-headed serpent Ananta as charioteer and devastates the Asura host, while Indra sends his own car, Airavata and Jayanta to aid the Yadavas.
events.one_line_summary: Pradyumna creates a celestial car with the thousand-headed serpent Ananta as charioteer and devastates the Asura host, while Indra sends his own car, Airavata and Jayanta to aid the Yadavas.

sources.source_excerpt: Pradyumna... created a car with his Māyā. He made the thousand-headed Nāga Ananta... his charioteer... he began to move about in the midst of the Asura army... three fourths of the Asuras were killed

events.working_title: Pradyumna Duels Vajranabha || Riding Garuda, Pradyumna wounds Vajranabha, who in turn fells him with a club; the sound of Krishna's Panchajanya conch revives the fallen hero.
events.one_line_summary: Riding Garuda, Pradyumna wounds Vajranabha, who in turn fells him with a club; the sound of Krishna's Panchajanya conch revives the fallen hero.

sources.source_excerpt: The highly powerful Vrajranābha was wounded on the breast with a club by the high-souled Krishna's son... Pradyumna, vomitted blood and lost his conciousness... At the sound of that Panchanjanya... Pradyumna revived and stood up

events.working_title: Pradyumna Slays Vajranabha with Krishna's Discus || Krishna's discus comes into Pradyumna's hand, and with it he severs Vajranabha's head, while Gada slays Sunabha and Shamba destroys the remaining Asuras.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna's discus comes into Pradyumna's hand, and with it he severs Vajranabha's head, while Gada slays Sunabha and Shamba destroys the remaining Asuras.

sources.source_excerpt: his discus... came into the hand of his son... that discus, discharged by Nārāyana's son, separated Vajranābha's head from his body... The dreadful Sunābha... was killed by Gada

events.working_title: Indra and Krishna Install the Four Young Kings || Indra and Krishna divide Vajranabha's conquered kingdom into four parts and anoint the four young princes — Vijaya and the sons of Pradyumna, Shamba and Gada — as kings of the Vajra realm.
events.one_line_summary: Indra and Krishna divide Vajranabha's conquered kingdom into four parts and anoint the four young princes — Vijaya and the sons of Pradyumna, Shamba and Gada — as kings of the Vajra realm.

sources.source_excerpt: Indra and Upendra divided Vajranābha's kingdom into four parts... one-fourth... to Jayanta's son Vijaya, one-fourth to Pradyumna's son, one-fourth to Shāmva's son and the remaining one-fourth to Gada's son Chandraprabha

events.working_title: Vishwakarma Adorns Dwarka for Krishna || At Indra's request, the celestial architect Vishwakarma beautifies Dwarka after Amaravati, building golden palaces for each of Krishna's queens, and Krishna enters the adorned city.
events.one_line_summary: At Indra's request, the celestial architect Vishwakarma beautifies Dwarka after Amaravati, building golden palaces for each of Krishna's queens, and Krishna enters the adorned city.

sources.source_excerpt: the king of gods sent for the celestial Architect and said:—"...do you... make his beautiful city more exquisite..." Vishwakarmā adorned it after Amarāvati... he built a highly beautiful golden palace... for Rukshmini

events.working_title: Krishna Returns to Dwarka and Honors Naraka's Captive Maidens || Krishna re-enters Dwarka with the Parijata and the treasure-mountain, blows the Panchajanya to the citizens' joy, and honors the maidens freed from Naraka's house with garments, riches and homes.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna re-enters Dwarka with the Parijata and the treasure-mountain, blows the Panchajanya to the citizens' joy, and honors the maidens freed from Naraka's house with garments, riches and homes.

sources.source_excerpt: he blew his conch the sound of which made the hairs of his enemies stand erect... honored all the maidens he had brought from Naraka's house with raiments, ornaments, maid-servants, riches... Krishna allotted to each of those women, separate houses, tanks, and gardens

events.working_title: The Yogamaya Appears Before Krishna and Rama || The illusory daughter of Yashoda — the goddess born the same moment as Krishna — appears before Krishna and Rama, who embrace her and seat her between them as the Vrishni women worship her.
events.one_line_summary: The illusory daughter of Yashoda — the goddess born the same moment as Krishna — appears before Krishna and Rama, who embrace her and seat her between them as the Vrishni women worship her.

sources.source_excerpt: the illusory daughter of Yashoda... appeared before Krishna and Rāma... Mādhava approached her... and held her by the hand. The highly powerful Rāma too... embraced her and smelt her head... The Vrishni women then saw her between her two brothers Rāma and Krishna

events.working_title: Narada Prophesies the Ocean Will Swallow Dwarka || Before departing, Narada prophesies that Krishna, having fulfilled the gods' work, will let the ocean inundate Dwarka and Bhogavati, and will be united with Narayana.
events.one_line_summary: Before departing, Narada prophesies that Krishna, having fulfilled the gods' work, will let the ocean inundate Dwarka and Bhogavati, and will be united with Narayana.

sources.source_excerpt: the highly illustrious Krishna will make the ocean devour the cities Bhogavati... and Dwārakā... The ocean, conversant with the desire of Krishna... will inundate this city of Dwārakā

events.working_title: Mayavati Reveals the Truth to Pradyumna || When the grown Pradyumna recoils at Mayavati's advances, she reveals he is not her son but the child of Rukmini and Vasudeva, stolen by Shamvara, and that she is his former wife.
events.one_line_summary: When the grown Pradyumna recoils at Mayavati's advances, she reveals he is not her son but the child of Rukmini and Vasudeva, stolen by Shamvara, and that she is his former wife.

sources.source_excerpt: You are not my son, nor Shamvara is your father... you are the delightful son of Vāsudeva and Rukshmini... you were stolen by my powerful husband... I seek you as my lover, because I have not given birth to you

events.working_title: Pradyumna Fells Shamvara's Standard to Provoke Him || To draw out the Danava who stole him, Pradyumna strikes down Shamvara's lion-emblazoned standard, and the enraged Shamvara sends his hundred sons to kill him.
events.one_line_summary: To draw out the Danava who stole him, Pradyumna strikes down Shamvara's lion-emblazoned standard, and the enraged Shamvara sends his hundred sons to kill him.

sources.source_excerpt: I will strike down the wonderful standard... having the emblem of a lion which stands like the mount Sumeru on his gate... Hearing of the spoliation of his standard... Shamvara, filled with anger, ordered his sons... "do you soon kill Rukshmini's son"

events.working_title: Pradyumna Slays the Hundred Sons of Shamvara || In a single battle, Pradyumna cuts down all hundred of Shamvara's sons who come against him, and stands victorious awaiting the father.
events.one_line_summary: In a single battle, Pradyumna cuts down all hundred of Shamvara's sons who come against him, and stands victorious awaiting the father.

sources.source_excerpt: he killed the ten highly powerful sons of Shamvara... Having thus slain one hundred sons of Shamvara, all good bow men, he stood in the battle field desirous of fighting

events.working_title: Pradyumna Slays Shamvara's Four Ministers || Pradyumna slays the four Danava ministers — Durdhara, Ketumali, Shatruhanta and Pramardana — one by one, and their army flees in terror.
events.one_line_summary: Pradyumna slays the four Danava ministers — Durdhara, Ketumali, Shatruhanta and Pramardana — one by one, and their army flees in terror.

sources.source_excerpt: he shot it at the breast of the short-lived Durdhara... with it before all he cut off Ketumāli's head... the heart of the highly powerful Shatruhantā was cut off... Kāma... crushed down Pramarddana with that club

events.working_title: Shamvara's Illusions and Pradyumna's Counters || Shamvara hurls illusory trees, stones, lions and a serpent-maya at Pradyumna, who counters each with fiery weapons and a Garuda illusion, to the applause of the gods.
events.one_line_summary: Shamvara hurls illusory trees, stones, lions and a serpent-maya at Pradyumna, who counters each with fiery weapons and a Garuda illusion, to the applause of the gods.

sources.source_excerpt: Shamvara... created a great illusory display by throwing on Pradyumna's car lions, tigers, bears, monkeys... Kāma however, with Gandharva weapons, cut them off into many pieces... Garudas began to move about and destroy the venomous serpents

events.working_title: Narada Reveals Pradyumna's True Identity and Arms Him || Sent by Indra, Narada reminds Pradyumna of his former birth as Kama, gives him the Vaishnava weapons and a coat of mail, and bids him slay Shamvara and reclaim his wife Mayavati.
events.one_line_summary: Sent by Indra, Narada reminds Pradyumna of his former birth as Kama, gives him the Vaishnava weapons and a coat of mail, and bids him slay Shamvara and reclaim his wife Mayavati.

sources.source_excerpt: Nārada... said to Pradyumna:—"...remember your pristine birth. O hero, you are Kāma... having killed Shamvara in the battle-field with Vaishnava weapons take your own wife Māyāvati and go to Dwārakā"

events.working_title: Narada's Riddle: Who Is Truly Great || When Narada cryptically hails Krishna as 'wonder and blessed' and Krishna answers 'presents', the puzzled kings ask the meaning; Narada recounts a journey from tortoise to Ganga, ocean, earth, mountains, Brahma, the Vedas and the Yajnas, each deferring to the next, until the riddle resolves in Vishnu with dakshina.
events.one_line_summary: When Narada cryptically hails Krishna as 'wonder and blessed' and Krishna answers 'presents', the puzzled kings ask the meaning; Narada recounts a journey from tortoise to Ganga, ocean, earth, mountains, Brahma, the Vedas and the Yajnas, each deferring to the next, until the riddle resolves in Vishnu with dakshina.

sources.source_excerpt: Nārada... said... "O thou of large arms, thou alone hast become an object of wonder to the gods"... Krishna, smilingly said:—"Yes I am an object of surprise and good luck, especially in the matter of presents"... Vishnu alone is the great wonder... great is a Yajna accompanied with presents

events.working_title: Garuda Quenches Bana's Protective Fire || As Bana's city-fire blazes out and robs the Yadavas of their lustre, Garuda assumes a thousand mouths, drinks the etherial Ganga and showers it down to extinguish the flames.
events.one_line_summary: As Bana's city-fire blazes out and robs the Yadavas of their lustre, Garuda assumes a thousand mouths, drinks the etherial Ganga and showers it down to extinguish the flames.
