sources.source_excerpt: Garuda... assumed a thousand mouths... drinking profuse water, he began to shower it on the fire... the fire was at once extinguished

events.working_title: Krishna Strikes Down Angira and the Fire-Gods || Bana's fire-gods, led by the chief Angira, attack Krishna on the way, and Krishna, cutting off Angira's mace, fells him with an arrow, putting the rest to flight.
events.one_line_summary: Bana's fire-gods, led by the chief Angira, attack Krishna on the way, and Krishna, cutting off Angira's mace, fells him with an arrow, putting the rest to flight.

sources.source_excerpt: cutting off his mace with crescent-shaped and sharpened arrows... Krishna... struck Angirā on the breast with a death-like-arrow. Thereat Angirā fell down bathed in blood... the four fire-gods... fled away to Vāna's city

events.working_title: Chitralekha Comes to Dwarka as Usha's Emissary || Usha's friend Chitralekha travels to Dwarka to bring Aniruddha back for her mistress, and secures Narada's blessing and the Tamasika power of illusion to carry out the abduction.
events.one_line_summary: Usha's friend Chitralekha travels to Dwarka to bring Aniruddha back for her mistress, and secures Narada's blessing and the Tamasika power of illusion to carry out the abduction.

sources.source_excerpt: Chitralekha... said to the celestial saint Nārada... "I have come here as a messenger for taking Aniruddha with me"... Nārada said to her... "Accept the Tāmasa learning which can infatuate all the worlds"

events.working_title: Aniruddha Routs Vana's Soldiers || When Vana discovers Usha living with Aniruddha and sends his soldiers to kill him, Aniruddha seizes a Parigha and single-handedly drives the Danava host from the field.
events.one_line_summary: When Vana discovers Usha living with Aniruddha and sends his soldiers to kill him, Aniruddha seizes a Parigha and single-handedly drives the Danava host from the field.

sources.source_excerpt: taking up a dreadful Parigha... he killed the Daityas... Having driven with Parigha the Dānavas from the battle-field the highly powerful hero Aniruddha delightfully set up a leonine shout

events.working_title: The Goddess Durga Releases Aniruddha from His Bonds || Imprisoned in Vana's city, Aniruddha hymns the goddess Katyayani, and Durga appears, cuts the serpent-nooses with her fingers, and consoles him, promising Krishna will sever Vana's thousand arms.
events.one_line_summary: Imprisoned in Vana's city, Aniruddha hymns the goddess Katyayani, and Durga appears, cuts the serpent-nooses with her fingers, and consoles him, promising Krishna will sever Vana's thousand arms.

sources.source_excerpt: the great goddess Durgā went where Aniruddha was kept in chains... with her fingers cut off the strong noose of serpents and then consoling Aniruddha said:—"...The holder of discus... will cut off the thousand arms of Vāna"

events.working_title: The Yadavas' Grief and Search for Aniruddha || Aniruddha's wives lament and the whole Yadava assembly falls into grief; Krishna broods over the disappearance, and messengers are sent out to search mountains, forests and every country in vain.
events.one_line_summary: Aniruddha's wives lament and the whole Yadava assembly falls into grief; Krishna broods over the disappearance, and messengers are sent out to search mountains, forests and every country in vain.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna... said:—"...where has Aniruddha been exiled?... I will in battle kill him with his own people who has put on my head this foot covered with ashes"... the messengers... said:—"...we saw Aniruddha nowhere"

events.working_title: Narada Reveals Aniruddha's Captivity by Vana || Narada arrives at the anxious court and tells Krishna that Vana's daughter Usha, with Chitralekha, took Aniruddha, that Vana bound him with serpent-shafts, and that he lives imprisoned awaiting rescue.
events.one_line_summary: Narada arrives at the anxious court and tells Krishna that Vana's daughter Usha, with Chitralekha, took Aniruddha, that Vana bound him with serpent-shafts, and that he lives imprisoned awaiting rescue.

sources.source_excerpt: Nārada... said:—"...Vāna... has a daughter by name Ushā. For her, the Apsara Chitralekhā has taken away Kāma's son... Vāna... has fettered the highly powerful Aniruddha with serpentine shafts... Aniruddha is not still deprived of life"

events.working_title: Jvara Consumes Baladeva; Krishna Saves Him || The fever-demon Jvara, with three legs, three heads and six arms, hurls a burning weapon that consumes Baladeva; Krishna embraces his brother and by his touch saves him from being burnt.
events.one_line_summary: The fever-demon Jvara, with three legs, three heads and six arms, hurls a burning weapon that consumes Baladeva; Krishna embraces his brother and by his touch saves him from being burnt.

sources.source_excerpt: Jvara... hurled his consuming weapon which fell on his breast... Krishna's elder brother was however being consumed... Haladhara said to Krishna:—"...I am being consumed"... he embraced Halāyudha... He was then saved by loving Krishna from being burnt

events.working_title: Krishna Grapples with Jvara || Krishna challenges Jvara and, bearing the demon's burning weapon and blows, grinds him with his arms in a fearful struggle.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna challenges Jvara and, bearing the demon's burning weapon and blows, grinds him with his arms in a fearful struggle.

sources.source_excerpt: the powerful Krishna... experienced a burning sensation for a few moments. Immediately after the fire was put out... Jvara... struck Krishna on the neck... grinded the sky-ranging Jvara adorned with golden ornaments with his arms

events.working_title: Jvara Possesses Krishna; Krishna Expels Him || The released Jvara enters Krishna's body and enfeebles him; Krishna creates a dreadful counter-Jvara from his own energy, which seizes and drags the fever out of his body.
events.one_line_summary: The released Jvara enters Krishna's body and enfeebles him; Krishna creates a dreadful counter-Jvara from his own energy, which seizes and drags the fever out of his body.

sources.source_excerpt: Jvara... entered into it (Krishna's body)... Krishna... created a dreadful Jvara, highly terrible unto creatures... Catching hold, by force, of the former Jvara the one, created by Krishna, presented it before him... driven out that Jvara from his body

events.working_title: Krishna Spares Jvara and Grants Him Boons || Commanded by an invisible voice, Krishna spares Jvara and grants him boons — that he alone be the world's fever, divided into forms to afflict beasts, plants and mankind.
events.one_line_summary: Commanded by an invisible voice, Krishna spares Jvara and grants him boons — that he alone be the world's fever, divided into forms to afflict beasts, plants and mankind.

sources.source_excerpt: an invisible voice was heard in the sky:—"...do not kill this Jvara... he is worthy of being protected by thee"... Jvara said:—"...I pray from thee for this boon only that I may be the only Jvara in this world"... dividing yourself into four parts... you are to live amongst mankind

events.working_title: Shiva and Kartikeya Enter the Battle for Vana || As Vana's army flees, Shiva, eyes red with anger, ascends his lion-drawn car surrounded by his ghostly host, and Kartikeya joins him to protect Vana.
events.one_line_summary: As Vana's army flees, Shiva, eyes red with anger, ascends his lion-drawn car surrounded by his ghostly host, and Kartikeya joins him to protect Vana.

sources.source_excerpt: Siva... had his eyes reddened with anger. And in order to protect Vāna, he stood on his lustrous car... Kumāra too ascended a car... Powerful Rudra, ascending a car drawn by lions... drove where Hari was

events.working_title: Kartikeya Duels the Yadavas; Krishna Counters Brahmashira || Kartikeya rides out and strikes Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna; when he discharges the world-destroying Brahmashira weapon, Krishna's discus blots out its lustre, and he strikes down Kartikeya's burning Sakti.
events.one_line_summary: Kartikeya rides out and strikes Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna; when he discharges the world-destroying Brahmashira weapon, Krishna's discus blots out its lustre, and he strikes down Kartikeya's burning Sakti.

sources.source_excerpt: Guha (Kārtikeya) drove towards Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna and struck them with hundreds of dreadful and sharpened arrows... Keshava took up his discus the destroyer and counteractor of all weapons... that discus... clouded, with its lustre, that of Brahmashira weapon

events.working_title: Kottavi Intervenes to Save Kartikeya || As Krishna raises his discus against Kartikeya, the naked goddess Kottavi, sent by Mahadeva, intervenes, and Krishna, unable to strike before her, puts away his discus.
events.one_line_summary: As Krishna raises his discus against Kartikeya, the naked goddess Kottavi, sent by Mahadeva, intervenes, and Krishna, unable to strike before her, puts away his discus.

sources.source_excerpt: the beautiful Kottavi, at the mandate of Mahādeva, came there naked for protecting Kumāra... Seeing the goddess stand before Kumāra the large-armed Krishna was baffled... put away his discus

events.working_title: Vana Vaunts and Fights Krishna || Vana boasts of his thousand arms, but Krishna answers and, with the Sarnga bow, sunders Vana's car, horses and standard, then strips him of crown, mail, bow and shield until he swoons.
events.one_line_summary: Vana boasts of his thousand arms, but Krishna answers and, with the Sarnga bow, sunders Vana's car, horses and standard, then strips him of crown, mail, bow and shield until he swoons.

sources.source_excerpt: Vāna... said... "how you will be able to fight with me who have a thousand arms?"... Keshava sundered Vāna's car, with horses and standards, into pieces... separated from Vāna's person his highly lustrous crown, coat of mail, bow and shield... Vāna lost his consciousness

events.working_title: Kottavi Again Intercedes; Krishna Vows to Cut Vana's Arms || When the naked goddess Kottavi again stands between them to honour her boon of protection to Vana, Krishna vows to cut off Vana's thousand arms, leaving only two, while sparing his life.
events.one_line_summary: When the naked goddess Kottavi again stands between them to honour her boon of protection to Vana, Krishna vows to cut off Vana's thousand arms, leaving only two, while sparing his life.

sources.source_excerpt: Lamvā... appeared naked before Vasudeva... said:—"...I conferred on him a boon saying that I would protect him"... Krishna... said:—"...I will forsooth cut off to-day his thousand arms... Your son will live even if Vāna has two arms"

events.working_title: Shiva Intercedes for Vana; Vana Dances and Wins Boons || Shiva intercedes for Vana's life, Krishna withdraws his discus, and the armless Vana, bidden by Nandi, dances before Shiva and receives boons, becoming the Pramatha chief Mahakala.
events.one_line_summary: Shiva intercedes for Vana's life, Krishna withdraws his discus, and the armless Vana, bidden by Nandi, dances before Shiva and receives boons, becoming the Pramatha chief Mahakala.

sources.source_excerpt: Mahadeva said:—"...I have promised Vāna protection... desist"... Krishna... "I withdraw my discus. At thy request Vāna will live"... Vāna... began to dance... Mahādeva... said:—"I am pleased with you... pray for a boon"

events.working_title: Krishna Celebrates Aniruddha's Wedding and Grants the Kingdom to Kumbhanda || Krishna celebrates Aniruddha and Usha's wedding, and confers Vana's kingdom on the minister Kumbhanda, who had counselled mercy toward Aniruddha.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna celebrates Aniruddha and Usha's wedding, and confers Vana's kingdom on the minister Kumbhanda, who had counselled mercy toward Aniruddha.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna... said:—"...You will now become the king of this kingdom. I confer this kingdom on you"... Janārddana celebrated the wedding festival of Aniruddha

events.working_title: Krishna Fights Varuna for the Celestial Cows || Seeking Vana's celestial kine in Varuna's charge for Satyabhama, Krishna routs Varuna's army and battles Varuna, whose Varuna-weapon is consumed by Krishna's Vaishnava weapon.
events.one_line_summary: Seeking Vana's celestial kine in Varuna's charge for Satyabhama, Krishna routs Varuna's army and battles Varuna, whose Varuna-weapon is consumed by Krishna's Vaishnava weapon.

sources.source_excerpt: the kine of Vāna... drinking whose milk a man becomes immortal... Varuna's... army... were all routed by the high-souled Keshava... with the energy of Vaishnava weapon that water was ablaze

events.working_title: Varuna Pleads His Promise; Krishna Relents || Varuna pleads his vow to Vana never to part with the cows, and Krishna, honouring his truthfulness, releases both Varuna and the cows and returns to Dwarka amid the rejoicing citizens.
events.one_line_summary: Varuna pleads his vow to Vana never to part with the cows, and Krishna, honouring his truthfulness, releases both Varuna and the cows and returns to Dwarka amid the rejoicing citizens.

sources.source_excerpt: Varuna said... "I had formerly promised, that if alive I would never give away these kine"... Krishna... said:—"...you are truthful and therefore for pleasing you I let loose Vāna's cows. And you too are released"

events.working_title: Usha Is Welcomed into the Yadu Family || Back in Dwarka, Ahuka bids a festival; Usha is conducted to Aniruddha's house amid benedictions, and Devaki, Revati and Rukmini welcome her with tears of joy, closing the Vana episode.
events.one_line_summary: Back in Dwarka, Ahuka bids a festival; Usha is conducted to Aniruddha's house amid benedictions, and Devaki, Revati and Rukmini welcome her with tears of joy, closing the Vana episode.

sources.source_excerpt: Ahuka said... "Do thou undertake a great festival for Aniruddha's return and wedding"... Devaki, Revati and... Rukshmini shed tears of joy... Ushā... lived in their palace and enjoyed best of happiness

events.working_title: Krishna Shatters the Rock-Shower with Indra's Thunderbolt || Buried under torrents of rocks hurled by Salwa's Danavas, Krishna wields Indra's thunderbolt and destroys the entire mass of crags, then resumes the fight.
events.one_line_summary: Buried under torrents of rocks hurled by Salwa's Danavas, Krishna wields Indra's thunderbolt and destroys the entire mass of crags, then resumes the fight.

sources.source_excerpt: torrents of rocks falling upon me covered me up, and I began to grow like an ant-hill ... And then wielding the thunderbolt, that favourite (weapon) of Indra, capable of riving stones, I destroyed that entire mass of crags!

events.working_title: Krishna Seizes Kalayavana's Host || Having destroyed Kalayavana by stratagem, Krishna captures his army of horses, elephants and cars, and delivers it to Ugrasena, freeing the Yadava race from fear of invasion.
events.one_line_summary: Having destroyed Kalayavana by stratagem, Krishna captures his army of horses, elephants and cars, and delivers it to Ugrasena, freeing the Yadava race from fear of invasion.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishńa having by this stratagem destroyed his enemy, returned to Mathurá, and took captive his army, rich in horses, elephants and cars, which he conducted to Dwáraká, and delivered to Ugrasena.

events.working_title: Krishna Restores Aditi's Earrings || Krishna restores the recovered earrings to Aditi, who blesses him; Satyabhama is promised unfading beauty.
events.one_line_summary: Krishna restores the recovered earrings to Aditi, who blesses him; Satyabhama is promised unfading beauty.

sources.source_excerpt: on beholding Adití, paid his respects to her, along with Śakra; and, presenting to her her own earrings, informed her of the destruction of the demon Naraka.

events.variant_notes: Cross-ref: Parijata-uprooting cluster (bp10c_046 etc.); VP's separate earrings-restoration beat.

events.working_title: Krishna Arrives at Indraprastha for the Rajasuya
events.one_line_summary: Krishna arrives at Indraprastha, where Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, the twins and Kunti embrace him with overflowing love.

sources.source_excerpt: Hearing of Krishna's arrival, Yudhishthira comes out with his preceptors and friends, and embraces Krishna again and again with tears of joy. Bhima, Arjuna and the twins also embrace him; Kunti rises from her couch and embraces her nephew, and Draupadi honors the queens Rukmini, Satyabhama, Bhadra and Jambavati. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 22-44)

Hari (Krishna) ... having appointed Vasudeva to the command of the (Yadava) army, and bringing with him for the king Yudhishthira just a large mass of treasure; entered that excellent city of cities. Khandava, himself surrounded by a mighty host and filling the atmosphere with the rattle of his chariot-wheels.

events.variant_notes: Bhagavata (10.71) frames the arrival as an emotional reunion/embrace; Mahabharata (2.32) frames it as arriving with treasure.

events.working_title: Yudhishthira Requests the Rajasuya and Krishna Approves
events.one_line_summary: Yudhishthira asks Krishna's permission and blessing to perform the Rajasuya, and Krishna approves, promising to win the kings of the earth for him.

sources.source_excerpt: Yudhishthira declares his wish to perform the purifying Rajasuya sacrifice and asks Krishna, the lord of all, to bring it about. Krishna approves, saying that after conquering all the kings and gathering the requisites the sacrifice should be performed, and that none can surpass Yudhishthira in splendor, not even the gods. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-10)

Krishna, extolling his virtues, said.--'Thou, O tiger among kings, deservest imperial dignity. Let, therefore, the great sacrifice be performed by thee. And if thou performest that sacrifice an obtainest its fruit we all shall regard ourselves as crowned with success.'

events.variant_notes: Same permission moment; Bhagavata 10.72 vs Mahabharata 2.32.

events.working_title: Krishna Receives the First Honor (Arghya) at the Rajasuya
events.one_line_summary: Sahadeva declares Krishna alone worthy of the highest honor at the sacrifice, and Yudhishthira washes Krishna's feet and worships him before all.

sources.source_excerpt: Sahadeva declares that Krishna alone, the lord of the Satvatas in whom all deities and all sacrifice abide, deserves the foremost honor. At this the whole assembly approves, and Yudhishthira, overwhelmed with love, washes Krishna's feet, bears the water on his head, and worships him with garments and jewels. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 17-28)

Bhishma the son of Santanu, judged it by his intelligence that on earth Krishna was the foremost of all. ... Sahadeva endued with great prowess duly presented the first Arghya of excellent ingredients unto Krishna of the Vrishni race. Krishna also accepted it according to the forms of the ordinance. But Sisupala could not bear to see that worship offered unto Vasudeva.

events.variant_notes: Bhagavata credits Sahadeva's declaration; Mahabharata credits Bhishma's direction.

events.working_title: Krishna Pacifies the Yadavas After Arjuna's Abduction of Subhadra
events.one_line_summary: Arjuna, disguised as a renunciant, wins Krishna's sister Subhadra and carries her off; when Balarama grows angry, Krishna pacifies him and he sends wedding gifts.

sources.source_excerpt: Arjuna, on pilgrimage, hears that Balarama intends to give their sister Subhadra to Duryodhana, and going to Dwaraka disguised as a tridandi renunciant, wins Subhadra's heart and carries her off on his chariot during a festival. Balarama grows furious, but Krishna pacifies him, and Balarama, appeased, sends rich wedding gifts for the bride and groom. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 1-11)

Vasudeva uttered these words pregnant with deep import and consistent with true morality. Gudakesa (the conqueror of sleep or he of the curly hair), by what he hath done, hath not insulted our family. He hath without doubt, rather enhanced our respect. ... I think Arjuna, seeing these faults in all the other methods took the maiden away by force, according to the ordinance. This alliance is very proper. ... go ye cheerfully after Dhananjaya and by conciliation stop him and bring him back. ... Hearing, O monarch, those words of Vasudeva, they did as he directed. Stopped by them, Arjuna returned to Dwaraka and was united in marriage with Subhadra.

events.variant_notes: Bhagavata (10.86) condenses abduction + pacification; Mahabharata (1.223) details the defense of the alliance.

events.working_title: Krishna Sends Wedding Gifts to the Pandavas After Draupadi's Marriage
events.one_line_summary: After the Pandavas' marriage to Draupadi, Krishna sends them gold ornaments, costly robes, gems, elephants, horses, and crores of gold coins, which Yudhishthira accepts with joy.

sources.source_excerpt: After the sons of Pandu had been married, Hari (Krishna) sent unto them (as presents) various gold ornaments set with pearls and black gems (lapis lazuli). And Madhava (Krishna) also sent unto them costly robes manufactured in various countries ... He also sent them vessels by hundreds, set with gems and diamonds. ... The slayer of Madhu, of immeasurable soul, also sent them coins of pure gold by crores upon crores in separate heaps. And Yudhishthira the just, desirous of gratifying Govinda, accepted all those presents with great joy.

After the sons of Pandu had been married, Hari (Krishna) sent unto them (as presents) various gold ornaments set with pearls and black gems (lapis lazuli). And Madhava (Krishna) also sent unto them costly robes manufactured in various countries... The slayer of Madhu, of immeasurable soul, also sent them coins of pure gold by crores upon crores in separate heaps. And Yudhishthira the just, desirous of gratifying Govinda, accepted all those presents with great joy.

events.variant_notes: Duplicate events from the same Ganguli translation (1.201).

events.working_title: The Yadavas Journey to Prabhasa
events.one_line_summary: Seeing the terrible omens rising in Dwaraka, Krishna tells the Yadava elders to leave at once for the holy tirtha of Prabhasa, and they cross the sea in boats and chariots to worship there.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna said: 'These dreadful omens are the banners of death; not for a moment should we remain here. Let the women, children and elders go to Shankhoddhara, and let us go to Prabhasa where the Sarasvati flows westward.' The Yadava elders answered 'so be it' and crossed over to Prabhasa. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 4-9)

Uddhava said: 'Then, after some months, the Vrishnis, Bhojas and Andhakas went joyfully to Prabhasa, deluded by fate; there they bathed, honoured the gods and rishis, and gave the brahmins cows, gold, silver, beds, garments, chariots, elephants and lands.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-27)

Hrishikesa, summoning the Yadavas, said unto them these words: 'The fourteenth lunation has been made the fifteenth by Rahu once more... It has once more appeared, it seems, for our destruction.' ... Vasudeva, having said so, endeavoured to bring about those occurrences which would make Gandhari's words true. That chastiser of foes commanded the Vrishnis to make a pilgrimage to some sacred water.

events.variant_notes: Command (Bhagavata 11.30, Mahabharata 16.2) and execution (Bhagavata 3.3) of the same journey.

events.working_title: The Hunter Jara Shoots Krishna's Foot
events.one_line_summary: After the Yadavas' destruction, Krishna sits in meditation at the foot of a pippala tree; the hunter Jara, mistaking Krishna's foot for a deer's, shoots it with the arrow made from the mace's iron, then, seeing the four-armed Lord, falls at his feet in terror.
locations: at the foot of a pippala tree

sources.source_excerpt: Seated at the foot of a pippala tree, four-armed and radiant, Krishna placed his right foot upon his thigh; the hunter Jara, taking the foot for a deer's face, pierced it with the arrow fashioned from the mace's iron. Seeing the four-armed Lord, the terrified hunter fell at his feet, begging forgiveness. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26, 31-34)

Then came there a hunter, named Jará, whose arrow was tipped with a blade made of the piece of iron of the club... beholding from a distance the foot of Krishńa, he mistook it for part of a deer, and shooting his arrow, lodged it in the sole... Then the illustrious Krishńa... abandoned his mortal body.

Having restrained all his senses, speech, and mind, Krishna laid himself down in high Yoga. A fierce hunter of the name of Jara then came there, desirous of deer. The hunter, mistaking Keshava, who was stretched on the earth in high Yoga, for a deer, pierced him at the heel with a shaft and quickly came to that spot for capturing his prey.

events.variant_notes: Vishnu Purana (5.37) condenses the shooting with the forgiveness and departure.

events.working_title: Krishna's Final Departure / Ascension
events.one_line_summary: As Brahma, Shiva and the hosts of gods watch, Krishna, seeing Brahma before him, closes his lotus eyes, draws his opulences into himself, consumes his body with the fire of yoga, and enters his own abode, his path unfathomable even to the gods.

sources.source_excerpt: Brahma, Shiva, Indra, the sages and the hosts of gods came, eager to see the Lord's departure, raining flowers and singing his deeds. Krishna, seeing Brahma, gathered his opulences into himself, closed his lotus eyes, consumed his body with the fire of yoga, and entered his own abode, while the gods, amazed, could not trace his path. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

Coming up, Jara beheld a man dressed in yellow robes, rapt in Yoga and endued with many arms. Regarding himself an offender, and filled with fear, he touched the feet of Keshava. The high-souled one comforted him and then ascended upwards, filling the entire welkin with splendour. When he reached Heaven, Vasava and the twin Ashvinis and Rudra and the Adityas... advanced to receive him.

events.variant_notes: Mahabharata's account also includes comforting the hunter Jara.

events.working_title: The Sea Swallows Dwaraka
events.one_line_summary: After Krishna's departure, his queens and family ascend the funeral pyres, Arjuna performs the last rites, and the sea floods and swallows Dwaraka — all but the Lord's own dwelling; Arjuna leads the survivors to Indraprastha and installs Vajra.

sources.source_excerpt: Daruka told Vasudeva and Ugrasena of the destruction; Devaki, Rohini and Vasudeva, seeing neither Krishna nor Balarama, gave up their lives in grief, and the queens, led by Rukmini, entered the fire. The sea swallowed Dwaraka, all but the Lord's own abode; and Arjuna, leading the surviving women, children and elders to Indraprastha, installed Vajra as king. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-24)

The eight queens of Krishńa... with Rukminí at their head, embraced the body of Hari, and entered the funeral fire... The ocean rose, and submerged the whole of Dwáraká, except alone the dwelling of the deity of the race of Yadu.

After all the people had set out, the ocean, that home of sharks and alligators, flooded Dwaraka, which still teemed with wealth of every kind, with its waters. Whatever portion of the ground was passed over, ocean immediately flooded over with his waters. Beholding this wonderful sight, the inhabitants of Dwaraka walked faster and faster, saying, 'Wonderful is the course of fate!'

events.variant_notes: Includes the queens' pyres and Arjuna's last rites; Bhagavata adds installing Vajra.

events.working_title: Krishna Visits the Pandavas at Indraprastha
events.one_line_summary: Krishna visits the Pandavas at Indraprastha, is joyously received by Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Draupadi and Kunti, and stays four months.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna came to Indraprastha to see the Pandavas; they rose at once, embraced him, and Kunti, weeping with love, said 'now we are protected, for you remember us.' Krishna stayed four months, delighting all. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-11)

events.variant_notes: Earlier visit (10.58); distinct from the Rajasuya arrival bp10d_006.

events.working_title: Krishna Weds Kalindi at the Yamuna
events.one_line_summary: While hunting with Arjuna, Krishna meets Kalindi, daughter of the Sun, doing penance at the Yamuna, and later weds her.

sources.source_excerpt: Arjuna, sent by Krishna, asked the beautiful maiden her name; she said 'I am Kalindi, daughter of Surya, doing penance to win Vishnu as husband'; Krishna took her on his chariot and later wed her at an auspicious time. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 12-28)

events.working_title: Krishna Grants the Khadava Forest to Agni
events.one_line_summary: Krishna, as Arjuna's charioteer, helps him give the Khadava forest to Agni, who bestows the Gandiva bow and inexhaustible quivers.

sources.source_excerpt: Dwelling there for the Pandavas' good, Krishna acted as Arjuna's charioteer when Arjuna gave the Khadava forest to Agni; pleased, Agni gave Arjuna the Gandiva bow, inexhaustible quivers and an invincible chariot, and the rescued Maya built the assembly hall. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 23-26)

events.variant_notes: Condensed Bhagavata account of the Khandava episode; cf. mb_a1_012 (Brahmana arrives), mb_a1_013 (Agni seeks help).

events.working_title: Narada Announces the Rajasuya
events.one_line_summary: Narada arrives at the assembly and announces that Yudhishthira will perform the Rajasuya sacrifice, requesting Krishna's consent and presence.

sources.source_excerpt: The divine sage Narada, radiant with matted tawny locks, appears in the assembly and is honored by Krishna. He announces that Krishna's cousin Yudhishthira, desiring imperial sovereignty, will worship Krishna with the Rajasuya sacrifice, and that Krishna should consent. Krishna then playfully asks Uddhava for his counsel. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 31-46)

events.variant_notes: Narada's announcement precedes the request; cf. bp10d_007/mb_a2_010.

events.working_title: The Pandavas Conquer the Directions
events.one_line_summary: Yudhishthira sends his four brothers to conquer the four quarters, and they return laden with tribute for the sacrifice.

sources.source_excerpt: Pleased, Yudhishthira dispatches his brothers on the conquest of the quarters — Sahadeva to the south, Nakula to the west, Arjuna to the north, and Bhima to the east. They vanquish the kings and bring back abundant wealth for the sacrifice. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 11-13)

events.variant_notes: Follows the Rajasuya permission; cf. bp10d_007.

events.working_title: The Rajasuya Completed
events.one_line_summary: Krishna completes the Rajasuya for Yudhishthira, gives the priests their fees, stays some months, and departs; only Duryodhana cannot bear the Pandavas' splendor.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, lord of the lords of yoga, completes the sacrifice, bestows ample fees on the priests, and after some months takes leave of the reluctant Yudhishthira and returns to his own city. All the assembled guests depart praising Krishna and the sacrifice, except the wicked Duryodhana, who could not endure the Pandavas' prosperity. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 46-52)

events.variant_notes: Rajasuya conclusion; cf. bp10d_015.

events.working_title: Duryodhana's Humiliation in Maya's Hall
events.one_line_summary: In the illusory assembly hall built by Maya, Duryodhana mistakes water for floor and falls; Bhima and the women laugh, and Duryodhana departs burning with shame and hatred.

sources.source_excerpt: In the wondrous hall built by Maya, Duryodhana mistakes a crystal floor for water and lifts his garment, then falls where he thought the floor was, deceived by the illusion. Bhima and the women laugh despite the king's restraint, and Duryodhana, humiliated and blazing with rage, departs in silence, while Krishna remains silent, intent on relieving the earth's burden. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 30-38)

events.variant_notes: Duryodhana's humiliation follows the sacrifice; cf. bp10d_018.

events.working_title: Krishna Rejoices as Arjuna Wins Draupadi
events.one_line_summary: Seeing Arjuna string the stiff bow and shoot the mark, Krishna is filled with joy and approaches the disguised Pandava with a white robe and a garland of flowers.

sources.source_excerpt: And Krishna beholding the mark shot and beholding Partha also like unto Indra himself, who had shot the mark, was filled with joy, and approached the son of Kunti with a white robe and a garland of flowers.

events.working_title: Krishna Stops the Angry Kings from Attacking the Pandavas
events.one_line_summary: When the insulted kings rush to attack Drupada and the Pandavas, Krishna declares that Draupadi has been justly won and persuades the monarchs to abandon the fight.

sources.source_excerpt: And Krishna, having beheld that feat of Bhima, believed them both to be the son of Kunti. And gently addressing the assembled monarchs, saying, 'This maiden hath been justly acquired (by the Brahmana),' he induced them to abandon the fight. Accomplished in battle, those monarchs then desisted from the fight.

events.working_title: Krishna and Balarama Meet the Pandavas at the Potter's House
events.one_line_summary: Suspecting the Pandavas to be alive, Krishna and Balarama come to the potter's house, touch Yudhishthira's and Kunti's feet, and warn the disguised brothers to keep hidden.

sources.source_excerpt: The hero of the Vrishni race (Krishna suspecting the five persons he had seen at the Swayamvara to be none else than the heroes of the Kuru race), came accompanied by the son of Rohini (Valadeva), to the house of the potter ... Then Vasudeva approaching that foremost of virtuous men--the son of Kunti--and touching the feet of that prince of the Ajamida race, said, 'I am Krishna.' ... And Ajatasatru ... asked, 'How, O Vasudeva, hast thou been able to trace us, as we are living in disguise?' And Vasudeva, smilingly answered, 'O king, fire, even if it is covered, can be known. ... And lest any of the monarchs recognise ye, let us return to our tent.'

events.working_title: Krishna Embraces Arjuna at Prabhasa and Hosts Him at Dwaraka
events.one_line_summary: During Arjuna's forest exile, Krishna learns of his arrival at Prabhasa and goes to meet him; the two friends, Nara and Narayana of old, embrace and Krishna hosts Arjuna at Dwaraka for many days.

sources.source_excerpt: Vibhatsu reached the sacred spot called Prabhasa. When the invisible Arjuna arrived at that sacred and delightful region, the slayer of Madhu (Krishna) heard of it. Madhava soon went there to see his friend, the son of Kunti. Krishna and Arjuna met together and embracing each other enquired after each other's welfare. Those dear friends, who were none else than the Rishis Nara and Narayana of old, sat down. ... he took up his abode there with Krishna for many days.

events.working_title: Krishna Counsels Arjuna to Abduct Subhadra
events.one_line_summary: At the Raivataka festival, Krishna notices Arjuna's love for his sister Subhadra and advises him to carry her away by force, the celebrated Kshatriya form of marriage.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna, observing Partha contemplate her with absorbed attention, said with a smile, 'How is this? Can the heart of one that rangeth the woods be agitated by the god of desire? This is my sister, O Partha ... Tell me if thy heart is fixed upon her, for I shall then speak to my father myself.' ... Vasudeva answered, 'O bull amongst men, self-choice hath been ordained for the marriage of Kshatriyas. But that is doubtful (in its consequences) ... In the case of Kshatriyas that are brave, a forcible abduction for purposes of marriage is applauded, as the learned have said. Therefore O Arjuna, carry away this my beautiful sister by force, for who knows what she may do at a self-choice.'

events.variant_notes: Krishna's counsel precedes the abduction; cf. bp10d_045/mb_a1_009.

events.working_title: Krishna Comes to Indraprastha Bearing Nuptial Gifts
events.one_line_summary: Hearing that Arjuna has reached Indraprastha with Subhadra, Krishna arrives with the Yadava host and presents the Pandavas with cars, cows, mares, mules, and damsels as nuptial gifts.

sources.source_excerpt: When that scorcher of foes, viz., Kesava of pure soul ... heard that the foremost of the Pandavas, viz., Arjuna, had reached his own excellent city of Indraprastha, he came thither accompanied by Rama and the other heroes ... bringing with them many nuptial presents. ... Krishna gave unto the Pandavas a thousand cars of gold furnished with rows of bells ... He also gave unto them ten thousand cows belonging to the country of Mathura ... Well-pleased, Janardana also gave them a thousand mares with gold harnesses and of colour white as the beams of the moon.

events.variant_notes: Nuptial gifts for Subhadra's marriage (distinct from Draupadi's wedding gifts); cf. bp10d_045.

events.working_title: Krishna Performs the Birth Rites of Abhimanyu
events.one_line_summary: Krishna stays on at Indraprastha with Arjuna, and when Subhadra bears Abhimanyu, Krishna performs the infant's birth rites; the child grows dear to him.

sources.source_excerpt: the high-souled Vasudeva remained there with Arjuna in the delightful city of Indraprastha. ... Then Subhadra, the favourite sister of Kesava, gave birth to an illustrious son ... And the son that Subhadra brought forth ... came to be called Abhimanyu. ... Upon his birth, Krishna performed the usual rites of infancy. The child began to grow up like the Moon of the bright fortnight.

events.working_title: Krishna and Arjuna Sport on the Yamuna and Receive a Mysterious Brahmana
events.one_line_summary: In summer Krishna and Arjuna go with friends to sport on the banks of the Yamuna, where a radiant Brahmana suddenly approaches the seated heroes.

sources.source_excerpt: After a few days, Vibhatsu, addressing Krishna, said, 'The summer days have set in, O Krishna! Therefore, let us go to the banks of the Yamuna. ...' Thereupon Vasudeva said, 'O son of Kunti, this is also my wish. ...' ... Unto Vasudeva and Dhananjaya happily sitting there like the Aswins in heaven, a certain Brahmana came. ... Beholding that foremost of Brahmanas blazing with splendour approach towards them both Arjuna and Vasudeva, hastily rising from their seats, stood, waiting (for his commands).

events.variant_notes: First beat of the Khandava episode; cf. mb_a1_013 (Agni reveals himself), bp10c_038 (Bhagavata summary).

events.working_title: Agni, in Brahman Disguise, Seeks Krishna and Arjuna's Help to Burn Khandava
events.one_line_summary: The Brahmana reveals himself as Agni and asks Krishna and Arjuna to shield him from Indra's rains so he can consume the Khandava forest.

sources.source_excerpt: Then that Brahmana addressed Arjuna and Vasudeva of the Satwata race, saying, 'Ye who are now staying so near unto Khandava are the two foremost of heroes on earth. I am a voracious Brahmana that always eateth much. ... I solicit you to gratify me by giving me sufficient food.' ... The illustrious Brahmana, thus replied to, said ... 'I do not desire to eat ordinary food. Know that I am Agni! ... This forest of Khandava is always protected by Indra. ... I pray you to prevent those showers from descending and any of the creatures from escaping, when I begin to consume this forest!'

events.variant_notes: Second beat of the Khandava episode; cf. mb_a1_012, bp10c_038.

events.working_title: Jarasandha Hurls His Mace toward Mathura
events.one_line_summary: Enraged by Kansa's death, Jarasandha whirls a mace ninety-nine times and hurls it toward Mathura where Krishna lives; the citizens inform Krishna of its fall.

sources.source_excerpt: Some time after when king Kansa was slain by Vasudeva, an enmity arose between him and Krishna. Then, O Bharata, the mighty king of Magadha from his city of Girivraja, whirling a mace ninety-nine times, hurled it towards Mathura. At that time Krishna of wonderful deeds was residing at Mathura. ... The citizens beholding the circumstance well, went unto Krishna and informed him of the fall of the mace.

events.working_title: Krishna Proposes Slaying Jarasandha as Prelude to the Rajasuya
events.one_line_summary: Krishna counsels that Jarasandha, unbeatable in battle by gods and asuras, must be slain in a bare-armed personal struggle, assigning policy to himself, strength to Bhima, and triumph to Arjuna.

sources.source_excerpt: In me is policy, in Bhima is strength and in Arjuna is triumph; and therefore, as prelude to performing the Rajasuya, we will certainly achieve the destruction of the ruler of Magadha.

events.variant_notes: VARIANT of the Rajasuya slaying-plan: Mahabharata attributes the proposal to Krishna himself; Bhagavata Purana 10.71 presents the same plan as Uddhava's counsel to Krishna. Attribution difference is material — kept as separate stories.

events.working_title: Krishna and the Pandavas Break the Chaityaka Peak
events.one_line_summary: Entering Girivraja not by the gate but by piercing the sacred Chaityaka peak, Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna break down the celebrated hill worshipped by the Magadhas.

sources.source_excerpt: On arriving then at the gate of the city, the brothers (instead of passing through it) began to pierce (with their shafts) the heart of the high Chaityaka peak that was worshipped by the race of Vrihadratha ... And attacking with their mighty arms that immovable and huge and high and old and celebrated peak always worshipped with perfumes and floral wreaths, those heroes broke it down.

events.working_title: Krishna Speaks for the Silent Disguised Brothers
events.one_line_summary: Received by Jarasandha, Krishna explains that his two companions observe a vow of silence until midnight, so he alone speaks for the disguised trio.

sources.source_excerpt: And addressing the monarch Krishna said,--'O king of kings these two are now in the observance of a vow. Therefore they will not speak. Silent they will remain till midnight After that hour they will speak with thee!'

events.working_title: Krishna Answers Jarasandha's Challenge about the Disguise
events.one_line_summary: When Jarasandha censures the disguised guests for entering by an improper gate, Krishna replies that a foe's abode is entered by the wrong gate and the foe's hospitality is refused.

sources.source_excerpt: These are the rules of the ordinance, viz., that an enemy's abode should be entered through a wrong gate and a friend's abode through the right one. And know, O monarch, that this also is our eternal vow that having entered the foe's abode for the accomplishment of our purpose, we accept not the worship offered to us!

events.working_title: Krishna Refrains from Slaying Jarasandha
events.one_line_summary: Remembering Brahma's command that Jarasandha is destined to die at Bhima's hands, Krishna withholds his own hand and leaves the king to Bhima.

sources.source_excerpt: the lord Sauri ever devoted to truth ... keeping in view the command of Brahma and remembering that the ruler of Magadha was destined to be slain in battle by Bhima and not by the descendant of Madhu (Yadavas), desired not to slay himself king Jarasandha.

events.working_title: Krishna Washes the Feet of the Brahmanas
events.one_line_summary: At the Rajasuya, Krishna the lord of all worlds humbly takes up the menial office of washing the feet of the Brahmanas.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna who was himself the centre of all worlds and round whom moved every creature, desirous of acquiring excellent fruits, was engaged at his own will in washing the feet of the Brahmanas.

events.variant_notes: Krishna's menial service at the sacrifice; precedes the first-honor episode; cf. bp10d_015/mb_a2_012.

events.working_title: Shishupala Incites the Kings to Battle
events.one_line_summary: Shishupala rallies the angry monarchs to obstruct the sacrifice, and Krishna perceives that the assembled kings are preparing for a rush.

sources.source_excerpt: Upon Krishna having received the first worship, Sunitha (Sisupala) ... said,--'When I am here to head ye all, what are ye thinking of now? Arrayed let us stand in battle against the assembled Vrishnis and the Pandavas?' ... Krishna then understood that the vast sea of monarchs with its countless waves of troops was preparing for a terrific rush.

events.variant_notes: Follows Shishupala's outburst; cf. bp10d_016/mb_a2_013.

events.working_title: Bhishma Foretells That Krishna Will Destroy Shishupala
events.one_line_summary: As Yudhishthira fears for his sacrifice, Bhishma declares the kings mere barking dogs before the sleeping lion of the Vrishnis, and that Vishnu has resolved to take back Shishupala's energy.

sources.source_excerpt: As dogs in a pack approaching the lion that is asleep bark together, so are all these lords of earth. ... Assuredly, O Bharata Vishnu hath been desirous of taking back unto himself the energy that existeth in this Sisupala.

events.variant_notes: Bhishma's foretelling within the Shishupala episode; cf. bp10d_016.

events.working_title: Krishna Grants Shishupala's Mother the Boon of a Hundred Offences
events.one_line_summary: When the frightened queen begs a boon, Krishna promises to pardon a hundred offences of Shishupala for her sake, a promise that now nears its limit.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna then said, 'O aunt, even when he will deserve to be slain, I will pardon an hundred offences of his. Grieve thou not.'

events.variant_notes: The hundred-offences boon, now expiring; cf. bp10d_017.

events.working_title: Draupadi Invokes Krishna as She Is Dragged and Disrobed
events.one_line_summary: As Dussasana drags her before the assembly and strips her, Draupadi cries out to Govinda, Kesava and Janarddana to rescue her from the Kaurava ocean.

sources.source_excerpt: 'O Govinda, O thou who dwellest in Dwaraka, O Krishna, O thou who art fond of cow-herdesses (of Vrindavana). O Kesava, seest thou not that the Kauravas are humiliating me. O Lord, O husband of Lakshmi, O Lord of Vraja (Vrindavana), O destroyer of all afflictions, O Janarddana, rescue me who am sinking in the Kaurava Ocean.'

events.variant_notes: Invocation beat; cf. mb_a2_020.

events.working_title: Krishna Protects Draupadi with Endless Robes
events.one_line_summary: Moved by Draupadi's call, Krishna comes to her aid from compassion; the unseen Dharma covers her so that as each garment is dragged off another appears, hundreds of robes protecting her honour.

sources.source_excerpt: Hearing the words of Draupadi, Krishna was deeply moved. And leaving his seat, the benevolent one from compassion, arrived there on foot. ... the illustrious Dharma, remaining unseen, covered her with excellent clothes of many hues. And, O monarch as the attire of Draupadi was being dragged, after one was taken off, another of the same kind, appeared covering her. ... owing to the protection of Dharma, hundreds upon hundreds of robes of many hues came off Draupadi's person.

events.variant_notes: Protection beat; cf. mb_a2_019.

events.working_title: Krishna Vows the Earth Shall Drink the Blood of the Pandavas' Foes
events.one_line_summary: Visiting the exiled Pandavas in the forest, an enraged Krishna vows that the earth shall drink the blood of Duryodhana, Karna, Dussasana and Sakuni, and that Yudhishthira will be reinstalled on the throne.

sources.source_excerpt: Kesava mournfully said, 'The earth shall drink the blood of Duryodhana and Karna, of Dussasana and the wicked Sakuni! Slaying these in battle and defeating their followers along with their royal allies, will we all install Yudhishthira the just on the throne! The wicked deserve to be slain! Verily, this is eternal morality.'

events.variant_notes: Forest-visit vow; parallel to pre-war vow in mb_b_001/mb_b_002.

events.working_title: Arjuna Pacifies the Wrathful Krishna
events.one_line_summary: When Krishna, inflamed by the Pandavas' wrongs, seems bent on consuming all creatures, Arjuna recites his former divine feats to calm him, and Krishna answers that he and Arjuna are Nara and Narayana.

sources.source_excerpt: when on account of the wrongs of Pritha's sons, Janardana had thus got into a passion, and seemed bent upon consuming all created things, Arjuna exerted himself to pacify him. ... 'Thou art mine and I am thine, while all that is mine is thine also! ... O thou irrepressible one, thou art Nara and I am Narayana or Hari!'

events.working_title: Krishna Promises Draupadi She Will Be Queen Again
events.one_line_summary: To the weeping Draupadi, Krishna vows that the wives of her enemies shall weep over their slain husbands and that she will once more be queen of kings, his words never futile.

sources.source_excerpt: Vasudeva then spake unto the weeping Draupadi as follows, 'O fair lady, the wives of those with whom thou art angry, shall weep even like thee, beholding their husbands dead on the ground, weltering in blood ... I promise thou shalt (once more) be the queen of kings! The heavens might fall, or the Himavat might split, the earth might be rent, or the waters of the ocean might dry up, but my words shall never be futile!'

events.variant_notes: Forest-visit promise; parallel to pre-war vow mb_b_002.

events.working_title: Krishna Laments His Absence from the Dice Game
events.one_line_summary: Krishna tells Yudhishthira that had he been present at Dwarka he would have prevented the dice game by counsel or force, and that his absence while fighting Salwa caused the Pandavas' calamity.

sources.source_excerpt: Vasudeva said, O lord of earth, if I had been present at Dwaraka, then, O king, this evil would not have befallen thee! ... O Kauravya, it is owing to my absence from the Anartta country at that time that thou hast fallen into such distress begot of dice!

events.working_title: Krishna Counsels the Pandavas to Return to Their Kingdom
events.one_line_summary: At Vidura's visit, Krishna (Vasudeva) advises that the Pandavas should accept their ancestral kingdom, and Drupada defers to his judgment.

sources.source_excerpt: Then Vasudeva said, 'I am of opinion that the Pandavas should go. But we should all abide by the opinion of king Drupada who is conversant with every rule of morality.' ... Kunti's son Yudhishthira himself doth not seek the welfare of the Pandavas so earnestly as, Kesava, that tiger among men.

events.working_title: Krishna Settles the Pandavas in Indraprastha and Returns to Dwaravati
events.one_line_summary: After the Pandavas receive half the kingdom, Krishna helps them establish Indraprastha, then takes his leave and returns to Dwaravati with Balarama.

sources.source_excerpt: And, O monarch, having settled the Pandavas there, the heroic Krishna, obtaining their leave, came back with Rama to Dwaravati.

events.working_title: Krishna Appears in Answer to Draupadi's Prayer
events.one_line_summary: When Durvasa arrives with ten thousand disciples and Draupadi has no food to offer, she prays to Krishna, who instantly leaves Rukmini's bed and comes to her.

sources.source_excerpt: The great and sovereign God, and Lord of the earth, of mysterious movements, the lord Kesava who is ever kind to the dependents, adored by Krishna, and perceiving her difficulty, instantly repaired to that place leaving the bed of Rukmini who was sleeping by his side.

events.variant_notes: cf. mb_e_005, mb_e_006 (Akshaya-patra episode).

events.working_title: Krishna Eats a Single Grain and Satisfies Durvasa and His Disciples
events.one_line_summary: Krishna finds one grain of rice sticking to Draupadi's vessel, eats it, and by that act the sage Durvasa and his ten thousand disciples feel their stomachs full and flee.

sources.source_excerpt: he looked into it and saw a particle of rice and vegetable sticking at its rim. And swallowing it he said unto her, 'May it please the god Hari, the soul of the Universe, and may that god who partaketh at sacrifices, be satiated with this.' ... these ascetics, having plunged into the river, were rubbing their bodies and observing that they all felt their stomachs to be full.

events.variant_notes: cf. mb_e_004.

events.working_title: Krishna Reassures the Pandavas and Departs
events.one_line_summary: After the frightened Munis flee, Krishna appears to the anxious Pandavas, assures them that Durvasa is gone and that the virtuous never suffer, then returns home.

sources.source_excerpt: the illustrious Krishna suddenly appeared to them and addressed them these words: 'Knowing, ye sons of Pritha, your danger from that wrathful Rishi, I was implored by Draupadi to come, and (therefore) have I come here speedily. But now ye have not the least fear from the Rishi Durvasa... Virtuous men never suffer. I now ask your permission to let me return home.'

events.variant_notes: cf. mb_e_005.

events.working_title: Balarama Tries to Halt the Mace-Duel
events.one_line_summary: Hearing that Bhima and Duryodhana are locked in their final mace-duel, Balarama goes to stop the slaughter but, unable to part the two, returns to Dwaraka.

sources.source_excerpt: Hearing of the battle of the Kurus and Pandavas and the slaughter of the warrior kings, Balarama, deeming the earth's burden lifted, goes to the field where Bhima and Duryodhana are fighting with maces. He tells the equal champions that neither can win and to desist, but the two, bound by enmity and remembering mutual insults, do not heed his words, and Balarama, accepting it as destiny, returns to Dwaraka. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 21-28)

events.working_title: Krishna Guides Arjuna Against Ashvatthama's Brahmastra
events.one_line_summary: After Ashvatthama releases the Brahmashira weapon at the Pandavas, a terrified Arjuna calls on Krishna, who tells him only a brahmastra can counter it; Arjuna discharges it and, at Krishna's word, withdraws both blazing weapons to save the worlds.

sources.source_excerpt: When the blazing weapon flares in every direction, Arjuna cries out, 'Krishna, Krishna, mighty-armed one, giver of fearlessness to your devotees, you alone are the rescue of those being burned.' Krishna answers: 'Know this to be the brahma weapon of Drona's son. He does not know how to recall it. Only an astra can quell an astra.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 21, 26-27)

events.working_title: Krishna's Verdict on Ashvatthama
events.one_line_summary: When Ashvatthama, the murderer of the sleeping children, is dragged before Krishna and the Pandavas, Krishna urges that the brahmin-slayer must be punished but not slain, and pronounces the compromise Arjuna carries out: strip his jewel and shave his head, sparing his life.

sources.source_excerpt: Krishna says: 'A brahmin's unworthy son is not to be slain, yet an assailant deserves punishment — both are my ordinances; uphold them. Keep the promise you made to your beloved, and satisfy Bhima, Panchali and me.' Then Arjuna, understanding Krishna's heart, cut off the jewel along with the hair of the brahmin, released him from his bonds, and drove him from the camp. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 52-55)

events.working_title: Krishna Shields Parikshit in Uttara's Womb
events.one_line_summary: As Krishna departs Hastinapura, the terrified Uttara cries for protection from Ashvatthama's weapon; Krishna enters her womb by his yoga-maya and shields the unborn Parikshit with the Sudarshana disc, extinguishing the unerring Brahmashira.

sources.source_excerpt: Uttara cries: 'Protect me, protect me, great yogin, Lord of gods, master of the world! May this blazing iron-tipped arrow burn me, but let my embryo not fall.' The Lord, loving to his devotees, understood that Drona's son's weapon was aimed to leave the Pandavas without heir; the Lord, indwelling soul of all beings, covered the womb of Virata's daughter with his own maya to preserve the Kuru line. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 8-13)

events.working_title: Bhishma's Passing in Krishna's Presence
events.one_line_summary: Lying on his bed of arrows at the auspicious northern solstice, Bhishma fixes his gaze on Krishna standing before him, glorifies him as Narayana himself, and passes away with his mind merged in the Lord, while the sages and Pandavas look on.

sources.source_excerpt: Bhishma says: 'This very Krishna, who came to me as I give up my life, out of love for his unalloyed devotees — may he be my refuge.' Then, gathering in his speech, he fixed his unblinking gaze upon the four-armed Krishna standing before him in yellow robes, and offered his final praise: 'May my love rest on Krishna...' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 21, 29-31)

events.working_title: The Kurukshetra War
events.one_line_summary: Uddhava recalls how the earth shook at Kurukshetra as the armies of the warring cousins gathered, and how Duryodhana lay at the last with his thigh broken, the burden of the earth lifted by Krishna's design.
themes: the lifting of the earth's burden

sources.source_excerpt: Uddhava said: 'The earth trembled at Kurukshetra beneath the armies of the kings who fell on either side; and Suyodhana, with his followers, lying with his thigh broken, he did not rejoice to see.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-12)

events.working_title: Draupadi Appeals to Krishna for Vengeance
events.one_line_summary: Draupadi, clutching her dishevelled hair, reminds Krishna of her humiliation in the assembly and begs him to avenge her on the Kauravas.

sources.source_excerpt: Lotus-eyed one that art anxious for peace with the enemy, thou shouldst, in all thy acts, call to thy mind these tresses of mine seized by Dussasana's rude hands! ... What peace can this heart of mine know unless I behold Dussasana's dark arm severed from his trunk and pulverised to atoms?

events.variant_notes: Pre-war appeal; parallel to forest-visit vow mb_a2_021.

events.working_title: Krishna Vows the Kuru Women Will Weep
events.one_line_summary: Krishna comforts the weeping Draupadi and swears that the women of the Kuru race will soon weep as she does, with their kinsmen slain.

sources.source_excerpt: The mighty-armed Kesava then spoke, comforting her in these words, 'Soon wilt thou, O Krishna, behold the ladies of Bharata's race weep as thou dost... The mountains of Himavat might shift their site, the Earth herself might split into a hundred fragments... still my words can never be futile. Stop thy tears, I swear to thee, O Krishna, soon wilt thou see thy husbands, with their enemies slain, and with prosperity crowning them.'

events.variant_notes: Pre-war vow; parallel to forest-visit promise mb_a2_023.

events.working_title: Krishna Accepts the Peace Mission
events.one_line_summary: Asked by Arjuna to go as envoy, Krishna agrees to go to Dhritarashtra to seek peace for the good of both the Pandavas and the Kurus.

sources.source_excerpt: The holy one said, 'Yes, I will go to king Dhritarashtra, desirous of accomplishing what is consistent with righteousness, what may be beneficial to us, and what also is for the good of the Kurus.'

events.working_title: Krishna Prepares His Chariot and Sets Out for Hastinapura
events.one_line_summary: After his morning rites, Krishna has his car armed with his conch, discus and mace; Garuda alights on its flagstaff, and he mounts and sets out with Satyaki.

sources.source_excerpt: And they yoked unto it those excellent steeds named Saivya and Sugriva and Meghapushpa and Valahaka... Garuda, the lord of the feathery creation, came and perched on the flag-staff of that car producing a terrible rattle. And Saurin then mounted on that car, high as the summit of the Meru... And taking Satyaki also upon it, that best of male beings set out.

events.working_title: Yudhishthira Entrusts Krishna with Messages for Kunti and the Elders
events.one_line_summary: Yudhishthira, following Krishna some distance, asks him to salute and comfort his grieving mother Kunti and to greet Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Vidura and all the elders.

sources.source_excerpt: Yudhishthira said, 'That lady who hath brought us from our infancy... should be asked about her welfare--Salute and embrace, and, oh, comfort her over and over, overwhelmed with grief as she is on account of her sons... Salute her for me, the Kuru king Dhritarashtra also... and Bhishma, and Drona, and Kripa... and also Vidura endued with great wisdom.'

events.working_title: Arjuna's Parting Warning and Bhima's Roar
events.one_line_summary: Arjuna warns that if Duryodhana acts improperly he will annihilate the Kshatriyas, and Bhima, hearing this, sets forth a terrible shout that makes all bowmen tremble.

sources.source_excerpt: Then Arjuna, proceeding a few steps, further said... 'If, however, Dhritarashtra's son, who always adopts improper means, acts otherwise, then I shall surely, O Janardana, annihilate the Kshatriya race.' ... he set forth a terrible shout. And hearing that shout of his, all the bowmen trembled in fear and steeds and elephants were seen to pass urine and excreta.

events.working_title: Krishna Meets the Celestial Rishis Led by Parashurama
events.one_line_summary: On the road Krishna alights to worship a band of celestial Rishis; Jamadagni's son Parashurama embraces him and says they come to witness the conclave and hear his words.

sources.source_excerpt: on his way Kesava of mighty arms met with some Rishis blazing with Brahmic lustre... Jamadagni's son... approached Govinda the slayer of Madhu, embraced him, and said, '...We are desirous of beholding all the Kshatriyas of the earth assembled from every side... We are also anxious... to listen to those words fraught with virtue and profit, which will be spoken by thee... unto the Kurus in the presence of all the kings.'

events.working_title: Krishna's Auspicious Journey to Hastinapura
events.one_line_summary: As Krishna journeys to Hastinapura, dread omens fall on the Kuru capital while wherever he passes the road becomes auspicious with showers of flowers; he passes the night at Vrikasthala.

sources.source_excerpt: Though there were no clouds in the sky, yet the roll of thunder accompanied by flashes of lightning was heard... A south-westerly wind, with the harsh rattle of the thunder, uprooting trees by the thousands, crushed the city of Hastinapura. In those places, however, O Bharata, through which he of Vrishni's race passed, delicious breezes blew and everything became auspicious. Showers of lotuses and fragrant flowers fell there.

events.working_title: Duryodhana's Lavish Pavilions That Krishna Ignores
events.one_line_summary: Duryodhana builds gem-studded pavilions to receive Krishna, but Krishna arrives at the Kuru capital without casting a single glance at them.

sources.source_excerpt: And the king of the Kurus took especial care to erect, for the reception of Krishna, a highly beautiful pavilion at Vrikasthala, full of precious gems... Kesava, however, of Dasarha's race, arrived at the capital of the Kurus, without casting a single glance at all those pavilions and all those gems of diverse kinds.

events.working_title: Vidura Exposes the Plan to Bribe Krishna
events.one_line_summary: When Dhritarashtra plans lavish gifts to win Krishna over, Vidura declares the gifts betray deception and that Krishna can never be separated from Arjuna.

sources.source_excerpt: Vidura said, '...Know, however, that Kesava deserves all this and much more, aye, the whole earth itself... By the external acts, O king, I know thy secret purpose. The five Pandavas, O king, desire only five villages. Thou, however, dost not wish to give them even that... thou seekest to separate Kesava from the Pandavas. I tell thee, however, that thou art unable, by wealth, or attention, or worship, to separate Krishna from Dhananjaya.'

events.working_title: Duryodhana Resolves to Imprison Krishna; Bhishma Departs in Anger
events.one_line_summary: Duryodhana announces his plan to imprison Krishna; Dhritarashtra is pained and Bhishma, denouncing the wicked scheme, rises in rage and leaves.

sources.source_excerpt: Duryodhana said, '...I will imprison Janardana who is the refuge of the Pandavas. He will come here tomorrow morning; and when he is confined, the Vrishnis and the Pandavas, aye, the whole earth, will submit to me.' ... Bhishma said, 'This wicked son of thine, O Dhritarashtra, hath his hour come... Having said this, that aged chief of the Bharata race, Bhishma of unbaffled prowess, inflamed with rage rose and left that place.

events.working_title: Krishna Enters Hastinapura and Meets Dhritarashtra
events.one_line_summary: Welcomed by Bhishma, Drona and the Dhartarashtras, Krishna enters Hastinapura, where the blind king Dhritarashtra and all the elders rise to honour him.

sources.source_excerpt: And meeting on the way Bhishma of spotless deed, and Drona, and Dhritarashtra's sons, he entered the city, surrounded by them all... And that lotus-eyed grinder of foes then entered Dhritarashtra's ash-coloured palace... the blind monarch of great fame stood up along with Drona and Bhishma, Kripa and Somadatta, and king Vahlika also.

events.working_title: Krishna Comforts the Grieving Kunti
events.one_line_summary: Krishna visits his aunt Kunti, who pours out her sorrows for her exiled sons; he consoles her and assures her she will soon see the Pandavas victorious.

sources.source_excerpt: Vasudeva said, 'What woman is there, O aunt, in the world who is like thee?... Endued with every virtue, and endued with great wisdom, it behoveth thee to bear with patience, both happiness and misery... The Pandavas with Krishna saluteth thee through me... Thou wilt soon behold them become the lords of the whole world, with their foe slain, and themselves invested with prosperity.'

events.working_title: Krishna Refuses Duryodhana's Hospitality
events.one_line_summary: Duryodhana invites Krishna to eat at his house, but Krishna refuses, saying envoys eat only after their mission succeeds and that he will accept food from Vidura alone.

sources.source_excerpt: The high-souled Govinda... replied... saying, 'Envoys, O king, eat and accept worship only after the success of their missions...' ... 'Defiled by wickedness, all this food, therefore, deserveth not to be eaten by me. The food supplied by Vidura alone, should, I think, be eaten by me.'

events.working_title: Vidura Warns Krishna of Duryodhana's Wickedness
events.one_line_summary: That night Vidura tells Krishna his coming was ill-judged, describing Duryodhana's vices and his belief that he can never be persuaded to make peace.

sources.source_excerpt: Vidura said unto him during the night, 'O Kesava, this advent of thine hath not been a well judged one, for, O Janardana, Dhritarashtra's son transgresseth the rules of both profit and religion, is wicked and wrathful... He will, therefore, never make peace.'

events.working_title: Krishna's Resolve: The Merit of Striving for Peace
events.one_line_summary: Krishna answers Vidura that he came knowing Duryodhana's wickedness, for great is the merit of one who strives to save the earth from destruction even if he fails.

sources.source_excerpt: The holy one said, '...Well knowing the wickedness of Dhritarashtra's son and the hostility of the Kshatriyas that have sided with him, I have still, O Vidura, come to the Kurus. Great will be the merit earned by him who will liberate from the meshes of death the whole earth, with her elephants, cars and steeds, overwhelmed with a dreadful calamity.'

events.working_title: Krishna Enters the Kuru Assembly
events.one_line_summary: Krishna rides in procession to the Kuru court, enters arm-in-arm with Vidura and Satyaki, and after the Rishis are seated takes his seat in the assembly.

sources.source_excerpt: And having reached the gate of the court, Sauri, that bull among the Satwatas, alighting from his car... entered the court which looked like a mass of newly-risen clouds... And that illustrious hero entered the court, arm-in-arm with Vidura and Satyaki on either side, and overshadowing with his own the splendour of all the Kurus.

events.working_title: Krishna's Plea for Peace Before the Assembly
events.one_line_summary: Before the assembled kings, Krishna urges Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and restore the Pandavas' share of the kingdom, to save the world from slaughter.

sources.source_excerpt: In order that, O Bharata, peace may be established between the Kurus and the Pandavas without a slaughter of the heroes, I have come hither... Save, O king, the world. Let not the population of the earth be exterminated... Giving unto the Pandavas their just share of the paternal kingdom, enjoy thou then, with thy sons, O chastiser of foes, happiness and luxury.

events.working_title: Parashurama Reveals Krishna and Arjuna as Nara and Narayana
events.one_line_summary: Parashurama, in the assembly, tells the tale of Dambhodbhava and declares that Nara and Narayana of old are now Arjuna and Krishna, urging Duryodhana to make peace.

sources.source_excerpt: Rama continued, '...They that were Nara and Narayana in days of yore are now Arjuna and Kesava. Know then, O great king, who those brave and foremost of persons are. If thou believest in this and dost not mistrust me adopt thou a virtuous resolution and make peace with the sons of Pandu.'

events.working_title: Krishna's Appeal to Duryodhana
events.one_line_summary: At Dhritarashtra's request, Krishna approaches Duryodhana directly and urges him, with reasoned counsel, to make peace with the Pandavas for the good of his own race.

sources.source_excerpt: The mighty-armed Govinda... said unto him these sweet words, 'O Duryodhana, O best of the Kurus, listen to these words of mine, uttered especially for thy good... Then, O tiger among men, make peace, O bull among the Bharatas, with the sons of Pandu who are all endued with great wisdom and great bravery...'

events.working_title: Duryodhana's Refusal: Not a Needle-Point of Land
events.one_line_summary: Duryodhana rejects Krishna's counsel, claiming he has done no wrong, and vows that not even land covered by the point of a needle will be given to the Pandavas while he lives.

sources.source_excerpt: Duryodhana replied... 'As long, O Janardana, as king Dhritarashtra liveth, both ourselves and they... should live in dependence on him... even that much of our land which may be covered by the point of a sharp needle shall not, O Madhava, be given by us unto the Pandavas.'

events.working_title: Krishna's Rebuke of Duryodhana's Crimes
events.one_line_summary: With eyes red in anger, Krishna recounts Duryodhana's crimes — the dice plot, Draupadi's humiliation, the attempts to burn and poison the Pandavas — and foretells his downfall.

sources.source_excerpt: he, of Dasarha's race, addressing Duryodhana... said these words, 'Wishest thou for a bed of heroes? Verily, thou shalt have it, with thy counsellors... Who else is there, capable of insulting a brother's wife in the way thou didst or of dragging her into the assembly and addressing her in language thou hadst used towards Draupadi?'

events.working_title: Krishna Urges the Elders to Bind Duryodhana
events.one_line_summary: After Duryodhana storms out, Krishna tells the elders that they are guilty for not seizing the wicked king, citing how he himself slew Kansa to save his kinsmen.

sources.source_excerpt: Kesava... said, 'Even this is great transgression, of which all the elders of the Kuru race are becoming guilty, for they do not forcibly seize and bind this wicked king... Kansa, the son of Ugrasena, abandoned by his relatives, was slain by me in a great encounter, from desire of benefiting my kinsmen... binding Duryodhana fast, make peace with the Pandavas.'

events.working_title: The Plot to Seize Krishna; Satyaki's Alarm
events.one_line_summary: Duryodhana, Karna, Sakuni and Dussasana resolve to seize Krishna by force; Satyaki, reading the signs, alerts Krishna and arrays the troops.

sources.source_excerpt: this was the resolution which Duryodhana and Karna and Suvala's son Sakuni, with Dussasana as their fourth, arrived at, 'This Janardana, quick in action, seeketh... to seize us first. We, however, shall forcibly seize this tiger among men, Hrishikesa, first, like Indra forcibly seizing Virochana's son.' ... Satyaki, capable of reading the heart by signs, soon came to know of it.

events.working_title: Krishna Defies the Conspirators
events.one_line_summary: Krishna tells Dhritarashtra that if they wish to seize him by violence they may try, for he could make over all of them to the Pandavas, but he will not commit a censurable deed.

sources.source_excerpt: Kesava, casting his eyes on Dhritarashtra, said... 'O king, if these (men) desire to chastise me by using violence, permit them to chastise me... this very day, O Bharata, seizing these with all that follow them, I can make them over to the sons of Pritha... I will not, however, O Bharata, commit in thy presence, O great monarch, any such censurable deed.'

events.working_title: Krishna Reveals His Universal Form
events.one_line_summary: Laughing at Duryodhana's boast to seize him, Krishna bursts into his universal form — gods issuing from his body, the whole court dazzled, all but a few closing their eyes in terror.

sources.source_excerpt: And as the high-souled Sauri laughed, from his body, that resembled a blazing fire, issued myriads of gods, each of lightning effulgence, and not bigger than the thumb. And on his forehead appeared Brahman, and on his breast Rudra... And beholding that awful form of the high-souled Kesava, all the kings closed their eyes with affrighted hearts, except Drona, and Bhishma, and Vidura... and Sanjaya... for the divine Janardana gave unto them this divine sight on the occasion.

events.working_title: Krishna Departs as Dhritarashtra Pleads Powerlessness
events.one_line_summary: With the assembly witnessed, Krishna takes leave of the elders, declares he will return to Yudhishthira, and mounts his car to depart as Dhritarashtra protests his powerlessness.

sources.source_excerpt: The mighty-armed Janardana then addressed Dhritarashtra, Drona, grandsire Bhishma, Kshattri, Vahlika, and Kripa and said, 'Ye have yourselves witnessed all that hath happened in the assembly of the Kurus... With the permission of you all, I shall now go back to Yudhishthira.' Saluting them, that bull amongst men, Sauri then mounted his car and set out.

events.working_title: Krishna Relays Kunti's Message: The Duty of a Kshatriya
events.one_line_summary: Krishna reports the failed embassy to Kunti and carries back her charge to Yudhishthira to recover his kingdom by the prowess of his arms as a Kshatriya should.

sources.source_excerpt: Kunti said, 'O Kesava, say unto king Yudhishthira of virtuous soul these words, "Thy virtue, O son, is decreasing greatly. Do not act vainly... Thou art a Kshatriya and therefore, the protector of all in distress. Thou art to live by the prowess of thy arms. O thou of mighty arms, recover thy paternal share of the kingdom which thou hast lost..."'

events.working_title: Kunti's Exhortation: The Story of Vidula and Sanjaya
events.one_line_summary: Kunti instructs Krishna to carry the ancient tale of Vidula, who shamed her defeated son Sanjaya back into battle, as an exhortation to war for Yudhishthira.

sources.source_excerpt: Kunti said, 'In this connection, O chastiser of foes, is cited an old story of the conversation between Vidula and her son... There was a high-born dame of great foresight, named Vidula... the princess Vidula, one day, rebuked her own son, who, after his defeat by the king of the Sindhus, lay prostrate with heart depressed by despair.'

events.working_title: Kunti's Final Messages and Krishna's Leave-Taking
events.one_line_summary: Kunti gives Krishna parting words for Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi and the twins, recalling the celestial voice that promised Arjuna victory, and Krishna takes his leave of her.

sources.source_excerpt: Kunti said, 'Say unto Arjuna, these words... "when thou wert brought forth in the lying-in room... a celestial and delightful voice was heard in the sky, saying... 'This one will vanquish in battle all the assembled Kurus...'"... Go thou on thy auspicious way, and protect my sons!'

events.working_title: Krishna Takes Karna Upon His Chariot and Returns to Upaplavya
events.one_line_summary: Krishna dismisses the Kuru chiefs, takes Karna upon his chariot, deliberates with him at length, then dismisses him and returns swiftly to Upaplavya.

sources.source_excerpt: And he then dismissed those chiefs among the Kurus with Bhishma at their head, and taking Karna upon his chariot, left (the Kuru city), accompanied by Satyaki... Having issued out of the (Kuru) city, that foremost of persons proceeded, deliberating with Karna for a long time... And quickly traversing a long way like fleet hawks, they reached Upaplavya very soon.

events.variant_notes: cf. mb_e_008 (Karna's leave-taking).

events.working_title: Krishna Reveals Karna's Birth and Offers Him the Kingdom
events.one_line_summary: Krishna tells Karna he is Kunti's firstborn son and therefore a Pandava, and offers to have him installed as king of the whole earth with the Pandavas as his followers.

sources.source_excerpt: Vasudeva said, 'O son of Radha, thou hast worshipped many Brahmanas fully conversant with the Vedas... It is said by those conversant with the scriptures that the two kinds of sons called Kanina and Sahoda... have him for their father who weddeth the maid. Thou, O Karna, hast been born in this way. Thou art, therefore, morally the son of Pandu. Come, be a king, according to the injunction of the scriptures... let the Pandavas know thee as a son of Kunti born before Yudhishthira... install thee as the lord of the whole earth.'

events.working_title: Karna Refuses, Pledging Loyalty to Duryodhana
events.one_line_summary: Acknowledging he is Kunti's son by Surya, Karna refuses the kingdom, declaring that Adhiratha and Radha who raised him are his parents and that he will not betray Duryodhana.

sources.source_excerpt: Karna said, '...Morally, I am the son of Pandu... Kunti, however, abandoned me without thinking of my welfare. The Suta, Adhiratha, as soon as he beheld me, took me to his home... I cannot venture, O Janardana, to behave falsely towards the intelligent son of Dhritarashtra... If king Yudhishthira... cometh to know me as the firstborn son of Kunti, he will never accept the kingdom.'

events.working_title: Karna's Prophecy of the Coming War as a Sacrifice
events.one_line_summary: Karna foretells the war as a great sacrifice of arms with Krishna as its witness, describing how each hero will play a priestly part, and asks Krishna to keep their talk secret.

sources.source_excerpt: a great sacrifice of arms is about to be celebrated by Dhritarashtra's son. Thou, O Janardana, wilt be the Upadrashtri of that sacrifice... The ape-bannered Vibhatsu accoutred in mail will be the Hotri... When mighty Bhimasena will slay Duryodhana, then, O Madhava, will this sacrifice of Dhritarashtra's son be concluded... bring Kunti's son (Arjuna) before me for battle, keeping for ever this our discourse a secret.

events.working_title: Krishna Directs Arjuna to Hymn Durga
events.one_line_summary: On the eve of the battle Krishna tells Arjuna to recite his hymn to Durga; the goddess appears in the sky, grants victory, and both warriors blow their conches.

sources.source_excerpt: The holy one said,--'Cleansing thyself, O mighty-armed one, utter on the eve of the battle thy hymn to Durga for (compassing) the defeat of the foe.' ...
